Budowa i utrzymywanie stabilnoci tego systemu s bardzo istotne, gdy kryzys finansowy oznacza zaamanie wzrostu gospodarki. Dbao o stabilno systemu finansowego jest wic przejawem troski o gospodarczy rozw kraju. Kluczowym elementem systemu finansowego jest sektor bankowy. Poza porednictwem w przeksztacaniu oszczdnoci w inwestycje i sprawowaniem wierzycielskiego nadzoru nad przedsibiorstwami - kredytobiorcami, banki tworz podstaw systemu rozliczania transakcji i dokonywania patnoci w gospodarce. W przypadku Polski i innych kraj Europy rodkowo-Wschodniej  wskutek sabego dotd rozwoju rynk kapitaowych  rola systemu bankowego w gospodarce jest szczegnie dua. W 2002 r. aktywa bankw stanowiy 80 proc. aktyww caego systemu finansowego. W latach 2001-2002 polski system bankowy przechodzi test stabilnoci. Po okresie szybkiego rozwoju gospodarczego i jeszcze szybszego wzrostu akcji kredytowej nastpio pogorszenie koniunktury. Okazao si, e cz udzielonych w okresie boomu kredytw w niedostatecznym stopniu uwzgldniaa ryzyko pogorszenia sytuacji. W poczeniu z dziaaniami nadzoru bankowego zmierzajcymi do ukazania faktycznej jakoci udzielonych przez banki kredytw, doprowadzio to do wzrostu udziau nalenoci zagroonych w portfelach kredytowych bank. W grudniu 2002 r. wyni on 20,7 proc. Naley jednak podkreli, e polskie regulacje nadzorcze w zakresie zasad klasyfikacji kredytw, tworzce swoisty system wczesnego ostrzegania przed ryzykiem kredytowym, s ostrzejsze od stosowanych w wielu krajach. Gdyby uwzgldni tylko kredyty wtpliwe oraz stracone pozostajce w bilansie bank nie duej ni rok, to wspczynnik kredyt zagroonych w grudniu 2002 r. wyniby 7,6 proc. wszystkich kredytw. To jest pornywalna w skali midzynarodowej wielko. Pogorszenie jakoci portfela kredytowego nie zagrozio stabilnoci systemu, gdy wysze ryzyko kredytowe zostao cakowicie zrnowaone zabezpieczeniami kredyt i rezerwami celowymi tworzonymi przez banki. Gwarancj bezpieczestwa systemu byo te dobre wyposaenie kapitaowe bank. S one zobowizane do utrzymywania kapita wasnych na poziomie zapewniajcym bezpieczestwo zgromadzonych depozyt i pozwalajcym pokrywa niespodziewane straty. Przecitny poziom wspczynnika wypacalnoci w grudniu 2002 r. wynosi13,7 proc., wobec wymaganego minimum 8 proc. Tylko w 5 bankach komercyjnych i 10 bankach spdzielczych jego poziom by niszy od tego minimum. Ich znaczenie w caym sektorze bankowym jest jednak niewielkie, a s one jednoczenie obiektem szczegnego zainteresowania nadzoru bankowego. Wanym aspektem stabilnoci systemu finansowego jest pynno bankw, czyli ich zdolno do regulowania biecych zobowiza. W 2002 r. banki utrzymyway wysoki poziom aktyw pynnych. Ich relacja do caoci aktyww wyniosa ok. 35 proc. i znacznie przewyszaa zobowizania z tytuu mniej stabilnych depozytw. Narodowy Bank Polski prowadzi w 2002 r. nastpujce, podstawowe dziaania na rzecz stabilnoci naszego systemu bankowego:  Gn form aktywnoci byo cige nadzorowanie dziaalnoci bank przez Generalny Inspektorat Nadzoru Bankowego. Przeprowadzono 108 inspekcji kompleksowych i 73 inspekcje problemowe. Zakres inspekcji poszerzono o badanie zarzdzania ryzykiem operacyjnym technologii informatycznej i bankowoci elektronicznej. W celu zwikszenia przejrzystoci dziaania nadzoru bankowego wprowadzono zasad przekazywania bankom informacji o przyznanych w wyniku bada ocenach.  Komisja Nadzoru Bankowego przyja proponowane przez GINB nowe regulacje ostronociowe. Pozwalaj one na dokadniejsze odzwierciedlenie rzeczywistego ryzyka, na jakie naraony jest bank. Wprowadzenie nowych zasad obliczania kapitau regulacyjnego powinno podnie jako zarzdzania ryzykiem przez banki i pozwoli na efektywniejsze wykorzystanie ich kapitau.  NBP czynnie uczestniczy w pracach nad projektem ustawy nowelizujcej prawo bankowe. Nowelizacja ta przewiduje zmiany w regulacjach ostronociowych, kte powinny wzmocni stabilno naszego systemu bankowego.  Co kwarta GINB przygotowuje raport nt. Oceny sytuacji ekonomicznej bank, zawierajcy kompleksow informacj o sytuacji sektora bankowego oraz o moliwych rach zagroe jego stabilnoci.  Wreszcie chciabym powiedzie, e w czerwcu 2002 r. utworzono w Narodowym Banku Polskim Departament Systemu Finansowego, kty wspdziaajc z Generalnym Inspektoratem Nadzoru Bankowego, na bieco bada stabilno systemu finansowego, w szczegnoci sektora bankowego. Departament prowadzi te analizy rozwoju krajowego systemu finansowego. III 5. Zarzdzanie rezerwami walutowymi. Panie Marszaku, Wysoka Izbo! Trzeci podstawow dziedzin dziaalnoci Narodowego Banku Polskiego jest zarzdzanie oficjalnymi rezerwami dewizowymi. Narodowy Bank Polski kieruje si tu trzema zasadami:  zapewnieniem wysokiego poziomu bezpieczestwa inwestowanych rodk;  utrzymaniem niezbdnego stopnia pynnoci, czyli zdolnoci do regulowania zobowiza;  oraz  przy respektowaniu tych dwh ogranicze - uzyskaniem maksymalnych dochodw z inwestycji. Zapewnieniu wysokiego stopnia bezpieczestwa i pynnoci rezerw suy system limit zaangaowania inwestycyjnego, dotyczcy struktury walutowej, ratingu kredytowego emitent papier wartociowych na wiecie oraz czasu trwania lokaty. Rezerwy dewizowe daj krajowi dwojakiego rodzaju korzyci: bezporednie i porednie. Korzyci bezporednie polegaj na osiganiu dochodu, kty co roku trafia do budetu pastwa. Ocena efektywnoci zarzdzania rezerwami walutowymi jest dokonywana na podstawie pornania dochodowoci osignitej (nazwanej dochodowoci biec) z dochodowoci tzw. portfela pornawczego (zwan dochodowoci parytetow) wyznaczonego przez Zarzd NBP. W ramach przyjtych limit bezpieczestwa Narodowy Bank Polski w 2002 r. ksztatowa struktur walutow rezerw zakadajc umacnianie si euro wobec dolara amerykaskiego. W zwizku z tym, udzia euro by utrzymywany w grnej strefie przedziau dopuszczalnych waha. Drugim zaoeniem strategii inwestycyjnej w 2002 r. byo przewidywanie spadku st procentowych na rynkach wiatowych. W warunkach spadku st procentowych rosn ceny papier wartociowych o staym oprocentowaniu. Dlatego w strukturze rezerw utrzymywano wikszy udzia tych papierw. Przyjcie owych dwch zaoe okazao si bardzo korzystne. Osignito doch z inwestowania rezerw w wysokoci 1,1 mld USD (4,6 mld z), a odpowiednio liczona dochodowo rezerw walutowych wyniosa w 2002 r. 5,5 proc. O korzyciach porednich z rezerw dewizowych czsto si zapomina i dlatego chciabym o nich przypomnie. Pod tym wzgldem przypominaj one zdrowie, kte si ceni wtedy, gdy si je traci. Korzyci porednie to zapewnianie wymienialnoci narodowego pienidza, stabilnoci jego kursu wobec innych walut oraz wiarygodnoci finansowej kraju. Owe korzyci rosn wraz z poziomem rezerw walutowych. Przy takim samym deficycie handlowym i zadueniu zagranicznym wielko rezerw moe decydowa, czy inwestycje w walucie danego kraju s postrzegane jako bezpieczne. Brak wystarczajcych rezerw przy niekorzystnym ukadzie innych czynnikw, moe spowodowa ucieczk kapitau, drastyczny wzrost st procentowych i gwatowne osabienie wartoci krajowego pienidza. Nawet najwiksze rezerwy walutowe nie mog jednak oczywicie zastpi dobrej polityki gospodarczej, mog natomiast agodzi skutki rnych wstrzs. Z praktyki bank centralnych wynika, e uznawany za bezpieczny poziom rezerw walutowych dla kraj mniej rozwinitych przekracza rwnowarto szeciomiesicznego importu, a ich relacja do krkoterminowego zaduenia zagranicznego kraju powinna wynosi co najmniej 100 proc. Na koniec 2002 roku oficjalne aktywa rezerwowe NBP z uwzgldnieniem zota wyniosy 29,8 mld USD i byy o 3,2 mld USD wysze ni rok wczeniej. Wzrost ten wynika gnie ze wzmocnienia kursu euro wobec dolara, bowiem w euro bya utrzymywana cz rezerw; dalej - z dochodu osignitego z ich inwestowania oraz wreszcie -ze spaty przez Ministerstwo Finans 1,1 mld dolar, w zwizku z udzielon rzdowi w 2001 r. poyczk na wczeniejsz i zyskown spat naszego zaduenia wobec Brazylii. W kocu 2002 r. rezerwy walutowe Narodowego Banku Polskiego pokryway rnowarto szeciu i p miesica importu i stanowiy ok. 233 proc. krkoterminowego zaduenia zagranicznego. Naley jednak podkreli, e w sytuacji zwikszonego ryzyka inwestorzy zagraniczni mog wymaga zwrotu rnie czci zaduenia dugoterminowego, np. sprzedajc polskie obligacje skarbowe. Dlatego trzeba patrze rnie na stosunek rezerw dewizowych do caego dugu zewntrznego. W 2002 r. rezerwy walutowe pokryway ok. 37 proc. owego dugu. Byo to na szczcie wyranie wicej ni w krajach, gdzie wystpiy w ostatnich latach kryzysy walutowe takich jak Rosja, Argentyna, Brazylia. Ale z kolei pod wzgldem innego miernika: stosunku rezerw dewizowych do PKB, Polska ze swoimi 16 proc. sytuowaa si na poziomie Wgier i znacznie niej ni Czechy (34 proc.) i Sowacja (39 proc.). W sumie mona uzna, e rezerwy walutowe Narodowego Banku Polskiego osigny pewien prg bezpieczestwa. Posiadanie silnej armii odstrasza potencjalnych agresorw, zapewniajc narodowe bezpieczestwo. Podobnie jest z posiadaniem duych rezerw dewizowych  mog one zapobiega atakom spekulacyjnym obliczonym na osabienie kursu zotego. A stabilno tego kursu jest jednym z podstawowych warunk stabilnoci cen, kta z kolei sprzyja dobremu gospodarowaniu. Stabilno kursu zotego jest istotna rwnie dlatego, e spora cz kredytw w bankach zostaa przez gospodarstwa domowe i firmy zacignita w walutach obcych. Raptowne osabienie zotego oznaczaoby dla nich duy cios, bo dug i odsetki wyraone w zotych odpowiednio by wzrosy. Znaczenie rezerw walutowych zwikszy si w niedalekiej przyszoci. Nasz kraj czeka bowiem w drodze do euro dwuletnie dowiadczenie w ramach europejskiego mechanizmu kursowego ERM2, w ktym dla utrzymania kursu w przedziale waha  obecnie przedziau nie mamy - mog by niezbdne interwencje banku centralnego na rynku walutowym. Wiarygodne, a wic skuteczne interwencje bd wymagay wysokiego poziomu rezerw walutowych. Wreszcie due rezerwy dewizowe umacniaj wiarygodno kraju, co umoliwia pastwu i prywatnym podmiotom gospodarczym zaciganie poyczek zagranicznych przy niszym oprocentowaniu ni w sytuacji, gdy poziom rezerw jest postrzegany jako zbyt niski. A z tego wynikaj oszczdnoci w kosztach obsugi dugu zagranicznego sigajce setek milion zotych. Z tego te oczywicie wynika, e nadmierne uszczuplenie owych rezerw mogoby nasz kraj bardzo wiele kosztowa. IV 6. Reformy wewntrzne w NBP. Panie Marszaku, Wysoka Izbo. Chciabym na koniec powiedzie o reformach, kte celem jest zwikszenie efektw lub obnienie koszt dziaania Narodowego Banku Polskiego.  W 2002 roku ograniczono sie terenow do 16 oddzia okrgowych. Pozwolio to na zmniejszenie zatrudnienia o 21 proc. Coroczne oszczdnoci dziki tej reformie szacuje si na blisko100 mln z, co stanowi okoo 11 proc. koszt dziaania banku. Majtek wygospodarowany w wyniku owej restrukturyzacji zosta w zdecydowanej wikszoci przekazany Skarbowi Pastwa, aby wzmocni baz materialn wykonywania podstawowych funkcji pastwa: -Ministerstwu Sprawiedliwoci  dla sd i prokuratur - przekazano budynki w Supsku, Czstochowie, Nowym Sczu, Zamociu, Kronie, Przemylu, Jeleniej Gze, Ostroce, Pocku, Radomiu, - Ministerstwu Spraw Wewntrznych i Administracji  gnie dla policji -przekazano budynki w Suwakach, Gorzowie Wielkopolskim, Wabrzychu i Legnicy.  W 2002 roku NBP wprowadzi dla swoich klient - jednostek budetowych i pastwowych funduszy celowych - system bankowoci elektronicznej. Do 21 lipca br. obj on ponad 2,5 tys. spor 3,5 tys. podmiotw posiadajcych rachunki w Narodowym Banku Polskim. Dziki temu - mimo ograniczenia sieci terenowej- utrzymano wysok jako obsugi klient. W maju 2003 roku NBP uzyska certyfikat jakoci ISO 9001:2000 w dziedzinie obsugi rachunk bankowych z wykorzystaniem bankowoci elektronicznej.  Od 2001 roku Narodowy Bank Polski obsadza wolne stanowiska kierownicze w drodze otwartych konkurs. W 2002 roku nominacje na stanowiska kierownicze w Centrali i oddziaach okrgowych otrzymao w ten spos 10 os, a do konkurs zgosiy si 264 osoby.  Narodowy Bank Polski  podobnie jak inne banki centralne - wzmacnia swoje piony analityczne. Departament Analiz Makroekonomicznych i Strukturalnych realizuje nowe zadania dotyczce zmian instytucjonalnych, finans publicznych i rynku pracy, a nowy Departament Systemu Finansowego skupia si na analizowaniu stabilnoci i rozwoju sektora bankowego i rynk finansowych.  Wreszcie, wzorem najlepszych bankw centralnych  NBP realizuje te Program Edukacji Ekonomicznej, skierowany do modziey i nauczycieli, dziennikarzy, przedsibiorc oraz organizacji pozarzdowych. W 2002 roku w ramach dziaa edukacyjnych Narodowego Banku Polskiego przeszkolono ponad 40 tys. os i opublikowano ponad 90 wydawnictw edukacyjnych, a we wsppracy z mediami lokalnymi i centralnymi ukazao si: 46 program telewizyjnych, 536 audycji radiowych, 259 wkadek, dodatk i cykli artyku w gazetach, o charakterze edukacyjnym. Dua ich cz dotyczya informacji o euro. *** Zmianom organizacyjnym i rozszerzaniu zakresu dziaa Narodowego Banku Polskiego towarzyszyy intensywne przygotowania do realizacji nowych zada wynikajcych z bliskiej ju perspektywy czonkostwa w Unii Europejskiej. Jednym z element przygotowywania si NBP do standard obowizujcych w Europejskim Systemie Bankw Centralnych by dwuletni projekt realizowany we wsppracy z Bankiem Woch i Bankiem Francji, a finansowany przez Uni Europejsk ze rodk Phare 2000. Kilka dni temu mielimy przyjemno goci Pana Trichet, Gubernatora Banku Francji i przyszego Prezesa Europejskiego Banku Centralnego na uroczystoci z okazji zakoczenia tego projektu. Z satysfakcj odnotowalimy, e w raporcie na temat wybranych projektw Phare w Polsce, opracowanym pod koniec 2002 roku na zlecenie Komisji Europejskiej, projekt NBP by jednym z dwh - spord 30 badanych  kty uzyska najwysz moliw ocen. 7. Zakoczenie. Panie Marszaku, Wysoki Sejmie! Koczc, pragn powiedzie, e stabilny pienidz, zdrowy system bankowy, due i dobrze zarzdzane rezerwy walutowe to niezbdne podstawy stabilnego, szybkiego dugofalowego rozwoju gospodarki. Dbajc o nie, Narodowy Bank Polski stara si wnosi wkad do procesu, od ktego zaley systematyczna poprawa warunkw ycia naszego spoeczestwa. Dzikuj za uwag.

Title: Report on the implementation of monetary policy assumptions in 2003
text: Warsaw, 20 July 2004 Speech by Leszek Balcerowicz, President of the National Bank of Poland, in the parliamentary debate on the "Report on the implementation of monetary policy assumptions in 2003" and "Report on the activities of the National Bank of Poland in 2003" 1. Introduction. 1.1. Benefits of price stability. Mr Speaker, Honourable Members, The social costs of inflation have been known to people for centuries.  In the twelfth century, the Czech chronicler Kosmas wrote: "No calamity, no pestilence, no mortality, no desolation by the enemy of the whole earth by plunder and fires would do no more harm to God's people than the more frequent change and treacherous deterioration of the coin. What plague or what hellish witch mercilessly strips, loses, and weakens Christians than the deception of the ruler in the coin?"  And in the sixteenth century, Nicolaus Copernicus mentioned the "bottoming of the coin" as the main one - next to it "discord, mortality and infertility of the earth" - the cause of the collapse of states. At that time, it was about the corruption of money by the ruler at the rate of several percent. annually. Such were the possibilities determined by its ore character. Persistently high inflation in times of peace is a phenomenon of a fresh date. It was only in the twentieth century, when money was permanently torn away from the bullion, that its quantity could be  by printing banknotes and entries in bank accounts  increase rapidly and practically indefinitely. Poland experienced such a catastrophe in the early twenties and again in 1989. Socialism left in Poland that year  in the language of Nicolaus Copernicus  "desolate" money. The breakdown of public finances led to a rapid issue of money - its mass increased by 615 percent, and this - to the explosion of prices, which grew at a rate of 20-40 percent. monthly. This situation was in stark contrast to the relative macroeconomic stability that prevailed at the time of the b. Czechoslovakia and Hungary. In this respect, Poland had much worse starting conditions than the countries mentioned above. Against this background, among others, the price stability and the position of the Polish zloty in 2003 should be assessed. Why is price stability so desirable and high inflation so socially harmful? Let me remind you just a few reasons:  With low inflation, movements of specific prices inform about a change in the demand for particular goods; at high - prices cease to provide such important information. In conditions of price stability, it is therefore possible to better calculate and more accurately select investment projects. As a result, low inflation is conducive to an increase in the productivity of labor and capital - the most valuable lever for increasing prosperity.  The lower inflation, the less money companies lose as a result of certain tax measures. If depreciation write-offs  as is often the case  are calculated from the price at which you bought the machine, and then as a result of inflation the prices of porous machines increase, then the funds accumulated from the write-off are not enough to buy a new device when the previous one has already worn out. Thus, price stability increases the financial capacity of companies to invest. Conversely, high inflation imposes an invisible, insidious tax on businesses  an inflationary tax.  This insidious tax associated with high inflation also affects farms home, especially poorer. Poorer people have far fewer opportunities than the wealthy to protect their meager savings from inflation. By providing a low inflation to the public, one acts in particular in the interests of its poorer part. This importance of price stability is confirmed by numerous scientific studies.  Low inflation is much less volatile than high inflation. So you can better predict future prices. This limits the exuberant flow of income between savers and borrowers. The distribution of income depends more on people's decisions and less on the monetary disturbances triggered by irresponsible policies.  Finally, if you manage to keep inflation low for a long time, you get a psychological "credibility bonus." Thanks to experience, people expect prices to be stable in the future as well. Such mass beliefs mean that the temporary increase in the prices of some dr, e.g. oil, is less transferred to other prices and can be more easily neutralized than in a society that has a higher inflation in its fresh memory. The interest rate on a loan  not only nominal, but also real  may be lower, because there is less overhead on its price for the risk of inflation rising. These social benefits come from people's confidence that once achieved, price stability will be sustainable, i.e. it will not be undermined by the reckless acts or omissions of those who are responsible for living conditions in the country. *** In September 1998, the Monetary Policy Council of the first term considered it a strategic goal to bring inflation below 4% in 2003. In order to achieve this, the Council adopted further annual support objectives. The inflation target for 2003 was set at 3% with a deviation range of /-1 percentage point. When the Council started its work, inflation was 14%. At the end of 2003 it had fallen to 1.7 per cent. The strategic objective of monetary policy was achieved in 2003. Inflation, on the other hand, was slightly below the lower limit of the auxiliary target at the end of this year. 2. The main factors explaining the failure to hit the inflation target. 2.1. Controlled Prices. This small increase  0.3 percentage points  was entirely caused by a slower than expected increase in controlled prices, e.g. prices of electricity, gas, hot water, which is not significantly affected by monetary policy. They increased by 2.3 percent. The Council prepared the monetary policy assumptions for 2003 in mid-2002, and at that time it was predicted that controlled prices would increase by 3.6-4.8%. The forecast of such a scale of increases was in line with the available assumptions for the Budget Act for 2003. If the forecasts for the growth of administered prices were correct, inflation in December 2003 would amount to 2-2.3 per cent, so it would be within the range of permissible deviations from the inflation target for 2003. 2.2. External environment and inflation. Slower-than-expected economic growth of the main trading partner Polish also contributed to lower price growth. According to forecasts by the European Commission, the International Monetary Fund and the OECD, which were available in mid-2002, GDP in the eurozone countries was expected to increase by 2.9% in 2003, including Germany by 2.5-2.7%. The actual GDP growth rate in the eurozone was 0.5 per cent, and in Germany -0.1 per cent. This illustrates the difficulties of forecasting in countries with a longer history of market economy than ours. If economic growth in our main trading partners were in line with the original forecast, then  with the same monetary policy in Poland  stronger external demand would lead to faster GDP growth as well as higher inflation. 3. Monetary policy. 3.1. Basic data on monetary policy 1998-2003. Thank you, Mr Marshal. High Chamber! In 1998, when the Monetary Policy Council of the first term began its work, the basic rate of the central bank was 24 percent. When the Council was finishing its mission, this rate was 5.25 percent. Within six years, the basic interest rate of the NBP fell more than four times; half as much as in the Czech Republic and more than twice as much as in Hungary. In real terms, i.e. after excluding the effect of inflation, it decreased almost threefold - from almost 9 to 3.5 percent. The average real interest rate on PLN loans for enterprises fell more than four times - from over 15 to below 3.5 percent, while the average real interest rate on PLN housing loans almost twice - from 10.5 to below 6 percent. Of course, there is also the reverse side of the coin, namely  the average real interest rate on the deposit of households has decreased from about 5 to just over 1 percent, and enterprises - from nearly 9 to about -1 percent. *** 3.2. The shape of monetary policy in 2003. In 2003, the Monetary Policy Council made six percentage reductions to the NBP. All of them were carried out in the first half. The base rate - the reference rate - was reduced from 6.75 to 5.25 percent. The reductions in percentages in the first quarter of 2003 were supported by the persistence of -with low inflation - a factor limiting its future growth:  Household inflation expectations were low. People expected that the price increase in the perspective of the year would be clearly below 2 percent.  Most measures of core inflation, i.e. the indicator of the factor cleared of the impact of the central bank, did not have much influence, showed a slight downward trend.  Strong wage discipline in enterprises persisted.  Credit for companies increased slowly. On the other hand, the following may have contributed to the increase in future inflation:  faster and faster growth of cash in circulation,  high oil prices on world markets and the possibility of their further increase and  resurgent demand. In the opinion of the Monetary Policy Council, the initial phase of economic recovery does not increased the upward pressure on prices to such an extent as to threaten the achievement of the inflation target in 2004. 3.3. Factors hampering the conduct of monetary policy. 3.3.1. Rapid deterioration of the state finances. Mr. Marshal, High Sejm! Monetary policy in 2003 was conducted, as in previous years, with poor public finances, which made it difficult to stabilise inflation at a low level. In the recent history of Polish rulers have twice led to the collapse of the finances of their own state with disastrous consequences for the economy. The first drama took place in the 70s, when a boom financed by foreign loans led to the collapse and bankruptcy of Polish in the 80s. The Third Polish Republic started with such ballast, it was not, for example, in the former Czechoslovakia. Foreign debt has been reduced by half, we repay capital and interest from the rest. The second financial collapse of our country took place in the first half of 1989. The rapidly widening deficit then led, as I mentioned, to accelerated money printing and, as a result, to galloping inflation. After such experiences, public finances should become an object of special care in Poland. Unfortunately, since 2001 their condition has been clearly deteriorating. Deficit fiscal, i.e. that part of the state's expenditure, which is not covered by its income, rose from 3% of GDP in 2000 to more than 5.5% of GDP on average in 20012003. This year, despite the acceleration of the economic growth rate, the deficit will probably exceed 7% of GDP, if it is calculated according to the methodology used in previous years  i.e. the rectal one. To finance rapidly growing expenses, debts had to be incurred. In 2000, public debt amounted to about 40% of GDP. In 2003, the first prudential pr of the Public Finance Act exceeded 50% of GDP. The second PR, i.e. 55% of GDP, may be exceeded this year. Breaking the statutory limits reduces the credibility of the state that established them, and this has its high social price, which further increases other effects: In particular, the foreign debt incurred by the state quickly increased. Its share in the total public debt increased in 2003 by almost 1.5 percentage points and exceeded 40%. New debts amounting to 1.1 billion were incurred abroad. But foreign creditors also acquired a large part of the Treasury securities issued in the country. The value of their bonds increased - for the second year in a row - by PLN 10 billion; exceeded PLN 40 billion and was almost two times higher than at the end of 2000. Incurring growing debt with foreign creditors is increasingly making Poland dependent on external portfolio capital, which can easily flow away. His sudden flight in many countries ended in crisis. Domestic banks accounted for a large part of their internal debt. The public finance sector increased its debt there in the years 2001-2003 by nearly PLN 49 billion, i.e. by 82% nominally and by 71% in real terms. In the years 1998-2000 public debt in of banks increased by 7 billion, which meant a nominal increase of 14 per cent and a real decrease of 12 per cent. Public debt in banks fell from 73 to 50 per cent of the total amount of credit for companies. However, at the end of 2003, the budget debt in banks increased to 84 percent. this loan. The large deficit in public finances and its effect  the growing public debt  threaten price stability in several ways. First, you have to pay interest on the debt - the more the credibility of the country decreases as the debt grows. Rising interest rates are pushing out other state spending and creating pressure to increase taxes. Both are politically unpleasant. Therefore, high public debt gives rise to the temptation of some to get rid of it by printing money. Such an increase in the mass of money leads to an increase in inflation. Public expenditure is sometimes covered by an insidious inflation tax. This dangerous mechanism has been known for centuries. In 1776, Adam Smith, the father of modern economics, referred to the American colonies, wrote: "[Governments] in the event of extraordinary state needs issue paper money to cover public expenses, and then, when it comes without difficulty to the colonies, buy it up at a gradually decreasing price. In 1747 [the Gulf Of Massachusetts Provincial Government] thus paid off most of the public debt for one-tenth of the value of the promissory notes issued to secure them." Stanley Fischer, the eminent American economist, can therefore be followed: "The assertion . . . that inflation is always and everywhere a monetary phenomenon is true. However, the state does not print money without a reason. It usually prints them to finance the deficit in public finances. One can imagine a sharp increase in the mass of money, which would not be caused by the unnerved finances of the state, but this is an unlikely situation. Hence, violent inflation is almost always a fiscal phenomenon." After painful experiences with printing money to cover the effects of irresponsible fiscal policies, democratic countries have found a solution: an independent central bank that is entrusted with the constitutional role of guardian of the value of money. It is no coincidence, ladies and gentlemen, that attacks on such a bank intensify as the state's finances deteriorate. It becomes, in fact, an increasingly uncomfortable obstacle on the way to passing on the effect of this corruption  to the value of money, when it does not agree that the spoiled finances of the state should be joined by corrupt money. Secondly, increasing the public finance deficit threatens price stability even when there is no risk of money printing, because an independent central bank does not allow it. The increase in the deficit, on the one hand, often stimulates demand, and on the other hand, in various ways inhibits the growth of production capacity of enterprises, among other things, by limiting their access to credit. When demand exceeds the capacity of companies, it raises prices and/or spills out abroad, increasing imports. The ideology of uncritical stimulation of the economy is an ideology of slow and unstable growth, the threat of high prices and the lack of innovation in foreign trade. Thirdly, sick public finances may fuel upward pressure on prices, contributing to the weakening of the national currency. Decrease in the exchange rate in response to The disease of public finances is often postponed in time. At its earlier stage, the exchange rate may even strengthen, because the increasing percentage, on which the state borrows, attracts portfolio capital. But financial markets sooner or later value the risk of sick public finances. Their reaction in the form of an outflow of capital abroad leads to a weakening of the exchange rate  the deeper it was, the greater its earlier inflow and the resulting strengthening of the exchange rate. By postponing the repair of the finances of one's own state, one introduces into society and its economy a growing uncertainty about the future external the value of the national money, and this is not conducive  to put it mildly  long-term decisions of the investor. *** The disease of public finances not only  as you can see  hinders the fight against inflation, but also harms the development of the economy in other ways. In an extreme case, the state enters the debt trap, which happened to Poland in the 70s. Such a budget disaster breaks down the finances of people and enterprises, and this leads to a collapse of production and a sharp increase in unemployment. The persistent deficit and growing public debt, even if it does not end in the collapse of the economy, systematically suppresses its development. It consumes part of the private savings that could and should finance the investments of enterprises. In competition with the state borrower, entrepreneurs are usually in a lost position. The growth of the economy is stifled not only by the deficit, but also by what constitutes its the main source, namely - by excessive public spending. Their large share in GDP inhibits, not stimulates, long-term development, even if it does not lead to the accumulation of state debt:  First, spending public money is usually preceded by a less careful bill than spending private money.  Secondly, the bulk of public spending - social spending often traps people in various dependencies. They reduce the readiness to look for a job, and by triggering pressure for abuse, they often end up in wasps who do not require support. According to the latest estimates of the World Bank, half of the social spending in Poland (excluding expenditure on pensions) goes to families who are either not poor or receive from the state more than is needed to stay above the threshold of the ubtwa.  Thirdly, large budget expenditures require high taxes, and these additionally limit people's willingness to work and save, and reduce the ability and willingness of companies to develop, which gives employment. It is no coincidence that huge budget expenditures in Poland are accompanied by an exceptionally low percentage of people aged 15-64 working in Poland. It is just over 50% - in Europe there is a lower employment rate only in Turkey and Bulgaria. This means that there is almost one non-working person of working age per one working person. People are most harmed when wealth is shared that does not yet exist, or the fruits of growth that have not been able to be consolidated. Some of the proponents of the doctrine of "the more budget spending, the more prosperity", i.e. the doctrine of stimulation, cite the examples of today's wealthy countries to justify the thesis that a large share of these expenditures in GDP does not harm and even favors development. This is an example of erroneous inference. This share in the period when developed countries were just building their wealth was much lower than today in Poland, and as the social state expanded, the development of these countries became slower. In the sixties, public spending in OECD countries amounted to an average of 29.4 per cent of GDP, which is one third less than today in Poland, and the economies of these countries grew at a rate of over 4 per cent per year. In the seventies, these expenditures increased to 37.5 per cent of GDP, and the dynamics of development fell to 2 per cent. In the eighties, there was a further increase in expenditure to 44.5 per cent of GDP and a further decrease in the growth rate to 1.7 per cent. In the nineties, expenditure reached 46.3 per cent, which is about the same as in much poorer Poland, and the dynamics of development amounted to 1.5 per cent. The expansion of the welfare state is not, of course, the only reason for the decline in the growth rate in developed countries, but - as many scientific studies show - it is an important factor. Large public spending in OECD countries not only hampered development, but also did not go hand in hand with improved indicators of social well-being, such as life expectancy, infant mortality, the level of education of the population, the efficiency of the justice system, or the quality of transport infrastructure. According to a study published by the European Central Bank, developed countries the lowest share of public spending in GDP has achieved  on average  better quality of life indicators than those in which this share was higher. The recovery of public finances necessary to save the long-term growth of the Polish economy does not necessarily mean its slowdown at the finish line. On the contrary, if excessive public spending is significantly reduced, then people make decisions that give almost immediate economic acceleration, because they do not have to worry that the improvement of the state's finances is only temporary and their illness will be repeated. As a result, the following non-Keynesian mechanisms are triggered:  Reducing public spending leaves more money for businesses and the consumer.  The convergence of the state's finances removes uncertainty in the financial markets, which reduces interest rates and increases the availability of credit.  The reduced financial risk of the country stimulates the inflow of foreign direct investment.  Reducing wage spending in the public sector strengthens wage discipline in enterprises, and this increases their competitiveness and increases profits from which investments can be financed.  Domestic investors are no longer afraid that they will have to pay higher taxes in the future. This improves the assessment of the profitability of the project and, as a result, unlocks investments.  Finally, for the same reason, consumers may be more inclined to make new purchases. The path of radical healing of its finances was chosen, among others, by Ireland in the second half of the eighties and from a sick man of Europe turned into an economic tiger. The country of our region has recently been repeated by the Baltic states. Between 2000 and 2001, they reduced public spending by 5-7% of GDP, and their economy grew from 5% to over 7% per year during that time. In Poland, the op comes across a program that would reduce the deficit by 1-2 percent of GDP in the next three years. Mr. Marshal, High Sejm! Without the recovery of public finances, it is impossible to maintain the rapid growth of the economy in Poland. But the Polish society is already paying for the sick finances of the state. The lack of clear prospects for their rapid improvement with growing public debt increases the risk of investing in Treasury securities, and this increases their profitability. Credit rating agencies have already downgraded the rating of the Polish's ability to service national public debt. Since the spring of 2003, the gap between the yields of e.g. 10-year bonds in our country and in Germany has almost tripled. At the turn of April and May 2003 it was just over 1 percentage point, and now about 3. At the same time, in our neighbors, where public finance recovery programs were introduced  in Slovakia this mark-up was less than 1 percentage point, and in Lithuania it fell from almost 2 percentage points to less than 0.5 percentage points. In Poland, the costs of servicing only this debt, which was incurred at a higher percentage until June 30 this year, will be  until its repayment  higher as a result of increased interest in total. by PLN 2.6 billion in current prices. Such a bill has already been issued to the Polish society as a result of postponing the recovery of public finances. If the large budget deficit persists, the burden on our future will continue to rise. Maintaining a high deficit, despite the rapid growth of the economy, is, ladies and gentlemen, like burning a fire in the forest in a hot summer with borrowed banknotes. It was best not to light such a fire, but if it is already burning, the most reasonable thing that can be done is to extinguish it quickly. 3.5. Monetary policy summary. Mr. Marshal, High Sejm! In recent years, inflation has been brought to a low level. In this way, from the monetary side, the foundation for the future rapid development was laid. But low inflation is not given to any society once and for all. This is shown by the situation this year and the reaction of the current Monetary Policy Council. To conclude the discussion of monetary policy, let me quote the words of John Maynard Keynes: "[Inflation] is the form of taxation that is most difficult for people to avoid. This tax can be imposed even by the weakest state, which cannot enforce anything else." High inflation is a symptom of a weak state. But a strong state is not only low inflation. It is also good law, efficient justice and security, it is a wide range of freedoms well protected by the state, means healthy finances and low taxes are everything that is conducive to long-term development. A strong state creates the conditions in which people find opportunities and incentives for decent work, for creativity, for innovation and, as a result, for improving their standard of living and the international position of their own country. Much remains to be done to build such a state in Poland. 4. Stability of the banking system. Mr Speaker, Honourable Members, The second, basic area of activity of the National Bank of Poland are activities for the stability of the banking system, which is the main part of the financial system in Poland. The financial system plays a fundamental role in the modern economy: it mobilizes savings, influences the investment project and the way of running companies, provides payment services. Scientific research conducted in recent years shows that the development of the financial sector is an important force for the development of the entire economy. This positive impact is primarily about increasing its effectiveness. External financing of companies by banks or the capital market increases the efficiency of investments and running businesses. In light of these results, the question arises: what favors and what hinders the development of the financial system? Well, this development  to an exceptionally large extent  is based on rational, that is, based on calculation, trust. First, it's about people's trust in money. In a situation where its value is not stable, they are less likely to keep their savings in it. And it is from financial savings that capital for enterprises comes. Lowering inflation and keeping it low is therefore an important action for the development of the financial system and, as a result, for the development of the entire economy. Secondly, the idea is that financial investors, that is, providers of capital: holders of savings deposits, banks, shareholders of companies, various investment funds, can have a reasonable confidence that they will get their money back with an adequate surplus. This, in turn, depends on the level of legal protection of the investor. The smaller and less protected by the state their rights, the less available and more expensive capital is for domestic entrepreneurs, because the risk of losing money raises the price of capital for all who need it. Its availability and cost, especially for small businesses, depend to a large extent on the scope of secured transactions, i.e. based on such legal institutions as pledge, assignment, transfer of ownership. The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development examined in 2003 the situation with regard to these transactions in the post-socialist countries, awarding them marks of 1 to 10 points. Hungary, Latvia, Slovakia, the Czech Republic, Lithuania and Estonia fared best, scoring above 8 points. Poland with a score of less than 4 points placed at the end of the list; only Armenia, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Azerbaijan and Bosnia and Herzegovina achieved worse rates. Poor Polish rating is not so much due to poor quality of the law, how much of its slow enforcement by the institutions of the judiciary and debt collection. In Poland, the banking sector is the largest segment of the national financial system  in 2003, the bank's assets accounted for 77 per cent of the assets of the entire financial system. The bank's particular position in the Polish financial system means that their situation is subject to constant and thorough assessment by the General Inspectorate of Banking Supervision and the Banking Supervision Commission. It should be emphasized, however, that no banking nave can replace the professionalism and responsibility of the owners and management of the bank. In the years 2001-2002, the banking system in Poland passed the resilience test. The economic downturn then resulted in a certain reduction in the quality of the loan portfolio. Banks created special-purpose reserves to cover losses and used their legal collateral. The year 2003 brought about positive changes  economic recovery and improvement of the situation of enterprises. These phenomena have not yet been reflected in a deeper decline in the share of NPLs in the bank's assets, but they have stopped the trend towards the deterioration of the quality of the loan portfolio and contributed to the improvement of the bank's financial situation. Banks have shown resilience to less favourable economic conditions and a weaker financial situation of their clients thanks to the appropriate level of equity. Proper provision of this capital to the bank meant that despite the significant burden of the costs of creating special-purpose reserves, the banking sector was not in danger of insolvency or disruption of its economy. The solvency ratio in 2003 was about 5 percentage points higher than the required eight percent minimum. Over the past year, the National Bank of Polish has carried out the following main activities for the stability of the banking system:  Employees of the General Inspectorate of Banking Supervision examined the situation in individual banks and in the entire banking sector on an ongoing basis. The nave was carried out in the form of direct inspections and through the analysis of reporting. GINB exercised a special overhead of banks in financial difficulty.  The National Bank of Polish participated in the work on new EU regulations  directives on the implementation of the provisions of the Second Basel Agreement, the so-called new capital agreement and effective supervision, the bank's rating system, harmonization of supervisory practices.  The National Polish Bank has proposed new prudential regulations. I will mention here only the most important regulation from the point of view of the bank's operation, regarding the classification of credit to the risk category, which was the result of an agreement concluded between the National Bank of Poland, the Ministry of Finance, the Ministry of Economy, Labor and Social Policy and the Polish Bank Association. It reduced the restrictiveness of the classification of receivables, extended the permissible debt repayment periods and enabled the adoption of the best legal collateral as a basis for assessing quality. Credit. The new system also includes incentives for the bank to accelerate the enforcement of overdue receivables. 5. Management of foreign exchange reserves. Mr Speaker, Honourable Members, I will now turn to the third important area of activity of the National Bank of Poland. -management of official foreign exchange reserves. The National Bank of Polish is guided by three principles:  achieving a high level of security of invested funds,  maintaining the necessary degree of liquidity, ensuring the efficient implementation of payment obligations Polish,  and  with the above 2 limitations  obtaining maximum income while observing the above rules. Ensuring a high degree of security and liquidity of reserves is provided by the system of limit investment exposure, regarding the currency structure, credit rating of the issuer of the security in the world and the duration of deposits. Within the adopted limits, the currency structure of the reserves managed by the National Polish Bank in 2003 included three currencies: the US dollar, the euro and the pound sterling. The investment strategy in 2003 was based on forecasts on the situation on the securities market. According to it, in in the first half of 2003, a higher share of securities with longer maturities was maintained, as they gave the highest rate of return. After the sharp depreciation of these securities in July 2003, their share in the portfolios was reduced due to the decrease in their value. This procedure turned out to be accurate, because in the second half these securities gave the lowest yield of all investment instruments. Such a strategy allowed to achieve in 2003 an income from investing reserves in the amount of USD 1.0 billion (PLN 3.7 billion). The obtained doch accounted for over 90 per cent of the profit of the National Bank of Poland transferred to the state budget. In addition to the income from investing, foreign exchange reserves bring other important social benefits. First of all, they support the stability of the zloty exchange rate. Of course, even the largest reserves cannot replace good economic policy. They can, however, mitigate the effects of unexpected shocks. Secondly, an adequate level of reserves is of great importance for the financial credibility of the country. With the same trade deficit and foreign debt, the larger the foreign exchange reserves, the lower the perceived risk of investing in a country's currency. The lack of sufficient reserves with an unfavorable arrangement of other factors can cause capital flight, a drastic increase in market percentages and a sharp weakening of the value of domestic money. The effects of such an event would be felt by the entire economy: at the end of 2003, foreign currency debt accounted for about 60 per cent of all corporate debt (not counting foreign trade loans), about 30 per cent of household debt and 35 per cent of public finance sector debt. The high level of reserves, strengthening the credibility of the country, allows the state and private economic operators to borrow foreign loans at lower interest rates than when the level of reserves is perceived by potential creditors as too low. According to international research, the level of reserves is one of the amounts affecting the so-called risk premium, i.e. the additional interest rate that investors demand for granting a loan to the government or companies of a given country. The higher the level of reserves, the lower, to a certain point, the risk premium demanded and the lower the costs of servicing foreign debt. At the current level of this debt, the decline in financial credibility resulting from the depletion of reserves would cost our country a lot. At the end of 2003, the NBP's official reserve assets amounted to US34.2 billion and were US4.4 billion higher than a year earlier. This increase was mainly due to the strengthening of the euro against the dollar, because a large part of our reserves and the income generated from their investment were held in euros. The practice of the central bank shows that the level of foreign exchange reserves for less developed countries considered safe exceeds the value of six months of imports, and their relation to the country's long-term foreign debt should be at least 100 percent. At the end of 2003, the foreign exchange reserves of the National Bank of Poland covered a value of 5.3 months of imports, and the level of our reserves to the long-term debt In a situation of increased risk, foreign investors may, however, demand the return of part of the long-term debt, e.g. by selling Polish treasury bonds. Therefore, the ratio of foreign exchange reserves to all external debt must also be taken into account. In 2003, foreign exchange reserves covered about 32 per cent of this debt. This was clearly more than in countries where currency crises have occurred in recent years, such as Russia, Argentina or Brazil, but less than in most countries of our region, which this year joined the European Union. The Czech Republic (88 per cent), Slovenia (82 per cent), Slovakia (64 per cent) and Lithuania (40 per cent) recorded a higher level of this measure than Poland. On the other hand, in terms of another measure: the ratio of foreign exchange reserves to GDP, Poland with 16 per cent was at the level of Hungary, well below Slovakia (36 per cent), the Czech Republic (31 per cent) and Lithuania (19 per cent). All in all, it can be considered that the foreign exchange reserves of the National Bank of Poland have reached a certain security level for the country. The importance of foreign exchange reserves will increase in the future. Our country is waiting on the way to the euro two years of experience under the European exchange rate mechanism ERM2, in which to maintain the exchange rate in the fluctuation range may be necessary interventions of the central bank on the currency market. Reliable and therefore effective interventions will require a high level of foreign exchange reserves, which will prevent possible speculative attacks calculated to weaken the zloty exchange rate. 6. Other areas of NBP's activity. Mr Speaker, High House. Finally, I would like to mention the reforms that the NBP introduces in order to reduce the cost of operation or improve the quality of its activities.  The National Bank of Polish systematically reduces the costs of its operations. In 2003, the restructuring of the network was completed, reducing the number of local branches from 49 to 16. As a result of the restructuring, employment fell by over 17 percent, which, combined with a reduction in administrative expenses, will allow to achieve savings estimated at PLN 76 million per year. The assets of the liquidated field units were distributed as follows: 17 properties with equipment with a market value of PLN 74 million were transferred to the State Treasury; 11 buildings were allocated for the needs of the court and the District Prosecutor's Offices, 4 for the central administration, and 4 for the local government administration.  In 2003, the NBP continued its efforts to ensure the stability and development of the payment system. One of the priority tasks in this area was to prepare the central bank to participate in the TARGET system, which allows cross-border payments between European Union countries. Joining the system will allow to improve the handling of cross-border payments and reduce their cost.  In 2003, the National Bank of Poland introduced modern internal audit principles aimed at improving management at the National Bank of Poland, in particular in the field of risk management. The adjustments also concerned accounting, the rules of which since 1 January 2004 have been harmonised with those applied by the central banks of the European Central Bank System.  By improving the service of its clients, the National Bank of Polish has completed the introduction of an electronic banking system for account holders. In May 2003, the National Bank of Polish obtained the ISO 9001:2000 quality certificate for servicing bank accounts using the electronic banking system.  As part of its statistical activities in 2003, work was carried out to adapt monetary, banking and balance of payments statistics to the requirements of the ECB and Eurostat. Preparations have also been made to expand the scope of statistical surveys, which will enable more accurate analyses of the financial sector in Poland in the future.  Following the example of the best central banks in the world, the National Bank of Polish develops activities aimed at disseminating economic knowledge and understanding the principles of the market economy. In 2003, over 35,000 pupils and students took part in educational projects of the National Bank of Poland addressed to young people. Thanks to the involvement of the National Bank of Poland in October 2003 at the almost 90 universities have started their studies almost 1600 scholarship holders of the "Bridge Scholarships" program - a graduate of glass from small towns and villages. In cooperation with local and central media, more than 40 educational project on the bank and financial institutions in Poland. In their the result was 67 television programs, 645 radio broadcasts and numerous cycles article in the press. 7. Termination. Mr. Marshal, High Sejm! Article 227(1) of the Constitution of our country "(...) The National Bank of Polish is responsible for the value of Polish money." Such a definition of the mission of the Polish central bank results from the conviction, grounded in economic theory and confirmed by world experience, that the greatest contribution that monetary policy can make to the long-term development is sound money; at the price of dearness, no one has yet bought prosperity. In order for money to always enjoy the trust of the people, a stable banking system, sufficient foreign exchange reserves are needed, deterring from an attack on the exchange rate of the national currency, healthy state finances. In an effort to ensure low inflation, to ensure the security of the banking system and to manage its foreign exchange reserves, the National Bank of Polish fulfils the task entrusted to it by the Constitution. In this way, he contributes to the development of our economy and, I firmly believe, serves the people.

Po pierwsze, od dugu trzeba paci odsetki - tym wiksze, im bardziej spada wiarygodno kraju w miar narastania zaduenia. Rosnce odsetki wypychaj inne wydatki pastwa i rodz presj na wzrost podatk. Jedno i drugie jest politycznie nieprzyjemne. Dlatego wysoki dug publiczny rodzi u niektych pokus, aby pozby si go przez dodruk pienidza. Takie zwikszenie masy pienidza prowadzi do wzrostu inflacji. Wydatki publiczne s wczas pokrywane przez podstpny podatek inflacyjny. Ten grony mechanizm jest znany od stuleci. W 1776 roku Adam Smith, ojciec nowoczesnej ekonomii, majc na myli amerykaskie kolonie, pisa: [rzdy] w razie nadzwyczajnych potrzeb pastwowych emituj pienidz papierowy na pokrycie wydatk publicznych, aby nastpnie, kiedy kolonii przychodzi to bez trudu, wykupywa go po stopniowo obniajcej si cenie. W r. 1747 [zarzd prowincji Zatoki Massachusetts] spaci w ten spos wikszo dug publicznych za jedn dziesit wartoci weksli, jakie wystawiono dla ich zabezpieczenia. Mona wic powtzy za Stanleyem Fischerem, wybitnym amerykaskim ekonomist, Twierdzenie (), e inflacja zawsze i wszdzie stanowi zjawisko pienine, jest prawdziwe. Jednak pastwo nie drukuje pienidzy bez przyczyny. Zwykle drukuje je dla sfinansowania deficytu w finansach publicznych. Mona sobie wyobrazi gwatowny wzrost masy pienidza, kty nie byby spowodowany niezrnowaonymi finansami pastwa, ale jest to sytuacja nieprawdopodobna. Std te, gwatowna inflacja jest prawie zawsze zjawiskiem fiskalnym. Po bolesnych dowiadczeniach z drukowaniem pienidza w celu pokrycia skutkw nieodpowiedzialnej polityki fiskalnej kraje demokratyczne znalazy rozwizanie: niezaleny bank centralny, ktemu powierza si konstytucyjn rol stranika wartoci pienidza. Nie jest przypadkiem Szanowni Pastwo, e ataki na taki bank nasilaj si w miar psucia finans pastwa. Staje si on bowiem wczas coraz bardziej niewygodn przeszkod na drodze do przerzucenia skutk tego psucia  na warto pienidza, gdy nie zgadza si, aby do zepsutych finans pastwa doczy zepsuty pienidz. Po drugie, zwikszanie deficytu finans publicznych zagraa stabilnoci cen take wtedy, gdy nie ma ryzyka dodruku pienidza, bo nie pozwala na to niezaleny bank centralny. Wzrost deficytu bowiem z jednej strony czsto pobudza popyt, a z drugiej na rne sposoby hamuje wzrost zdolnoci produkcyjnych przedsibiorstw, m. in. ograniczajc ich dostp do kredytu. Gdy popyt przewysza zdolnoci wytwcze firm, to podbija ceny i/lub wylewa si za granic, zwikszajc import. Ideologia bezkrytycznego pobudzania gospodarki, to ideologia powolnego i niestabilnego wzrostu, zagroenia droyzn i niernowagi w handlu zagranicznym. Po trzecie, chore finanse publiczne mog podsyca presj na wzrost cen przyczyniajc si do osabienia kursu waluty krajowej.
