Takie okrelenie misji banku centralnego wynika z przekonania, e najwiksz wartoci, jak polityka pienina moe wnie do dugofalowego rozwoju Polski, jest silny i stabilny zoty. Jako Prezes Narodowego Banku Polskiego w 2007 roku chc pooy nacisk na: -rozw Banku w kierunku wiodcego w Europie rodkowo - Wschodniej orodka analityczno  badawczego i zwikszenie wykorzystania potencjau regionalnych orodk akademickich. Dlatego te w biecym roku powoana zostaa Rada Naukowa przy Zarzdzie NBP, zoona z wybitnych ekonomist z najwikszych uczelni ekonomicznych w Polsce, - przeprowadzenie kompleksowej i obiektywnej analizy na temat koszt i korzyci przyjcia wspnej waluty przygotowanego we wsppracy z ekspertami instytucji finansowych, przedstawicielami rodowiska akademickiego oraz parterami spoecznymi. W tym celu powoane zostao Biuro ds. Integracji ze Stref Euro. - wzmocnienie przejrzystoci polityki pieninej, ktego jednym z element jest publikowany od maja 2007 roku syntetyczny opis dyskusji po decyzyjnych posiedzeniach Rady Polityki Pieninej tzw. minutes; dc do jeszcze wikszej transparentnoci polityki pieninej zamierzam zabiega o dokonanie przez Wysoki Sejm odpowiednich zmian ustawowych umoliwiajcych szybsze przekazywanie otoczeniu informacji o przebiegu obrad Rady Polityki Pieninej, -wzrost bezpieczestwa finansowego oraz przygotowanie sprawnego systemu zarzdzania sytuacj kryzysow. W tym celu podjem dziaania zmierzajce do przesunicia likwidacji GINB na 1 stycznia 2013 roku oraz utworzenie Komitetu Stabilnoci Finansowej, w skad ktego wchodziliby wysokiej rangi przedstawiciele Ministra Finans, Narodowego Banku Polskiego, Komisji Nadzoru Finansowego, Komisji Nadzoru Bankowego i Bankowego Funduszu Gwarancyjnego. Na forum Komitetu uzgadniane byyby dziaania, suce wspieraniu stabilnoci finansowej w kraju, zarno w sytuacjach normalnych jak rnie w przypadku zagroenia kryzysem. Przy tej okazji zwracam si do Pa Posanek i Pan Pos z prob o uchwalenie przez Wysoki Sejm Ustawy zmieniajcej ustaw o nadzorze nad rynkiem finansowym. Podsumowujc, chc stwierdzi, e Narodowy Bank Polski poprzez dbanie o silny pienidz i stabilny system finansowy, a take nieustannie pracujc nad jakoci wykonywanych zada, wnosi i bdzie wnosi istotny i trway wkad w systematyczn popraw warunk ycia naszego spoeczestwa. Dzikuj za uwag.

Title: Speech
text: Przemienie Slawomir Skrzypek Of the President of the NBP before the Sejm Public Finance Committee on 31 January 2008. High Commission, Mr President, I would like to thank the rapporteur for this report. Thank you for the invitation to the meeting of the Public Finance Committee, all the more so because the current situation in the National Bank of Poland has not yet been the subject of the High Commission's deliberations. As I announced when I was still a candidate for the President of the NBP, I do not avoid meetings with representatives of the Parliament. The situation in the National Bank of Poland is stable. The bank effectively fulfills the tasks entrusted to it. Regardless of personnel changes, the Management Board of the National Bank of Poland operates efficiently and effectively. That is why I believe that the recent public remarks made to the Management Board and the President of the NBP, to which I will address in detail in the further part of my speech, are, firstly, unjustified, and secondly, publicizing them does not serve the reputation and stability of the central bank. High Commission! For me, as the President of the National Bank of Poland, a transparent and clear way of communicating about the activities of the National Bank of Poland is particularly important, but it should be carried out in a way that guarantees respect for the independence of the central bank. Accordingly, my statement will be limited by Article 227 of the Constitution, Article 108 of the Treaty establishing the European Community and other provisions. In implementing Article 22(2) of the NBP Act, I would like to present to the High Commission information on the activities of the National Bank of Poland. The highest statutory good for the National Bank of Poland is to ensure the stability of the country's financial system. Therefore, after the liquidation of the General Inspectorate of Banking Supervision in order to maintain the security of the financial system, as a result of a joint initiative of me, the Minister of Finance and the Chairman of the Polish Financial Supervision Authority, at the end of December 2007, the Financial Stability Committee was established. I would like to add that I had already sought to establish the Committee by statutory means in April 2007. The Committee consisted of the Minister of Finance, the President of the National Bank of Poland, the Chairman of the Polish Financial Supervision Authority. Its aim is to ensure effective cooperation to support the stability of the national safety net system, including coordination of activities and exchange of information to protect and support financial stability in the country. At this point, I want to assure you that despite the disturbances on the international financial markets, the banking system in Poland is stable and safe. Reserve management at the National Bank of Poland is becoming more and more efficient. The return on foreign exchange reserves denominated in the currency of the individual investment vehicles in 2007 was the highest in four years and amounted to about 5.4%, while the average yield on reserves in the years 2004-2006 was at the level of 2.8%. In recent years, the profitability of provisions has been positively influenced by the decisions to change the currency structure taken by the NBP Management Board for 2006 and 2007. In 2007, a long-term foreign exchange reserves management strategy was adopted aimed at maximizing the profitability of NBP's foreign exchange reserves in the long term, within the acceptable level of financial risk and taking into account the limitations resulting from the NBP's mission. Last year, the National Bank of Poland also undertook organizational initiatives aimed at modernizing the bank along the lines of the best-managed central banks in Europe. Among other things, through the creation of the Economic Institute, the process of strengthening the analytical and research functions of the bank began. The creation of the Economic Institute will increase the possibilities of developing economic research and will contribute to an increase in the quality of analyses prepared at the NBP. Work has also been initiated on the creation of a comprehensive Report on the accession of Polish to the euro area. The report is being prepared in cooperation with all stakeholders in the euro: public administration institutions, the world of science, financial institutions, employers' and employees' unions. A preliminary draft of this document will be ready in the middle of the year, while the full report will be ready in December 2008. I have taken the liberty of giving the President an outline of this report, counting on the valuable contribution of the High Commission to improving this report. Due to recent events related to the fact of resignation by the First Deputy President of the NBP and the unprecedented publication of the reasons for this decision by him, as well as in the face of his formulation of a number of false allegations, out of concern for the reputation of the National Bank of Poland and the collegiate body, which is the NBP Management Board, I feel obliged to provide the High Commission with reliable information in this matter. In the wake of press releases, based on an incorrect assessment of the factual and legal situation, there were m.in allegations regarding the decisions taken at the National Bank of Poland and their non-compliance with the NBP Act. I would like to remind you that in accordance with Article 6 of the Act on the National Bank of Poland, the bodies of the National Bank of Poland are the President, the Monetary Policy Council and the Management Board. These bodies have separate areas of competence defined by law. The competences of the Management Board are defined in Article 17 of the NBP Act, in accordance with the activities of the NBP are directed by the Management Board. Within the scope of its competences, the Management Board has the power to determine the m.in scope of activity and internal organization of the NBP Head Office and other organizational units of the NBP, as provided for in Article 7 paragraph 2 point 2 of the Act and the principles of organization and division of tasks in the NBP, as provided for in Article 17(4)(9) of the NBP Act. And it was on the basis of these provisions that on 26 January 2001, during the term of office of the previous President of the NBP, Prof. Leszek Balcerowicz, the NBP Management Board adopted amendments to the NBP Organizational Regulations. These changes consisted in introducing for the first time an institution authorized by the President of the NBP member of the Management Board exercising on behalf of the President the current supervision over the subordinates of the President departments and organizational units. Based on this change, the President of the NBP, Prof. Leszek Balcerowicz, authorized a member of the Management Board to supervise the indicated departments on an ongoing basis. The correctness and compliance of this solution with the NBP Act has never been questioned by anyone. Also, the annual audit of the Supreme Audit Office did not undermine the properties of these solutions. Therefore, the amendment to the Nbp Organizational Regulations undertaken by the current Management Board on 5 November 2007 was only a continuation of the solutions that have been functioning for 6 years in the National Bank of Poland! The possibility of making such a decision by the Management Board in the light of the provisions of the NBP Act was confirmed not only by the NBP Legal Department but also by eminent experts in the field of law: Prof. Piotr Winczorek, Dr. Tomasz Stawecki and Prof. Adam Jaroszy?ski. I would also like to confirm with full conviction that in the National Bank of Poland it is the Vice-Presidents who manage the work departments designated by the President. Taking responsibility for the supervised work department, they also have a real impact on its shape. In addition, the Vice-Presidents hold numerous positions of The Chairmen of the Commission operating in the National Bank of Poland and represent the National Bank of Polish outside. And so, the First Deputy President of the NBP d0 Mr. Jerzy Pruski, supervising the following departments: Statistics, Financial System and Operational Risk Management Team, at the same time serves as the Chairman of the Committee for Risk Management, the Commission for the Introduction of Euro Banknotes and Coins, the Committee on Budgets and the Committee on Foreign Exchange Markets. He is also a permanent representative of the NBP in the Committee of the Minister's Council, as well as a member of, among others, the Financial Market Development Council or the Public Debt Management Committee. In addition, until 31 December 2007, he was a representative of the NBP in the Banking Supervision Commission. The Vice-President of the NBP, Krzysztof Rybi?ski, is responsible for the Department of Foreign Operations, the Department of Financial Risk Management and the Department of the Payment System. He represents the NBP in the Polish Financial Supervision Authority, chairs the Investment Committee of Foreign Exchange Reserves, the Payment System Council. In addition, he supervises many important projects at the NBP, e.g. the implementation of the issue and treasury system and nbp's preparations to join the Target2 platform. The appointment of the Vice-Presidents' work department by the President of the NBP is an action taken pursuant to Article 10(3) of the Act. o NBP, who authorizes the President of the NBP to do so. It should be emphasized that the above right is an independent competence of the President of the NBP. Only the decision of the President of the NBP depends on which labor departments will appoint to head vice presidents. The NBP Act does not set any limits in determining the scope of the work department, which is entrusted to vice-presidents pursuant to Article 10(3) of the Act. In this respect, the President of the NBP is left with discretionary freedom, that is to say, freedom of decision. This position is also confirmed by the legal opinions of Professor Piotr Winczorek and Tomasz Stawecki, quoted earlier, quote: "No standards or guidelines are included in the Act, which could constitute a way to limit the discretionary decision of the President of the NBP. Nor is a decision in that regard determined by procedural rules.' (...) End of quote. It is worth recalling that in September 2005, during the period of his function by the previous President of the NBP, he decided to significantly change the Vice-President's work department, excluding key analytical departments from the management of one of the Vice-Presidents, transferring them to the area of responsibility of the President, in which they remain to this day. At that time, no one questioned the legal basis of this decision, neither the First Deputy President of the NBP nor the Vice-President, nor did it become the subject of public discussion, as it is currently the case. Because, as I mentioned earlier, Article 10(3) gives the President discretion in this regard. Referring to the issues related to the exercise of the position of the head of the department by a member of the Management Board at the same time, I would like to explain that this form raised doubts in the light of the provision of Article 18 of the Act. about the National Bank of Poland, which explicitly states that a Member of the Management Board may not occupy any other function. The analysis of the best corporate governance practices recommended by international financial institutions, as well as the unequivocal critical opinion of the world expert in the field of central bank management, Mr. John Mendzela and legal opinions, which are in the possession of the NBP, confirmed the legal defect of the previously used management structure. The Management Board adopted a solution aimed at improving the management of the Bank and greater empowerment of the Management Board members in order to ensure the proper functioning of the Management Board and the Bank. I would also like to emphasize that none of the solutions adopted by the Management Board limited the rights of a member of the Management Board to participate in the decision-making process and present their opinions, which was confirmed by the statements of the Member of the Management Board. In conclusion, once again I would like to thank the High Commission for the opportunity to present the specifics of the functioning of the central bank, which is the National Polish Bank, and to inform about the Achievements of the Bank and the problems that arose after a year of my function as the President of the NBP. The fact that the Bank's internal affairs have been made public and its credibility has been undermined by making unjustified statements, makes me very unsure of the reputation and prestige of the National Bank of Poland. That is why I am sympathetic to the High Commission's concern for the functioning of the NBP. This also confirms my belief in the common responsibility for the fate of the Polish zloty. However, I would like to recall the decision of the Constitutional Tribunal issued on behalf of the Republic of Poland on 22 September 2006, which refers to the issue of the independence of the National Bank of Poland, quote :'The President of the NBP does not have immunity in respect of his activities, but this does not mean that it is permissible to create a situation that gives the impression of political pressure. Such an impression could have a negative "chilling effect" on the exercise of the statutory powers of a body independent of parliament" end of the quote. This quote can be treated as a summary of the situation that has arisen in recent days. One of the competences of the Management Board resulting from Article 7(2)(2) of the NBP Act is "defining the principles of organization and division of tasks in NBP" and the encroachment of other bodies, such as external institutions, in such decisions would amount to unjustified interference in the internal affairs of the NBP, and this would mean a violation of the independence of the central bank guaranteed by the Constitution and the regulations of the Community law, including in particular Article 108 of the Treaty establishing the European Community. The High Commission will allow me to recall that this provision states that, I quote, 'in the exercise of the powers and the tasks and duties which are entrusted to them by this Treaty and by the Statute of the European Central System, neither the European Central Bank nor the national central bank nor the member of any of their decision-making bodies shall seek or take instructions from the institutions or body of the Community, the government of the Member States or any other body. The institutions and bodies of the Member States, as well as the governments of the Member States, undertake to respect this principle and not to seek to influence the member decision-making body of the ECB or the national central bank in the performance of their tasks", end of quotation. The actions of the NBP Management Board and the President of NBP were assessed as lawful in the opinions of the Legal Department as well as in the opinions of eminent authorities in the field of legal sciences. By taking care of strong money and a stable financial system, as well as the high quality of its tasks, the National Bank of Polish makes a significant and lasting contribution to the systematic improvement of the living conditions of our society. This task can be carried out only in conditions of calm and lack of political pressure, which is guaranteed to the National Bank of Poland by the Constitution of the Republic of Poland. Therefore, High Commission, honourable Members, in view of the difficult situation on the international financial markets, it is extremely important for me to feel that responsibility for the stability of the Polish currency is our great concern. Thank you for your attention.
text_original: Przemienie Sawomira Skrzypka Prezesa NBP przed Sejmow Komisj Finans Publicznych w dniu 31 stycznia 2008 r. Wysoka Komisjo, Panie Przewodniczcy! Dzikuj za zaproszenie na posiedzenie Komisji Finans Publicznych, tym bardziej e bieca sytuacja w Narodowym Banku Polskim nie bya jeszcze przedmiotem obrad Wysokiej Komisji. Tak jak zapowiadaem bdc jeszcze kandydatem na Prezesa NBP, nie unikam spotka z przedstawicielami Parlamentu. Sytuacja w Narodowym Banku Polskim jest stabilna. Bank w spos efektywny wypenia powierzone mu zadania. Niezalenie od zmian kadrowych, Zarzd Narodowego Banku Polskiego dziaa sprawnie i efektywnie. Dlatego uwaam, e publicznie stawiane w ostatnim czasie uwagi pod adresem Zarzdu i Prezesa NBP, do ktych w dalszej czci mojej wypowiedzi odnios si szczegowo, s po pierwsze nieuzasadnione, po drugie naganianie ich nie suy reputacji i stabilnoci banku centralnego. Wysoka Komisjo! Dla mnie - jako Prezesa Narodowego Banku Polskiego, transparentny i klarowny spos komunikowania o dziaalnoci Narodowego Banku Polskiego jest szczegnie wany, jednak powinien on przebiega w spos gwarantujcy przestrzeganie niezalenoci banku centralnego. W zwizku z powyszym moja wypowied bdzie ograniczona artykuem 227 Konstytucji, artykuem 108 Traktatu ustanawiajcego Wspnot Europejsk oraz innymi przepisami. Realizujc, artyku 22 ustp 2 ustawy o NBP pragn przedstawi Wysokiej Komisji informacj o dziaalnoci Narodowego Banku Polskiego. Najwyszym ustawowym dobrem dla Narodowego Banku Polskiego jest zapewnienie stabilnoci systemu finansowego kraju. W zwizku z tym, po likwidacji Generalnego Inspektoratu Nadzoru Bankowego w trosce o utrzymanie bezpieczestwa systemu finansowego, w wyniku wspnej inicjatywy mojej, Ministra Finans a take Przewodniczcego Komisji Nadzoru Finansowego, pod koniec grudnia 2007 r. powoany zosta Komitet Stabilnoci Finansowej. Dodam, e o powoanie Komitetu w drodze ustawowej zabiegaem ju w kwietniu 2007 r. W skad Komitetu weszli Minister Finans, Prezes Narodowego Banku Polskiego, Przewodniczcy Komisji Nadzoru Finansowego. Jego celem jest zapewnie efektywnej wsppracy na rzecz wspierania stabilnoci krajowego systemu safety net, w tym koordynacji dziaa i wymiany informacji sucej ochronie oraz wspieraniu stabilnoci finansowej w kraju. W tym miejscu chc Pastwa zapewni, e mimo zaburze na midzynarodowych rynkach finansowych, system bankowy w Polsce jest stabilny i bezpieczny. Zarzdzanie rezerwami w Narodowym Banku Polskim przebiega w spos coraz bardziej efektywny. Dochodowo rezerw walutowych wyznaczona w walucie poszczegnych instrument inwestycyjnych bya w 2007 r. najwysza od czterech lat i wyniosa ok. 5,4% podczas gdy rednia dochodowo rezerw w latach 2004-2006 ksztatowaa si na poziomie 2,8%. Na dochodowo rezerw w ostatnich latach korzystnie oddziayway decyzje o zmianie struktury walutowej podejmowane przez Zarzd NBP na rok 2006 oraz 2007. W 2007 roku przyjto dugoterminow strategi zarzdzania rezerwami dewizowymi majc na celu maksymalizacj dochodowoci rezerw dewizowych NBP w dugim okresie, w ramach akceptowanego poziomu ryzyka finansowego i przy uwzgldnieniu ogranicze wynikajcych z misji NBP. W minionym roku w Narodowym Banku Polskim podjte zostay rnie inicjatywy organizacyjne, majce na celu unowoczenienie banku wzorem najlepiej zarzdzanych bank centralnych w Europie. Midzy innymi, poprzez utworzenie Instytutu Ekonomicznego, rozpocz si proces wzmacniania funkcji analityczno-badawczych banku. Stworzenie Instytutu Ekonomicznego zwikszy moliwoci rozwoju bada ekonomicznych i przyczyni si do wzrostu jakoci analiz opracowywanych w NBP. Zainicjowane zostay rwnie prace nad stworzeniem kompleksowego Raportu o przystpieniu Polski do strefy euro. Raport jest przygotowywany we wsppracy ze wszystkimi stronami zainteresowanymi zagadnieniem euro: instytucjami administracji publicznej, wiatem nauki, instytucjami finansowymi, zwizkami pracodawc i pracownik. W poowie roku gotowy bdzie wstpny szkic tego dokumentu, natomiast peny raport bdzie gotowy w grudniu 2008 roku. Pozwoliem sobie przekaza na rce Pana Przewodniczcego konspekt tego raportu, liczc na cenny wkad Wysokiej Komisji w ulepszenie tego raportu. Ze wzgldu na ostatnie wydarzenia zwizane z faktem zoenia rezygnacji przez I Zastpc Prezesa NBP oraz bezprecedensowym upublicznieniem przez niego powod tej decyzji, a take w obliczu sformuowania przez niego szeregu faszywych zarzut, w trosce o reputacj Narodowego Banku Polskiego jak i kolegialnego organu, jakim jest Zarzd NBP, czuj si w obowizku przedstawi Wysokiej Komisji rzeteln informacj w przedmiotowej sprawie. Wr informacji prasowych, opartych na bdnej ocenie stanu faktycznego i prawnego, pojawiy si m.in. zarzuty dotyczce podejmowanych decyzji w Narodowym Banku Polskim i ich niezgodnoci z ustaw o NBP. Pragn przypomnie, e zgodnie z artykuem 6 ustawy o Narodowym Banku Polskim organami Narodowego Banku Polskiego s Prezes, Rada Polityki Pieninej oraz Zarzd. Organy te maj odrbne, okrelone ustaw, zakresy kompetencji. Kompetencje Zarzdu okrela artyku 17 ustawy o NBP, zgodnie z ktym dziaalnoci NBP kieruje Zarzd. W ramach swoich kompetencji Zarzd posiada uprawnienia do okrelenia m.in. zakresu dziaalnoci oraz organizacji wewntrznej Centrali NBP i pozostaych jednostek organizacyjnych NBP, o czym stanowi artyku 7 ustp 2 punkt 2 ustawy oraz zasad organizacji i podziau zada w NBP, o czym stanowi artyku 17 ustp 4 punkt 9 ustawy o NBP. I wanie na podstawie tych przepisw w dniu 26 stycznia 2001 roku, za kadencji poprzedniego Prezesa NBP, prof. Leszka Balcerowicza, Zarzd NBP uchwali zmiany do Regulaminu Organizacyjnego NBP. Zmiany te polegay na wprowadzeniu po raz pierwszy instytucji upowanionego przez Prezesa NBP czonka Zarzdu sprawujcego w imieniu Prezesa biecy nadz nad podporzdkowanymi Prezesowi departamentami i jednostkami organizacyjnymi. W oparciu o t zmian, czesny Prezes NBP prof. Leszek Balcerowicz upowani czonka Zarzdu do biecego nadzoru nad wskazanymi departamentami. Poprawno i zgodno tego rozwizania z ustaw o NBP, nie bya nigdy przez nikogo zakwestionowana. Take corocznie odbywajca si kontrola Najwyszej Izby Kontroli, nie podwaya waciwoci tych rozwiza. Zatem, podjta przez obecny Zarzd w dniu 5 listopada 2007, zmiana do Regulaminu Organizacyjnego NBP bya jedynie kontynuacj rozwiza funkcjonujcych ju od 6 lat w Narodowym Banku Polskim! Moliwo podjcia przez Zarzd takiej decyzji w wietle uregulowa ustawy o NBP potwierdzi nie tylko Departament Prawny NBP ale rnie wybitni eksperci z dziedziny prawa: prof. dr hab. Piotr Winczorek, dr hab. Tomasz Stawecki oraz prof. dr hab. Adam Jaroszyski. Pragn rwnie z caym przekonaniem potwierdzi, e w Narodowym Banku Polskim to Wiceprezesi kieruj wyznaczonymi przez Prezesa dziaami pracy. Biorc odpowiedzialno za nadzorowany dzia pracy posiadaj rnie realny wpyw na jego ksztat. Ponadto, Wiceprezesi sprawuj liczne funkcje Przewodniczcych Komisji dziaajcych w Narodowym Banku Polskim jak i reprezentuj Narodowy Bank Polski na zewntrz. I tak, Pierwszy Zastpca Prezesa NBP  pan Jerzy Pruski nadzorujc departamenty: Statystyki, Systemu Finansowego oraz Zesp Zarzdzania Ryzykiem Operacyjnym, jednoczenie peni funkcj Przewodniczcego Komisji ds. Zarzdzania Ryzykiem, Komisji ds. Wprowadzenia Banknot i Monet Euro, Komisji Budetowej oraz Komitetu ds. Rynk Walutowych. Jest rnie staym przedstawicielem NBP w Komitecie Rady Ministr, a take czonkiem midzy innymi Rady Rozwoju Rynku Finansowego czy Komitetu Zarzdzania Dugiem Publicznym. Ponadto do dnia 31 grudnia 2007 roku, by przedstawicielem NBP w Komisji Nadzoru Bankowego. Wiceprezes NBP, Krzysztof Rybiski, odpowiedzialny jest za Departament Operacji Zagranicznych, Departament Zarzdzania Ryzykiem Finansowym oraz Departament Systemu Patniczego. Reprezentuje NBP w Komisji Nadzoru Finansowego, przewodniczy Komitetowi Inwestycyjnemu Rezerw Dewizowych, Radzie Systemu Patniczego. Ponadto, nadzoruje wiele istotnych projekt w NBP np. wdroenie systemu emisyjno-skarbcowego oraz przygotowania NBP do przystpienia do platformy Target2. Wyznaczanie, przez Prezesa NBP dzia pracy Wiceprezesom, jest dziaaniem podejmowanym na podstawie artykuu 10 ustp 3 ustawy o NBP, kty to, wanie Prezesa NBP upowania do tych czynnoci. Naley podkreli, i powysze uprawnienie jest samodzieln kompetencj Prezesa NBP. Tylko od decyzji Prezesa NBP zaley, kte dziay pracy wyznaczy do kierowania wiceprezesom. Ustawa o NBP nie ustala bowiem adnych granic w okreleniu przedmiotowego zakresu dzia pracy, kte powierza si Wiceprezesom na podstawie artykuu 10 ustp 3 ustawy. Prezesowi NBP pozostawiona jest w tym zakresie swoboda o charakterze dyskrecjonalnym, to znaczy swoboda decyzji. Stanowisko to rnie potwierdzaj przywoane przeze mnie wczeniej opinie prawne profesor Pana Piotra Winczorka i Pana Tomasza Staweckiego, cytuj: adne standardy ani wytyczne nie s w ustawie zawarte, kte mogyby stanowi spos ograniczenia uznaniowej decyzji Prezesa NBP. Decyzja w tym zakresie nie jest te wyznaczona poprzez przepisy proceduralne. () Koniec cytatu. Warto przypomnie, e we wrzeniu 2005 roku, w okresie sprawowania funkcji przez poprzedniego Prezesa NBP, podj on decyzj o znaczcej zmianie dzia pracy Wiceprezes, wyczajc spod kierowania jednego z Wiceprezes kluczowe departamenty analityczne, przenoszc je w obszar odpowiedzialnoci Prezesa, w ktym pozostaj do dzisiaj. Wczas, nikt nie kwestionowa podstaw prawnych tej decyzji, ani I Zastpca Prezesa NBP ani Wiceprezes ani nie staa si ona przedmiotem publicznej dyskusji, jak to ma miejsce obecnie. Poniewa jak wczeniej wspomniaem Artyku 10 ust. 3 daje Prezesowi swobod w tym zakresie. Odnoszc si do kwestii dotyczcych sprawowania przez czonk Zarzdu jednoczenie stanowiska dyrektora departamentu wyjaniam, e forma ta budzia wtpliwoci w wietle zapis artykuu 18 ustawy o Narodowym Banku Polskim, micym wprost, e Czonek Zarzdu nie moe zajmowaadnej innej funkcji. Analiza najlepszych praktyk adu korporacyjnego, rekomendowanych przez midzynarodowe instytucje finansowe, jak rnie jednoznaczna krytyczna opinia wiatowego eksperta w dziedzinie zarzdzania bankami centralnymi, Pana Johna Mendzeli oraz opinie prawne, kte s w posiadaniu NBP, potwierdziy uomno prawn stosowanej uprzednio konstrukcji zarzdczej. Zarzd przyj rozwizanie majce na celu popraw zarzdzania Bankiem oraz wiksze upodmiotowienie czonk Zarzdu w celu zapewnienia prawidowego funkcjonowania Zarzdu i Banku. Pragn te podkreli, e adne z przyjtych przez Zarzd rozwiza nie ograniczao uprawnie czonk Zarzdu do udziau w procesie decyzyjnym oraz przedstawiania swoich opinii, co potwierdziy wypowiedzi czonk Zarzdu. Na zakoczenie, jeszcze raz pragn podzikowa Wysokiej Komisji za moliwo przyblienia specyfiki funkcjonowania banku centralnego jakim jest Narodowy Bank Polski oraz poinformowania o osigniciach Banku oraz o problemach, kte si pojawiy po roku penienia przeze mnie funkcji Prezesa NBP. Fakt upublicznienia wewntrznych spraw Banku oraz podwaanie jego wiarygodnoci przez formuowanie nieuzasadnionych stwierdze, budzi m wielki niepok o reputacj i presti Narodowego Banku Polskiego. Dlatego te ze zrozumieniem podchodz do troski Wysokiej Komisji o funkcjonowanie NBP. Utwierdza mnie to rnie w przekonaniu, o wspnej odpowiedzialnoci za losy polskiego zotego. Pragn jednak przypomnie o orzeczeniu Trybunau Konstytucyjnego wydanego w imieniu Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej w dniu 22 wrzenia 2006 r., kte odnosi si do kwestii niezalenoci Narodowego Banku Polskiego, cytuj Prezes NBP nie ma immunitetu w zakresie swojej dziaalnoci, ale to nie oznacza, e dopuszczalne jest tworzenie sytuacji wywoujcej wraenie nacisku politycznego. Takie wraenie mogoby mie negatywny efekt mrocy dla realizacji ustawowych kompetencji organ niezalenych od parlamentu koniec cytatu. Ten cytat mona potraktowa jako podsumowanie zaistniaej w ostatnich dniach sytuacji. Jedn z kompetencji Zarzdu wynikajc z artykuu 7 ustp 2 punkt 2 ustawy o NBP, jest okrelanie zasad organizacji i podziau zada w NBP a wkraczanie innych organ jak rnie instytucji zewntrznych w tego rodzaju decyzje, sprowadzaoby si do bezpodstawnej ingerencji w wewntrzne sprawy NBP, a to oznaczaoby naruszenie niezalenoci banku centralnego zagwarantowanej Konstytucj i regulacjami prawa wspnotowego w tym w szczegnoci artykuem 108 Traktatu ustanawiajcego Wspnot Europejsk. Wysoka Komisja pozwoli, e przypomn, e przepis ten stanowi i cytuj w wykonywaniu uprawnie oraz zada i obowizk, kte zostay im powierzone niniejszym Traktatem i Statutem Europejskiego Systemu Bank Centralnych, ani Europejski Bank Centralny ani krajowy bank centralny, ani czonek ktegokolwiek z ich organ decyzyjnych nie zwraca si o instrukcje ani ich nie przyjmuje od instytucji czy organ wspnotowych, rzd Pastw Czonkowskich, ani jakiegokolwiek innego organu. Instytucje i organy wspnotowe, jak rnie rzdy Pastw Czonkowskich zobowizuj si szanowa t zasad i nie dy do wywierania wpywu na czonk organ decyzyjnych EBC lub krajowych bank centralnych przy wykonywaniu ich zada koniec cytatu. Dziaania Zarzdu NBP i Prezesa NBP zostay ocenione jako zgodne z prawem w opiniach Departamentu Prawnego jak i w opiniach wybitnych autorytet z zakresu nauk prawnych. Dbajc o silny pienidz i stabilny system finansowy, a take o wysok jako wykonywanych zada, Narodowy Bank Polski wnosi istotny i trway wkad w systematyczn popraw warunk ycia naszego spoeczestwa. Zadanie to moe by prowadzone tylko w warunkach spokoju i braku nacisk politycznych, co gwarantuje Narodowemu Bankowi Polskiemu Konstytucja Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej. Dlatego, Wysoka Komisjo, Panie Posanki, Panowie Posowie, wobec trudnej sytuacji na midzynarodowych rynkach finansowych, niezwykle wane jest dla mnie poczucie, e odpowiedzialno za stabilno polskiego pienidza jest nasz wspn trosk. Dzikuj za uwag.

Title: Report on the implementation of monetary policy assumptions in 2007
text: Transforming Sawomir Skrzypek, President of the Nbp, in the Sejm debate on "Reports on the implementation of monetary policy assumptions in 2007" and "Reports on the activities of the National Bank of Poland in 2007" Admission Mr. Marshal, High Sejm! Today I have the honour to present to the House a summary of the activities of the National Bank of Poland in 2007. It covers the issues included in the documents submitted to the High Chamber: "Report on the implementation of monetary policy assumptions" and "Report on the activities of the National Bank of Poland". Standing before the House a year ago, I was pleased with what actions I would give the highest priority in 2007. I announced the strengthening of the analytical and scientific role of the NBP, the creation of a report on the impact of adopting the euro, the improvement of the transparency of monetary policy and actions to increase the stability of the financial system. Today I would like to present to you the results of these activities:  In order to strengthen the role of the NBP as an important analytical centre in our region, I have established the Working Committee for Scientific Research at the NBP. It analysed ways organization of research in the best central banks in the world. The result of this work was a change in the organization of the ANALYTICAL AND DELIVERY DIVISION of the NBP. Research activities are very important for the effectiveness of the central bank and its prestige and reputation as an institution of public trust. In order to improve the process of conducting economic research, the Economic Institute was established at the National Bank of Poland. We strive to make it the leading analytical and research centre in Central and Eastern Europe. This goal was also served by the establishment of the Scientific Council at the NBP Management Board. It consists of eminent economists from the largest economic universities in Poland. The main task of the Council is to give opinions on the plan of scientific research carried out and commissioned by the National Bank of Polish.  In May 2007, I set up the Office for Integration into the Euro Area, whose main task is to prepare a comprehensive report on the impact of adopting a common currency. Joining the euro area will be one of the most important economic decisions Polish in the twenty-first century. The National bank of Polish makes every effort to ensure that this decision is made in conditions of full information. This results in a very open and transparent process of creating a report. We consult extensively with the social partners. Representatives of trade unions, entrepreneurs and bankers participate in the the process of creating a report at the working, expert level and during official debates. In 2007, we planned and commissioned prominent economists to do about 100 scientific studies on the effects of adopting a great currency. Their results are currently presented at open seminars at the NBP. I think that all these activities serve to establish new standards of public debate in Poland. The publication of the Report is planned for December 2008.  Last year, the transparency of the Monetary Policy Council's activities also increased significantly. Since May 2007, the NBP has been presenting a description of the discussions from the decision-making meetings of the Monetary Policy Council. The publication, the so-called minutes, is an accepted practice of leading central banks. It strengthens the transparency of monetary policy and improves the central bank's communication with financial markets, businesses and the public.  As you will remember, from April to the end of 2007 I took measures to strengthen the Polish financial stability system. They aimed at:  First of all  postponement of the Liquidation of the General Inspectorate of Banking Supervision operating in the NBP. I was guided by the conviction that such action would serve the stability of our financial system well in a situation of serious disturbances in the global financial markets. I would like to strongly emphasize that the current institutional model of the organisation of banking supervision has been assessed positively, zarno in Poland and abroad. A well-functioning superstructure significantly contributed to the fact that Poland avoided financial turmoil. In recent years, such problems have affected many countries, as well as in our region. According to data from the Czech Central Bank, the crisis in the Czech Republic cost 24% of GDP. The loss of GDP in Hungary as a result of the crisis is estimated at 10%. These costs in these countries were borne by the state budget as well as by all the taxpayers. I would like to emphasize that the NBP intends to continue to play an active role in activities aimed at maintaining the financial stability of our country.  The second important element of the statutory amendments I proposed at that time was the establishment of a Financial Stability Committee by statutory means, which was a forum for exchanging views and coordinating actions in the event of a financial crisis. It was to include representatives of the institutions of the so-called financial safety net, i.e. the NBP, the Ministry of Finance and the Polish Financial Supervision Authority. Unfortunately, the proposed bill to amend the act in both cases did not even become the subject of a parliamentary debate. In view of the impossibility of solving the problem in a statutory manner, I accepted with satisfaction and full openness the proposal of the Minister of Finance to establish the Financial Stability Committee by agreement. With the active role of the National Bank of Poland, within a few days the content of the "Agreement between President of the National Bank of Poland, Minister of Finance and Chairman of the Polish Financial Supervision Authority on cooperation in supporting the stability of the national financial system". This agreement was signed on 21 December 2007. Monetary policy Mr Speaker, High House, I will now turn to the most important task of the NBP, which is to take care of the stability of Polish money. In line with its monetary policy strategy, since 2004 the National Bank of Polish has been aiming to maintain inflation at 2.5% with a symmetrical range of deviations 1 percentage point. In 2007, the average annual price index of consumer goods and services was 2.5%, and thus was at the level of the NBP's inflation target. In the following months, the annual price index of consumer goods and services increased gradually. For most of last year, it was within the range of deviations from the NBP's inflation target. At the end of last year, however, it crossed the limit of deviations from the target, reaching the level of 4.0% in December. The gradual increase in inflation in 2007 was mainly due to the increase in the dynamics of food and fuel prices, as evidenced by the increase in food and fuel prices. a significant difference between CPI inflation and the net core inflation rate. This was the result of the action of m.in the supply conditions in the country, which were unfavourable for some agricultural products, the increase in prices on international agri-food markets, as well as a significant increase in oil prices on world markets in the fourth quarter. 2007 The last two factors were only partially amortized by the zloty's appreciation against the dollar. In addition, the increase in the prices of tobacco products, resulting from the government's increase in the excise duty rate on these products, to a level higher than that resulting from the European Union regulations, contributed to raising the general level of consumer prices in Poland. It should be underlined that these factors, which largely accounted for the increase in inflation in the second half of 2007, were outside the direct impact of national monetary policy. At the same time, inflation growth was also driven by high growth in 2007, accompanied by strong employment growth and falling unemployment. These factors contributed to the acceleration of wage growth, but the fact that it shifted to prices to a limited extent, m.in thanks to the good financial situation of enterprises and the relatively small and stable share of the cost of labor in the total cost of production. Thank you, Mr Marshal. High Sejm! In 2007, macroeconomic shocks in the economy were an important element of the conditions in which monetary policy was conducted. World. The first of these was the turmoil on the international financial markets, which has occurred since August 2007, initiated on the subprime mortgage market in the United States. These disturbances were a significant surprise. This is evidenced by the revisions of the projected economic growth made during 2007 by the most significant institutions such as the European Commission, the International Monetary Fund and the world's leading investment banks. The second shock was a significant increase in the prices of energy raw materials, especially oil, and the prices of food and agricultural raw materials on world markets, most of which led the country to a marked acceleration of inflation at the end of 2007 in most of the country. As part of these internal and external conditions, as well as as part of the effort to maintain inflation at the level of the inflation target in the horizon of the monetary policy impact, in 2007 the Monetary Policy Council increased the NBP interest rates four times  in April, June, August and November, each time by 25 basis points. Over the next 6 months of this year, there was an increase of another 100 basis points. It is worth emphasizing that since the beginning of 2007, in no EU country has the scale of percentage increases been greater than in Poland. Only a few countries in the world have had a more restrictive monetary policy than ours. These include m.in Ghana, where rates have been raised by 450 basis points to 17% since the beginning of last year, South Africa  where the increase has fallen 300 basis points to 12%, and Chile and Norway  where rates have been raised by 225 basis points to 7.25% and 5.75%, respectively. What are the effects of the NBP policy? Currently, inflation as measured by the consumer price index is 4.6% and the harmonized index by the so-called HICP is 4.3%. This is, next to Slovakia, the lowest score in the region of Central and Eastern Europe. The current level of inflation is largely due to the increase in food and energy prices. This is evidenced by the level of core inflation excluding these dwh price categories. It is currently 2.1%. The average annual consumer price index in Poland in 2007 was at the level of the inflation target of 2.5%. In the Czech Republic, where interest rates have been raised from a lower initial level in a similar range as in Poland, inflation is 6.7%. This happened despite the fact that the tightening of monetary policy began earlier than in our country. Although a slowdown is expected in the coming quarters, economic growth remains relatively fast. Taking this into account, it can be concluded that the actions taken by the Monetary Policy Council in 2007 were effective. An even greater and faster tightening of monetary policy would increase the risk of an excessive slowdown in economic growth. In conclusion, I would like to remind you once again that the National Bank of Polish is obliged to maintain price stability. Seeks to reduce inflation to the target of 2.5% over the medium term. At the same time, I will try to continue to conduct monetary policy in such a way as to support the maintenance of balanced economic growth. The tightening of monetary policy initiated in April 2007 should contribute to bringing inflation back to its target. However, due to the nature of the price shocks, which are predominantly responsible for the increase in inflation, the reduction to the target will be gradual. It should be borne in mind that in order to ensure price stability in the longer term, it is necessary to introduce public finance reform and other structural reforms. It is also desirable to coordinate the monetary and fiscal policies, the so-called policy mix, in order to reduce the potential cost of maintaining low inflation. Bank Supervision Mr Speaker, Honourable Members, The statutory tasks of the NBP in this respect include, m.in, shaping the conditions necessary for the development of the banking system. This issue was particularly a major challenge in 2007 and resulted from a combination of the following circumstances:  Firstly, at the beginning of 2008, the New Capital Agreement entered into force in Poland and in other European Union countries. raising the standards of the bank's capital equipment. The implementation of these regulations in commercial banks as well as on the supervisor's side is a complicated process.  Secondly, in mid-2007, serious turmoil began on the global financial markets related to the crisis in the subprime credit sector in the United States. The need to carry out, in these structural conditions, changes in the functioning of Polish banking supervision raised my serious doubts. However, as I mentioned at the outset, my efforts to suspend the liquidation of the General Inspectorate of Banking Supervision by law and to establish the Financial Stability Committee did not meet with the recognition of the Sejm. As a consequence, on the basis of the provisions of the Act on financial market supervision, a very significant change in the institutional organization of banking supervision has been made. Since 1 January 2008, tasks in this area have been performed by the Polish Financial Supervision Authority. On the other hand, the General Inspectorate of Banking Supervision was liquidated, which functioned in the central bank. The National Bank of Polish has made every effort to ensure that these changes do not interfere with the operational activities of banking supervision. We have provided all the resources necessary to perform supervisory tasks, including movable assets, human resources and the GINB archive. We also defined the rules for the operation of the IT system and the scope and mode of information exchange between the PFSA and the NBP. The National bank Polish handed over the banking sector to the Polish Financial Supervision Authority in very good condition. This is evidenced by the sector's highest profits in years: the gross financial result amounted to PLN 16.8 billion and was 30% higher in terms of 2006. In 2007, the banking sector had historically the lowest share of non-performing loans in assets. It was 5.2% compared to 11% in 2006, while the solvency ratio was at a safe level of 11.9%, compared to the required 8%. The commercial banking sector did not experience a liquidity problem in 2007. The average level of excess liquidity of the banking sector averaged PLN 19.5 billion per year. However, there was a gradual deterioration in the deposit-to-credit ratio. In the middle of last year, the value of loans in the banking sector exceeded the value of deposits accepted. This situation is increasingly forcing banks to use market financing, including foreign financing. This is a common phenomenon in countries experiencing convergence. However, a gradual change in the funding structure requires both the bank and the supervisor to focus more on liquidity management. With this in mind, the General Inspectorate of Banking Supervision has developed standards for liquidity risk management. These regulations, adopted by the Banking Supervision Commission in March last year, have been in force since 2008. Management of foreign exchange reserves As part of the work on establishing a strategic benchmark for 2007 r. The NBP Management Board decided to reduce the share of the US dollar in the currency structure of reserves and began investing in the Australian dollar. Last year, the return on provisions expressed in currency was the highest in recent years, reaching 5.4%. However, due to the appreciation of the zloty against reserve currencies, the profitability of provisions expressed in PLN was negative and amounted to minus 6.8%. In recent years, there has been a significant increase in the value of official reserve assets. In 2007 alone, official reserve assets increased in dollar terms by 35.6% to USD 65.7 billion, in euro  by 21.3% to EUR 44.7 billion, and in zloty  by 13.4% to PLN 160.1 billion. The increase in the value of reserve assets was primarily the result of: the inflow of funds from the European Union, changes in exchange rate relations and income from investing reserves. In 2007, the currency structure of the reserves managed by the NBP included four currencies: the US dollar, the euro, the pound sterling and the Australian dollar. In order to increase the profitability of foreign exchange reserves, the National Bank of Polish diversifies the currency structure of reserves. Decisions to change it are made on the basis of analyses of macroeconomic prospects in the world, forecasts of the development of the situation on international financial markets and the result of optimization analysis. The diversification of the currency structure carried out in 2006-2007 had a positive impact on the profitability of provisions. As a result, in the years 2006-2007, the profitability calculated in Polish zlotys was over 110 basis points higher than the profitability that would have been obtained if the currency structure of 2005 had been in force. In 2007, work was completed on a long-term strategy for the management of foreign exchange reserves for the years 2007-2012 assuming further diversification of currencies and the financial instrument. Result on investment activities Despite unfavorable exchange rate conditions, the activity of managing foreign exchange reserves showed positive effects. The ogny result on investment activities amounted to PLN 6 billion 142 million and increased by 42.9% in 2006. The increase in the profitability of reserves was related, among other things, to the higher return on investments for most reserve currencies. In addition, the rate of return achieved was positively influenced by the increase in the prices of government bonds, which over the course of 2007 was recorded in the USA and the UK. As a result, the profitability of reserves exceeded the average, official interest rate for reserve currencies. In 2007, we observed a strong appreciation of the zloty against foreign currencies. For example, the zloty strengthened by 16.2% against the US dollar, by 14.7% against the British pound and by 6.5% against the euro. The zloty's appreciation trend has continued to date. The effect of the appreciation was to generate unrealized rnice from the exchange rate valuation in the amount of PLN 15 billion 14 million. Until now, these losses were offset by a revaluation account, created in 1991. The earlier long-term depreciation of the zloty meant that the increase in the zloty value of the bank's assets was recorded on the side of its liabilities, as an increase in the revaluation account. In turn, the strengthening of the zloty, causing a decrease in the zloty's asset valuation, lowered the level of this account. This was a buffer protecting the NBP against the negative effects of the zloty's appreciation. The appreciation of the Polish currency, which has been maintained since 2004, led to the complete exhaustion of the revaluation account, which in 2003 exceeded PLN 32 billion. At the end of 2006, it reached the level of PLN 331 million and was completely exhausted in March 2007. It should be noted that in the years 2004-2006 the appreciation effects of the zloty were fully offset by revenues from the solution. a revaluation account. If it were not for this account, the NBP would have incurred losses since 2004 They would amount to: in 2004  PLN 18 billion and PLN 96 million, in 2005  PLN 2 billion 350 million, in 2006  PLN 1 billion 257 million. In 2007, as a result of the appreciation of the zloty, the NBP recorded a loss of PLN 12 billion 427 million. The main elements influencing such a financial result were the aforementioned unrealized rnice from the exchange rate valuation at the level of PLN 15 billion 14 million. It should be emphasized, however, that the remaining components of the NBP's profit and loss account were realized in a positive amount of PLN 2 billion 587 million. It should be noted here that the central banks of other countries whose currency is subject to appreciation also show a loss. For example, in the Czech Republic in 2007 it was 37.5 billion Czech crowns, in Slovakia  19.4 billion Slovak crowns, and in Hungary  16.5 billion forints. Taking into account the current economic and legal conditions, at the moment nbp may allocate funds from the reserve fund to cover the loss, which amounts to PLN 970 million. The method of covering the loss provided for in the current provisions of the Act on the National Bank of Poland in the event of a continuing trend of zloty appreciation in subsequent years may result in a long-term negative financial result. One should also take into account its deepening. In connection with the above, an amendment to the NBP Act would be a possible solution, which would allow the Bank's loss to be covered by profits from subsequent years. Since the NBP does not have a legislative initiative, I turned to the Minister of Finance with a request for cooperation in the development of optimal solutions regarding the method and principles of covering the central bank's loss. The aim of the great activities will be to develop appropriate amendments to the NBP Act. Payment system As part of the clearing service, at the end of 2007 NBP ran two payment systems based on gross settlement: SORBNET for high-value settlements in PLN and SORBNET  EURO for high-value settlements in the common European currency. In the SORBNET system, nbp settled 1 million 454 thousand transactions in PLN, i.e. 14.5% more than in 2006. In turn, in the SORBNET  EURO system, it completed 138 thousand transactions, i.e. 38% more than in 2006. In 2007, as part of its activities for the payment system, nbp focused on preparations for participation in the TARGET2 system and the Single Euro Payments Area, i.e. SEPA. The pan-European euro clearing system, TARGET2, has been in operation since 19 November 2007 and has completely replaced the previous TARGET system since 19 May 2008. The NBP joined the system on 19 May 2008. On that date, three commercial banks also became direct participants in TARGET2, and 24 banks obtained the status of indirect participant through NBP. The entry of NBP and Polish banks into the TARGET2 system means, m.in: faster payment processing time, the possibility of reducing the fees incurred by the customer for transfers in euros, expanding the potential number of customers and enabling banks to compete on the European market on equal terms. Emission activities High Sejm, The National Bank of Poland has the exclusive, statutory right to issue a monetary sign of the Republic of Poland. At the end of 2007, almost 86 billion zlotys of ready-made money were in circulation. Economic growth in Poland caused an increase in the demand for ready-made money, which increased by PLN 10 billion, i.e. by 14% in 2006. The total cost of purchasing cash money by the NBP last year amounted to PLN 261 million. In order to disseminate knowledge about the culture and history of Polish, NBP issues collector coins. In 2007, 11 were introduced new topic. These were, among others: the 75th anniversary of breaking the Enigma code, or the 750th anniversary of the location of Krakow. Previously started series were also continued, such as: -Polish Podrnicy and Researchers -History of the Golden; -Monuments of Material Culture in Poland; At the same time, in each month of 2007, one topic from the historical cities in Poland series was broadcast. Collector coins issued by the NBP, due to their interesting subject matter and interesting design, are very popular. As a curiosity, I can give the example of a coin Konrad Korzeniowski  Joseph Conrad, who took second place at the Second International Coin Competition in the category "Original technology". It should be added that the NBP does not have to subsidize this form of cultural and educational activity. In 2007, this activity brought PLN 15.7 million in profit. (in 2006 it was PLN 14.5 million) Educational activities NBP attaches great importance to educational activities. It is an important element of the NBP's mission as an institution, which supports the economic development of Polish. It includes activities aimed at popularizing economic education, understanding the principles of functioning of the market economy and promoting entrepreneurship. As part of its educational activities, over 600,000 students were covered by NBP programs in 2007. We organized training for 3,000 teachers. More than 70,000 students took part in the investment game "From class to cash". In addition to its own educational projects, the National Bank of Polish through the Commission for Promotion and Education supports the initiatives of libraries, foundations and associations. In 2007, we allocated over PLN 2 million for external funding of the project and the scholarship program. The NBP has funded over 1100 bridge scholarships aimed at carving out educational opportunities for young people from rural areas. In order to reach the largest number of recipients with educational knowledge, NBP also supports media projects. The average listenership of the episode of the educational radionovela "Motel w p drogi" amounted to 1 million listeners. It is also worth mentioning the EDUCATIONAL PORTAL OF THE NBP. The number of visits to this website increased in 2007 by 1 million 200 thousand, reaching the level of over 6 million users. The NBP Open Days were also a great success, during which about 50,000 visitors visited the Bank. Handling of budget accounts As part of the bank account service, in 2007 the NBP served 3,765 account holders and maintained 16,537 accounts. Work continued on the introduction of new rules for handling the state budget. The capabilities of the Electronic Banking system have been extended by introducing the transmission of payment orders in foreign currencies, other than the euro, directed to accounts held outside the NBP, and the system of placing orders in the emergency mode has been simplified. In 2007, amendments were also prepared to facilitate the management of funds accumulated in bank accounts. Internal activities Mr. Speaker, High House, In November 2007, amendments were made to the NBP Organizational Regulations specifying the competences of the Nbp President. This was the result of a resolution adopted by the NBP Management Board in 2001 concerning the m.in authorizing designated members of the Management Board to exercise, on behalf of the President of NBP, ongoing supervision over departments and organizational units subordinated to the President of NBP. The introduced changes are aimed at improving management, especially in the situation of adapting the practice to statutory requirements related to the prohibition of combining the position of a member of the NBP Management Board with other positions. At the end of 2007, the members of the Management Board ceased to be the director of the department. At this point, I would like to emphasize once again that the amendment to the Organizational Regulations undertaken by the current Management Board on November 5, 2007 was only a continuation of the solutions that have been functioning for 6 years in the National Bank of Poland! The possibility of making such a decision by the Management Board in the light of the provisions of the NBP Act was confirmed not only by the Legal Department, but also by eminent experts in the field of law: Prof. Piotr Winczorek, Dr. Tomasz Stawecki and Prof. Adam Jaroszyski. The Monetary Policy Council adopted a different position on this matter. High Sejm, The NBP, headed by me, attaches great importance to limiting the cost of the bank's operation. Administrative costs, despite the increase in the prices of goods and services, were 10 million lower than in the previous year, which is a decrease of 2.9%. At the same time, the rationalization of employment in NBP district branches continued. Total employment decreased by 57 FTEs. On the other hand, the remuneration fund increased by 4.5%, which, however, is significantly lower dynamics than in the commercial banking sector, where wages increased by 10% last year. When it comes to the salaries of a NBP employee in specialized positions, they still differ from the level in commercial banks, which may cause an increase in personnel risk. Investments In 2007, a total of PLN 71 million 147 thousand was allocated for the implementation of investment tasks. This appropriation was intended, m.in, for: - ICT tasks in the amount of PLN 44 million, -cash and treasury activity in the amount of PLN 3 million 498 thousand, - security investments in the amount of PLN 3 million 120 thousand. In 2007, the construction of the treasury and the Central Computer Center in Zegrze was not completed. The NBP presents its views on the Committee of the Council of Ministers, in the Sejm and in all other possible forums. Our voice is not sufficiently taken into account. In the face of today's problem, all over the world, more than ever, cooperation between the most important institutions responsible for the image of the economy is needed. The exclusion of monetary issues from the vortex of current politics is one of the most important achievements of the political system of the last few decades. Being aware of the need for such a separation of competences, however, I believe that it should be a 'friendly chapter'. The independence of the central bank is of great value, but effective communication with government administrations and parliament is also essential. That is why I do not cease to strive to ensure that the spirit of cooperation and dialogue replaces the atmosphere of confrontation. This is reflected in the numerous proposals and solutions put forward in my official correspondence. In the absence of a response, I made a public appeal to the government for cooperation. Today I renew my appeal. I believe that the achievement of the most important goal of the parliament, the government and the central bank will proceed faster in an atmosphere of understanding and cooperation. This goal, although pursued within the framework of various constitutional obligations, is common to all of us. It is the prosperity of all Poles. Thank you for your attention.
