Ten cel, cho realizowany w ramach rnych obowizk konstytucyjnych, jest dla nas wszystkich wspny. Jest nim dobrobyt wszystkich Polak. Dzikuj Pastwu za uwag.

Title: Speech in the Sejm
text: Transformation of the President of the NBP in the Sejm d0 21 July 2010 Mr Speaker, Honourable Members, For the first time, as the President of the National Bank of Poland and the Chairman of the Monetary Policy Council, I have the honour to present to the House two documents: report on the implementation of the monetary policy assumptions for 2009 and Report on the activities of the National Bank of Poland in 2009. As in the previous year, in 2009 the NBP's activity was determined by macroeconomic conditions. The years 2007-2009 were a period of global crisis. The collapse of the global financial system has spilled over into the real world, turning into the deepest recession of the world economy since the Great Depression. The effects of the crisis are primarily a strong decline in global demand, a collapse in world trade and a significant increase in price volatility on global financial markets. Despite the unprecedented scale of the anti-crisis programme, the recovery of the global economy was weak, as evidenced by such phenomena as the lack of improvement in the situation on the labour market and the persistently elevated and volatile risk aversion on financial markets. The crisis has hit the economies of Central and Eastern Europe very hard. The main channels through which the global economic crisis spread to the country of this region were financial markets and foreign trade. As a result, the scale of capital outflows and depreciation of national currencies was one of the largest emerging economies in our region. The recovery of the global economy is largely based on emerging economies, including mainly Asian countries, but the sustainability of the recovery also depends to a large extent on the success of the current anti-crisis policy. There are still risk factors for the return of recession. These include: First, the risk of insolvency of the country. The example of Iceland and the country of southern Europe, especially Greece, showed the scale of possible economic destabilization and dysfunction of financial markets. Secondly, the volatility of expectations and investor sentiment remains high, which determines the direction of capital flow and affects price fluctuations in the financial market. On the one hand, the "risk appetite" and capital inflow to emerging markets, including Polish, are systematically returning, on the other hand, any negative information from the macroeconomic environment of the country causes capital flight to the so-called "safe havens", which remain debt securities of the United States, Germany or Switzerland, as well as gold. Thirdly, trade, consumption and investment imbalances persist, resulting in strong disparities in trade balances across countries and regions. Fourthly, the regulation of the financial market and the supervision of them have proved to be ineffective, in particular the banking sector. These regulations have not been able to prevent a global financial crisis, and the process of creating new solutions is still unfinished. Fifth, uncertainty about the financial health of some global financial institutions persists, resulting in limited mutual trust and market activity. To rebuild this trust, stress tests of their solvency are to be carried out and the result of these studies are to be made public. In the face of the problem of the world economy, the need to limit inflation has fallen into the background, which is currently at a low level. However, it should not be forgotten that the primary objective of the central bank is to maintain a stable price level, and the loss of control over inflation raises the risk of anchoring at a higher level of inflation expectations, making inflation persistent and more difficult to control. The National bank Polish in its activities was part of the anti-crisis strategy. We must emphasize that the global financial and economic crisis has also contributed to a serious slowdown in the growth rate in Poland to 1.8 per cent in 2009 from 5.1 per cent in 2008. The recession in the main trading partners caused a decrease in foreign demand for goods and services produced in Poland and significantly reduced the investment of enterprises. The latter is also associated with a strong slowdown in credit growth, which has affected the real economy. The economic slowdown was accompanied by a deterioration in the situation on the labour market, as well as a deterioration in the situation of the public finance sector. At the same time, the significant depreciation of the zloty exchange rate contributed to an increase in the price competitiveness of Polish products abroad and a decrease in the competitiveness of imported production on the domestic market. As a result, in 2009 the contribution of net exports to GDP growth was positive, becoming the most important factor of economic growth in Poland. The Polish economy has shown relatively high resilience to the global crisis, which was due to m.in less dependence of the domestic economic situation on foreign demand than in other countries, a lower share of credit in real finance and relatively strong domestic demand. The sustainability of economic growth was also strengthened by appropriate macroeconomic policies before and during the crisis, including monetary policies aimed at maintaining medium-term price stability under the floating exchange rate regime. Polish banking system has also shown great resilience to the global crisis, as a result of which the Polish taxpayer did not have to allocate any funds to save the solvency of the bank in Poland. This was due to the effectiveness of supervision, as well as banking regulations based on the experience of the Polish market during our difficult 20-year economic transformation. High Chamber! Referring to the monetary policy decisions taken last year, it should be emphasized that in view of the strong decline in economic activity in the world and in Poland, which had an impact on reducing inflationary pressures d0 in the first half of 2009 the Monetary Policy Council continued the easing of monetary policy started at the end of 2008. Last year, the interest rates of the National Bank of Poland were reduced four times - in January, February, March and June, by a total of 150 basis points, reaching the lowest level since the beginning of the economic transformation. The NBP reference rate was reduced from 6% in November 2008 to 3.5% in June 2009. The decrease in percentage stps resulted in a decrease in most market percentages. WIBOR 3M, which is the reference rate for a significant part of the credit agreements, decreased from 6.7 per cent in November 2008 to 4.2 per cent in August 2009, i.e. by 2.5 percentage points, and in the following months it was in the range of 4.1-4.2 per cent. This supported a decline in interest rates on loans already taken out and newly granted to households and non-financial corporations, which at the end of 2009 was lower by 1.2 percentage points and 2.2 percentage points respectively than at the end of 2008. Such a formation of percentages by the NBP also had a positive impact on the conditions of the bank's operation, as it reduced their financing costs. In the second half of 2009, in view of the gradually improving economic situation and at the same time the persistence of significant uncertainty regarding the sustainability of the recovery in growth abroad, the Council kept interest rates unchanged. As a result of declining inflationary pressures, the annual consumer price index decreased by 0.7 percentage points compared to 2008 and reached 3.5%, reaching the level of the national bank of Poland's inflation target of 2.5%. On the development of the inflation rate in 2009 Factors outside the direct impact of national monetary policy were significantly affected, in particular increases in administered prices and excise duty rates. In addition, the level of inflation was affected by a significant depreciation of the zloty in the period July 2008 - February 2009 resulting from an increase in risk aversion on global financial markets and the outflow of foreign capital from emerging markets. In the first half of this year, inflation fell to the level of the National Bank of Poland's target and has been close to it since March. It is worth recalling here that in accordance with the monetary policy strategy implemented by the NBP, the objective of monetary policy is to maintain inflation at the assumed level in the medium term. It should be noted that since the start of the implementation of the continuous inflation target at the level of 2.5 percent, i.e. since 2004, the average growth rate of consumer prices in Poland amounted to 2.8 percent, which was close to the assumed target. This confirms the effectiveness of the implementation of the constitutional task of the National Bank of Poland, which is to ensure price stability. An important role in the design of such a monetary policy is played by analytical and research work carried out at the National Bank of Poland, which is one of the most important elements supporting decisions taken by the Monetary Policy Council and the NBP Management Board. The NBP's research activity last year concerned in particular the monetary transmission mechanism and its recent disturbances, caused to a large extent by the financial crisis. The results of this work were also used to build and improve econometric model tools for the development of macroeconomic forecasts. An important element of analytical and research activity is the dissemination of its result. This is achieved through scientific publications prepared by a NBP employee, of which there were over 100 last year, as well as seminars and scientific conferences organized at the NBP, as well as presentations of NBP research achievements at domestic and foreign conferences and research cooperation with domestic and foreign research centers and international organizations. Let us add that in 2009 the National Bank of Polish organized 4 international conferences and 13 open scientific seminars. Thank you, Mr Marshal. (PL) Honourable Members, Turning to the issue of the stability of the Polish financial system, I would like to remind you that the National Bank of Polish started 2009 in a new legal environment. On 13 December 2008, the Act on the Financial Stability Committee entered into force, also amending the Act on the National Bank of Poland. As a result, measures for the stability of the national financial system were included in the central bank's list of tasks. The Act imposed on the NBP the obligation to analyse the stability of the national financial system. It should be emphasized that in practice the National Bank of Polish has already carried out the above tasks. This was due to the fact that financial stability is a prerequisite for the conduct of an effective monetary policy aimed at maintaining price stability as well as the smooth functioning of the payment system. According to the Act on the Financial Stability Committee, its meetings should be held at least once every year. In 2009, due to the continuing crisis situation on the global financial markets and the need to closely observe the current situation in Poland, seven meetings of the Committee were held. The NBP participated in all meetings, repeatedly initiating their convening in order to discuss issues important for maintaining financial stability. The change in the legal conditions of the NBP's operation coincided with new challenges resulting from the financial and economic crisis in the world. Therefore, at that time, the NBP's main action was to mitigate the effect of the hypocritical functioning of the interbank market and reduce the bank's liquidity risk by creating the possibility for them to obtain liquidity in PLN and foreign currencies. To this end, the National Bank of Polish in October 2008 introduced the so-called Confidence Package, under which it began to apply a much wider set of monetary policy instruments than in previous years. As part of this Package, the Central Bank shall: - firstly, it started regular operations providing the banking sector with PLN liquidity in the form of 3 and 6 month repo transactions. The average level of these operations in 2009 amounted to nearly PLN 11.5 billion. - secondly, it started to provide the bank with foreign exchange liquidity in the form of foreign exchange swap transactions, which gave banks the opportunity to hedge the exchange rate risk associated with the granting of foreign currency loans. Banks showed the greatest interest in transactions on the Swiss franc/zloty pair. Due to the progressive calming of the situation on the currency market, the demand for such operations gradually decreased over the year and the last operation on which banks reported demand was carried out on October 26 last year. The average level of foreign exchange swap operations in 2009 amounted to PLN 1,076 million. - thirdly, the list of eligible assets as collateral for the Bank's refinancing operations was extended and the principle of the so-called netting of collateral, i.e. the use of the same collateral in renewed repo transactions, was introduced, which effectively expanded the Bank's ability to obtain liquidity from the NBP. In addition, the Bank took additional measures to permanently increase the bank's liquidity, which consisted of: -early redemption, in January 2009, of 10-year NBP bonds, as a result of which the banking sector was provided with liquid funds worth PLN 8 billion 221 million, and -reduction of the reserve requirement rate by 0.5 percentage points (from 3.5% to 3.0%) from 30 June 2009, which in turn contributed PLN 3.3 billion to the banking sector. Due to the fact that the normalization of the situation on the interbank market was quite slow, the National Bank of Polish replaced the interbank market to some extent. Such an action, of an extraordinary and transitional nature, was successful, because none of the banks operating in Poland got into problems related to the lack of liquidity, nor was it necessary to use other financial assistance instruments. The central bank's operations have significantly reduced the bank's liquidity risk and gradually restored confidence in the interbank market. In order to reduce liquidity risk in the banking sector, the NBP also took measures to make it easier for banks to finance lending. These actions were related to the fact that the effects of the crisis on global financial markets began to move to the sphere of the real Polish economy. There was a decline in the value of loans granted by banks to enterprises, which threatened to weaken economic growth. Therefore, the National Bank of Polish proposed and initiated the conclusion of the so-called Pact for the Development of Lending. As part of this activity, the National Bank of Polish organized a series of meetings with banks, with the participation of representatives of the Ministry of Finance and the Polish Financial Supervision Authority. As a result, the most important barriers to credit growth in banks were identified, which d0 apart from increased credit risk d0 included: relatively low level of capital and liquidity risk. As a result of intensive efforts of the PFSA and the NBP, banks retained the profits generated in 2008, which eased the capital barrier, and the liquidity risk was reduced thanks to nbp operations supplying the banking sector with liquid funds. The global financial crisis has shown the need for changes in the organisation of the financial safety net, including in the European Union. An expression of these activities is the construction of a new supervisory architecture in Europe, within which the European Systemic Risk Board and the European Banking Authority are to be established. In the area of macroprudential supervision (this is the first Systemic Risk Board), the new solutions assign a special role to the European Central Bank and national central banks, which affects a new look at their role in monitoring and supervising the financial market, and banking in particular. The NBP conducted its own analyses in this respect, which resulted in the report Institutional organization of financial supervision in the European Union countries published in 2009. It presents the main directions of changes in the institutional organisation of financial market supervision in the Union, taking into account the role of central banks in this process. I believe that Poland should also draw conclusions from the recent financial crisis and strengthen the national financial safety net and consider expanding the role of the NBP in this area. Thank you, Mr Marshal. High Chamber! Last year was important for the National Bank of Poland when it comes to preparing Polish for full membership in the Economic and Monetary Union. The NBP conducted active work related to preparations for the adoption of the euro by Poland. In January 2009, the National Bank of Poland established a Commission for the introduction of the euro, whose chairman is the Management Board Plenipotentiary for the introduction of the euro. Task forces have been set up: for the development of the Strategy for the inclusion of the zloty in the ERM II mechanism and for the selection of the scenario for the introduction of euro banknotes and coins in Poland. In February 2009, the Report on the full participation of the Republic of Poland in the third stage of Economic and Monetary Union was published, in which the cost-benefit analysis of the Polish's accession to the euro area was carried out. Throughout 2009, further analyses were carried out on the convergence of the real and nominal Polish economy with the euro area economies, cyclical monitoring of the situation in the euro area and the resulting implications for the Polish and studies on the level of the gdp rate. Last year, the National Bank of Polish cooperated with the government in creating the final provisions of the Ministerial Council Regulation on the establishment of the National Coordination Committee for the Euro, the Coordination Council and the Interinstitutional Working Group on Preparations for the Introduction of the Euro by the Republic of Poland. According to this regulation, the NBP Management Board Plenipotentiary for the introduction of the euro acts as the co-chairman of the National Coordination Committee and the Coordination Council. In turn, NBP representatives are part of seven out of eight working teams. Thank you, Mr Marshal. High Chamber! An important area of activity of the National Bank of Poland is the management of foreign exchange reserves. The size of foreign exchange reserves is one of the key factors influencing the perception by a participant of the financial market of the security of investments in the currency of a given country. The high level of foreign exchange reserves strengthens the country's financial credibility, which reduces the risk of uncontrolled outflow of foreign capital and at the same time reduces the cost of foreign loans taken out by the state as well as private economic entities. These aspects are particularly relevant during periods of heightened volatility in global financial markets and high risk aversion. Foreign exchange reserves can also be used to ensure the effective implementation of exchange rate policy. When managing foreign exchange reserves, the National Bank of Polish is guided by three basic principles: ensuring a high level of security of invested funds, maintaining the necessary degree of their liquidity and striving to obtain the highest possible profitability of reserves. The NBP's reserve assets increased in 2009 by db11.1 billion to db55.2 billion. The increase in the size of reserves was influenced by a positive balance of external flows, the additional allocation of SDRs carried out by the International Monetary Fund, as well as the doch from the investment of reserves. In dollar terms, official reserve assets increased by 17.4 billion to 79.6 billion US dollars. As for the current data, the state of reserve assets at the end of June this year amounted to 70.0 billion euros, or 85.5 billion dollars. In the process of managing foreign exchange reserves, NBP invests in typical instruments used by central banks. The dominant part of foreign exchange reserves are American, German and British government securities, characterized by the highest degree of security and liquidity. The National Bank Polish also invests in non-governmental securities, including those issued by international institutions and government agencies. A small part of the reserves is held in deposits deposited in reputable banks. In 2009, the National Bank of Polish obtained a high, comparable to the previous year, doch from investment activities related to the management of foreign exchange reserves. It amounted to PLN 6.1 billion, without taking into account exchange rate ratios. At the same time, the result on the realized exchange rate losses amounted to PLN 15.1 billion, which allowed to increase the provision for exchange rate risk in the amount of PLN 14.2 billion. The rate of return of foreign exchange reserves in 2009 calculated in PLN amounted to 1.9 per cent, while the cumulative rate of return of reserves, calculated since the introduction of the long-term strategy for the management of foreign exchange reserves, i.e. for the years 2008-2009, amounted to 23.8 per cent. Thank you, Mr Marshal. (PL) Honourable Members, In recent years, the issue of the NBP's financial result has been the subject of a discussion d0 not devoid of emotions. It also made arguments and expressed opinions that could be interpreted as influencing the independence of the central bank, which could weaken the stability of our financial system. At this point, I would like to clearly point out that the NBP's financial result is determined on the basis of the accounting principles in force at the Bank, adopted by the Monetary Policy Council in 2003, which are consistent with the accounting standards used in the European Central Bank System and the principles adopted by the MPC in 2006 for creating and resolving a provision to cover the risk of changes in the zloty's exchange rate to foreign currencies, in line with the rules applicable to the ECB and other Eurosystem central banks. The financial result of the National Bank of Poland for 2009 amounted to PLN 4 billion 165 million 554 thousand, while in 2008 it was at zero level. The increase in the NBP's financial result last year was primarily the result of the Bank generating higher revenue from foreign exchange reserve transactions than in 2008, constituting about 90 per cent of the Bank's assets. Due to the volatility of the exchange rate and their unpredictability, the value of these assets is subject to high fluctuations, and the Bank is exposed to losses due to exchange rate losses. An example of such a phenomenon was the year 2007, in which, as a result of the appreciation of the zloty, the NBP recorded a loss of PLN 12.4 billion. In accordance with the NBP Act, the Bank may cover this loss in subsequent years only with a reserve fund, created from a 5% profit write-off. In 2008, the reserve fund was only sufficient to cover 8% of this loss. In order to limit the negative impact of exchange rate fluctuations on the Bank's financial result, in 2008 and 2009 the NBP took steps to build a capital buffer in the form of a provision for the risk of changes in the zloty's exchange rate to foreign currencies. This provision was created in the amount of PLN 16.4 billion. The creation of this provision was necessary because it cannot be ruled out that the trend of appreciation of the zloty will return, negatively affecting the Financial Result of the Bank. Let us remember that the Polish legal order does not provide for the coverage of losses or recapitalization of the Bank from external foals. And a central bank without real capital cannot properly perform its constitutional and statutory functions, I can give here the example of the central bank of Iceland in recent years. High Sejm! The year 2009 was another year of intensive contact between the National Bank of Poland and its partners on the international arena. The Governor of the Bank attended the meetings of the ECB's General Council and representatives of the Bank participated in the work of twelve committees and around 50 working groups and the task force of the European System of Central Bank. In 2009 the European System of Central Bank discussed, m.in, issues related to the establishment of the European Systemic Risk Board. Given the role of the central bank in the planned structure of macroprudential supervision, the National Bank Polish actively participated in the work carried out at national and EU level, presenting its position on the future shape of the supervisory system. NBP representatives also took part in informal meetings of the ECOFIN Council and in the work of the auxiliary body of the Council of the European Union devoted primarily to the causes and consequences of the financial and economic crisis. In order to strengthen the position of the Polish in the World Bank Group, representatives of the National Bank of Poland actively participated in the ongoing work in 2009 on the second phase of the reform of the World Bank. Representing Poland in the World Bank Group, NBP representatives participated in the Meetings of the Governor's Councils of the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund, which took place in April and October last year. In cooperation with the IMF, representatives of the National Bank of Poland participated in the work in 2009, which resulted in the IMF making available Polish amount of SDRs 13 billion 690 million under the Flexible Credit Line from May 2009. The possibility of using the Flexible Credit Line to increase the level of NBP foreign exchange reserves was conducive to lowering the risk premium on the financial markets, contributing to strengthening the positive image of our economy and helped to effectively counteract the crisis. This year, in view of the still uncertain prospects for the global economy and the situation on the financial markets, the Minister of Finance and the President of the NBP submitted a request to extend the IMF Flexible Credit Line for the next year, which application was positively considered by the Fund on 2 July this year. In the area of foreign activity, the National Bank of Polish cooperated with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, the Bank for International Settlement in Basel and the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development. This cooperation included an ongoing analysis of the state of the world economy and the financial system and the search for solutions to counteract the zarn crisis at the global and national level. On the initiative of the NBP, in December 2009 a meeting of representatives of Polish in international financial institutions was organized, with representatives of the Ministry of Finance, the Ministry of Economy, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the NBP. These meetings are held periodically once a year and are a forum for the exchange of information and serve to improve the coordination of positions Polish presented in the forum of international financial institutions. Last year's meeting was an opportunity to discuss issues such as the reform of the World Bank and the IMF and to prepare the Polish for the Presidency of the Council of the European Union in the second half of next year. In addition, last year the National Bank of Polish continued its cooperation with the National Bank of Slovakia. This cooperation focused on analysing the experience of preparing for the introduction of the euro and on observing the first experiences of the introduction of the euro. A strategic element of international cooperation for the National Bank of Poland is technical and training assistance offered to central banks of countries in transition. The Management Board of the National Bank of Poland adopted a new Strategy for the development of technical assistance provided by the NBP for the years 2010-2012. The strategy treats as a priority d0 as a recipient of NBP technical assistance d0 the central banks of the countries covered by the Eastern Partnership program and the countries belonging to our constituent body in bretton Woods organizations. The National Polish Bank has also expanded the circle of recipients of technical assistance offered to central banks of the country in transition to include central banks of some African countries and South and Central America, i.e. Chile, Egypt, Kenya, Morocco, Paraguay and Tunisia. So far, 28 central banks have benefited from NBP technical assistance. In 2009, the process of negotiations and preparations related to the twinning project implemented by the National Bank of Polish in cooperation with the Deutsche Bundesbank for the National Bank of Ukraine was completed. On 10 February this year, a twinning agreement was signed between the beneficiary of the aid, the members of the consortium and the European Commission and the project was launched. In October 2009, the Cooperation Agreement was signed between the National Bank of Poland and the National Bank of the Republic of Belarus, which defines the principles and forms of cooperation between the two banks in the field of technical assistance. This is the fifth agreement concluded by the NBP with central banks in recent years. So far, similar agreements have been signed with the central banks of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Mongolia and Vietnam. Thank you, Mr Marshal. (PL) Honourable Members, In 2009, the National bank Polish actively contributed to the further development of the Polish payment system. The work related to the preparation of the Program for the development of cashless trade in Poland for the years 2010-2013 has been completed, which was referred to the Ministry of Finance in order to adopt it as a government program to cover all institutions involved in this issue. The programme contains a number of objectives and actions to promote cashless transactions for the benefit of society, the economy and public and local government institutions, including reducing the cost of future entry of Polish into the euro area. 2009 was another year of introduction of the Single Euro Payments Area, the so-called SEPA. The aim of the project is to create uniform standards and rules for making cashless payments throughout the SEPA area, i.e. within the European Economic Area. The National bank Polish plays an important role in handling the pan-European SEPA Credit Transfer, acting as a settlement bank for those domestic commercial banks that want to use the NBP intermediation (currently 12 banks use this service). High Chamber! Another important area of activity of the central bank is the issuance activity. Pursuant to the Act, the National Bank of Poland has the exclusive right to issue a cash sign of the Republic of Poland. By ensuring the security of settlement liquidity by providing all nominal values of banknotes and coins of general circulation and the quality of cash circulation, the National Bank of Polish contributes to the maintenance of monetary stability. As at the end of last year, PLN 100.3 billion was in circulation. This means a decrease in the value of cash money by PLN 1.8 billion in terms of money by 2008. The total cost of the purchase of cash money by the National Bank of Polish last year amounted to PLN 429.4 million. Last year, the National Bank of Polish was working on changing the system for selling collector coins. New rules for the sale and distribution of these values through the online auction sales system have been prepared, which have been in force since January this year. To carry out this task, the Kolekcjoner web application was created and introduced. The basic assumption of the new sales system was to introduce a transparent, market-based mechanism for the allocation of collector values and to eliminate the price preference of numismatic companies. The new system of selling collector's values is supported by the established Foundation of the National Bank of Poland. Thank you, Mr Marshal. (PL) Honourable Members, The year 2009 was also a period of significant changes in the area of management of the National Bank of Poland. In October 2008, the Management Board of the Bank adopted the Management Strategy of the National Bank of Poland for the years 2009-2012. The strategy is the basis for the introduction of a modern strategic management system, enabling to increase the efficiency of the Bank's operations. This is achieved m.in the introduction of an integrated process and design approach, as well as strategic controlling. Last year, the reorganization of the NBP district branch, which began in September 2008, was completed. There was a reduction in employment resulting m.in from the standardization of activities in the field of accounting, administration, security and IT as well as outsourcing of selected services. In 2009, the average employment at the NBP amounted to 3,770 FTEs in the whole country and was lower than in the previous year by 199 FTEs, i.e. by 5.0%. Salary costs in 2009, together with provisions and mark-ups on salaries, were higher than in 2008 by 4.1%. High Chamber! The National Bank of Polish is very actively involved in shaping the economic awareness of Polish society. A key role in this context is played by our educational activities. Its aim is to increase public awareness of the functioning of the market economy, and the tools are economic education at the school level, as well as the implementation of numerous educational programs. In the latter, one can distinguish programmes addressed through the media to a wide audience, as well as profiled programmes addressed to specific social groups at risk of so-called financial exclusion. NBP's educational projects are addressed to a wide range of addressees, i.e. school environments, academic environments and adult learning, religious and rural environments and the general public. In 2009 The NBP Management Board adopted the Strategy of Economic Education of the National Bank of Poland for the years 2010-2012, the essence of which is to increase public awareness of the role and mission of the central bank in economic life. There is the NBP Economic Education Portal, which publishes articles explaining economic mechanisms and contains e-learning courses and multimedia presentations. The Financial Observer portal devoted to current economic events in Poland and in the world has also been launched. It is the only one on our market and one of the few portals in the world presenting the debate of the most respected economists. It is of particular importance for the NBP to perform its information and educational function. It is also a source of information and exchange of views for representatives of the media, the leader of opinion and teaching and academic circles. In addition, in order to support activities promoting the development of economic sciences and education, at the end of 2009 the Foundation of the National Bank of Poland was established. High Sejm! In conclusion, I would like to remind you that in 2009 the process of transferring ownership to the NBP of the collection of paintings, which were originally owned by Art B, was successfully completed. The collection of works of art obtained by the National Bank of Polish as a result of settlements: 34 paintings, graphics and drawings and 11 objects of artistic handicrafts, worth PLN 6 million 325 thousand, was planned to be made available to the public. We have signed an agreement with the National Museum in Warsaw to deposit all works of art. The museum organized an exhibition at which they were presented to a wide audience. Thank you, Mr Marshal. (PL) Honourable Members, The activities of the National Bank of Poland in 2009 were managed by the tragically deceased President of the Nbp d0 S?awomir Stanis?aw Skrzypek. It was a particularly difficult year for the economy, in which the world struggled with the deepest economic collapse since the thirties of the last century. In these difficult conditions, the National Bank of Polish fulfilled its role in a proper manner. From the very beginning, he actively counteracted the growth of crisis phenomena and led activities aimed at maintaining the stability of the financial system in Poland. It has pre-emptively initiated measures to limit the negative effects of the global economic crisis, and responsible monetary policy has contributed to sustaining positive economic growth, which no other country in the European Union has been able to do. The tragic death of the NBP President S?awomir Skrzypek, who was also the Chairman of the NBP Management Board and the Chairman of the Monetary Policy Council, could have destabilised the NBP body, causing disruptions in the functioning of the financial market in Poland. At this point, I would like to emphasize that the competent, dignified and responsible behavior of the member of the NBP Management Board led by the First Deputy President Mr. Piotr Wiesio?ek and a member of the Monetary Policy Council after the tragedy, as well as the decisions taken in this difficult and legally complicated situation, ensured the continuity of the central bank's operations and saved our financial system from destabilization. As the President of the National Bank of Poland, I declare that the central bank will continue to work for the value of Polish money and a stable price level while supporting the Government's economic policy. The National Bank Polish remains ready to take additional measures to preserve the country's financial stability and maintain economic growth. The condition for success is full cooperation and coordination of the NBP's monetary and economic policy of the Government and the supervisory policy of the Polish Financial Supervision Authority. I hope that the cooperation between the National Bank of Poland and all centers of economic power will continue to develop, and its effect will be sustainable, balanced and high economic growth taking place in conditions of low inflation, which will allow to effectively catch up with the most economically developed countries in the world. I assure you that the National Bank of Polish will pursue this goal with full determination.
