Wyni on 6,1 mld zotych, bez uwzgldnienia rnic kursowych. Jednoczenie wynik z tytuu zrealizowanych rnic kursowych wyni 15,1 mld zotych, co pozwolio na powikszenie rezerwy na ryzyko kursowe w wysokoci 14,2 mld zotych. Stopa zwrotu rezerw walutowych w 2009 r. wyliczona w zotych wyniosa 1,9 proc., natomiast skumulowana stopa zwrotu rezerw, wyliczana od momentu wprowadzenia dugoterminowej strategii zarzdzania rezerwami dewizowymi, czyli za lata 2008-2009, wyniosa 23,8 proc. Panie Marszaku! Panie Posanki! Panowie Posowie! W ostatnich latach wok kwestii wyniku finansowego NBP toczya si  nie pozbawiona emocji  dyskusja. Paday w niej take argumenty i wypowiadano opinie, kte mona byo interpretowa jako pry wpywania na niezaleno banku centralnego, co mogoby osabia stabilno naszego systemu finansowego. W tym miejscu chc wyranie zaznaczy, e wynik finansowy NBP jest ustalany na podstawie obowizujcych w Banku zasad rachunkowoci, przyjtych przez Rad Polityki Pieninej w roku 2003, kte s zgodne ze standardami rachunkowoci stosowanymi w Europejskim Systemie Bank Centralnych oraz przyjtych przez RPP w 2006 r. zasad tworzenia i rozwizywania rezerwy na pokrycie ryzyka zmian kursu zotego do walut obcych, zbienych z zasadami stosowanymi w EBC oraz innych bankach centralnych Eurosystemu. Wynik finansowy Narodowego Banku Polskiego za rok 2009 wyni 4 miliardy 165 milion 554 tysicy zotych, podczas gdy w 2008 r. uksztatowa si na poziomie zerowym. Wzrost wyniku finansowego NBP w ubiegym roku by przede wszystkim skutkiem wypracowania przez Bank wyszych ni w roku 2008 przychod z transakcji rezerwami dewizowymi, stanowicymi okoo 90 proc. aktyw Banku. Z powodu zmiennoci kurs walutowych i ich nieprzewidywalnoci warto tych aktyw podlega wysokim wahaniom, a Bank naraony jest na straty z tytuu rnic kursowych. Przykadem takiego zjawiska by rok 2007, w ktym na skutek aprecjacji zotego NBP odnotowa strat w wysokoci 12,4 mld z. Zgodnie z ustaw o NBP, strat t Bank moe pokrywa w kolejnych latach jedynie funduszem rezerwowym, tworzonym z 5-procentowego odpisu z zysku. W 2008 r. fundusz rezerwowy wystarczy jedynie na pokrycie 8 proc. wspomnianej straty. W celu ograniczenia negatywnego wpywu waha kurs walutowych na wynik finansowy Banku, w latach 2008 i 2009 NBP podj dziaania zmierzajce do zbudowania bufora zabezpieczajcego w postaci rezerwy na ryzyko zmian kursu zotego do walut obcych. Rezerwa ta zostaa utworzona w kwocie 16,4 mld z. Utworzenie tej rezerwy byo konieczne, poniewa nie mona wykluczy, e trend aprecjacji zotego powri, wpywajc negatywnie na wynik finansowy Banku. Pamitajmy przy tym, e polski porzdek prawny nie przewiduje pokrycia strat czy dokapitalizowania Banku ze re zewntrznych. A bank centralny bez realnego kapitau nie moe prawidowo wykonywa swoich konstytucyjnych i ustawowych funkcji, mog tutaj poda przykad banku centralnego Islandii z ostatnich lat. Wysoki Sejmie! Rok 2009 r. by kolejnym rokiem intensywnych kontakt Narodowego Banku Polskiego z partnerami na arenie midzynarodowej. Prezes Banku bra udzia w posiedzeniach Rady Ognej EBC, a przedstawiciele Banku uczestniczyli w pracach dwunastu komitet oraz okoo 50 rnych grup roboczych i zespo zadaniowych Europejskiego Systemu Bank Centralnych. W 2009 r. przedmiotem obrad gremi Europejskiego Systemu Bank Centralnych byy m.in. kwestie zwizane z powoaniem Europejskiej Rady ds. Ryzyka Systemowego. Biorc pod uwag rol bank centralnych w planowanej strukturze nadzoru makroostronociowego, Narodowy Bank Polski aktywnie uczestniczy w pracach prowadzonych zarno na poziomie krajowym, jak i unijnym, przedstawiajc swoje stanowisko w odniesieniu do przyszego ksztatu systemu nadzoru. Przedstawiciele NBP brali take udzia w nieformalnych posiedzeniach Rady ECOFIN oraz w pracach organ pomocniczych Rady Unii Europejskiej powiconych przede wszystkim przyczynom i konsekwencjom kryzysu finansowego i gospodarczego. Dc do wzmocnienia pozycji Polski w Grupie Banku wiatowego, przedstawiciele Narodowego Banku Polskiego aktywnie uczestniczyli w toczcych si w 2009 r. w pracach nad II faz reformy Banku wiatowego. Reprezentujc Polsk w Grupie Banku wiatowego, przedstawiciele NBP uczestniczyli w Spotkaniach Rad Gubernator Banku wiatowego oraz Midzynarodowego Funduszu Walutowego, kte odbyy si w kwietniu i w padzierniku zeszego roku. W ramach wsppracy z MFW przedstawiciele Narodowego Banku Polskiego w 2009 r. uczestniczyli w pracach, ktych rezultatem byo postawienie przez MFW do dyspozycji Polski kwoty 13 miliard 690 milion SDR w ramach Elastycznej Linii Kredytowej od maja 2009 r. Moliwo ewentualnego wykorzystania Elastycznej Linii Kredytowej w celu zwikszenia poziomu rezerw walutowych NBP, sprzyjao obnieniu premii za ryzyko na rynkach finansowych, przyczyniajc si do wzmocnienia pozytywnego wizerunku naszej gospodarki i pomoga skutecznie przeciwdziaa kryzysowi. W biecym roku, wobec wci niepewnych perspektyw globalnej gospodarki i sytuacji na rynkach finansowych, Minister Finans wspnie z Prezesem NBP wystpili z wnioskiem o przeduenie Elastycznej Linii Kredytowej MFW na nastpny rok, kty to wniosek zosta pozytywnie rozpatrzony przez Fundusz 2 lipca br. Zasady korzystania ze rodk MFW zostay wczeniej uzgodnione pomidzy Zarzdem NBP a Ministrem Finans. W obszarze dziaalnoci zagranicznej Narodowy Bank Polski wsppracowa z Europejskim Bankiem Odbudowy i Rozwoju, Bankiem Rozrachunk Midzynarodowych w Bazylei oraz z Organizacj Wsppracy Gospodarczej i Rozwoju. Wsppraca ta obejmowaa biec analiz stanu gospodarki wiatowej i systemu finansowego oraz poszukiwanie rozwiza przeciwdziaajcych kryzysowi zarno na poziomie globalnym jak i krajowym. Z inicjatywy NBP w grudniu 2009 r. zorganizowano spotkanie przedstawicieli Polski w midzynarodowych instytucjach finansowych, z przedstawicielami Ministerstwa Finans, Ministerstwa Gospodarki, Ministerstwa Spraw Zagranicznych oraz NBP. Spotkania te odbywaj si cyklicznie raz w roku i stanowi forum wymiany informacji oraz su deniu do usprawnienia koordynacji stanowisk Polski prezentowanych na forum midzynarodowych instytucji finansowych. Ubiegoroczne spotkanie byo okazj do dyskusji na temat takich kwestii jak reforma Banku wiatowego i MFW oraz przygotowania Polski do sprawowania prezydencji w Radzie Unii Europejskiej w II poowie przyszego roku. Ponadto w ubiegym roku Narodowy Bank Polski kontynuowa wspprac z Narodowym Bankiem Sowacji. Wsppraca ta koncentrowaa si na analizie dowiadcze zwizanych z przygotowaniami do wprowadzenia euro oraz na obserwacji pierwszych dowiadcze w zwizku z wprowadzeniem euro. Strategicznym dla Narodowego Banku Polskiego elementem wsppracy midzynarodowej jest pomoc techniczna oraz szkoleniowa, oferowana bankom centralnym pastw znajdujcych si w okresie transformacji. Zarzd Narodowego Banku Polskiego przyj now Strategi rozwoju pomocy technicznej udzielanej przez NBP na lata 2010-2012. Strategia traktuje priorytetowo  jako biorc pomocy technicznej NBP  banki centralne pastw objtych programem Partnerstwa Wschodniego oraz pastwa nalece do naszej konstytuanty w organizacjach Bretton Woods. Narodowy Bank Polski rozszerzy take krg odbiorc pomocy technicznej oferowanej bankom centralnym kraj w fazie transformacji o banki centralne niektych pastw Afryki oraz Ameryki Poudniowej i rodkowej, tj. Chile, Egipt, Kenia, Maroko, Paragwaj i Tunezja. Dotychczas z pomocy technicznej NBP skorzystao 28 bank centralnych. W 2009 r. zakoczono proces negocjacji i przygotowa zwizanych z projektem twinningowym realizowanym przez Narodowy Bank Polski we wsppracy z Deutsche Bundesbankiem na rzecz Narodowego Banku Ukrainy. 10 lutego tego roku podpisano umow twinningow pomidzy beneficjentem pomocy, czonkami konsorcjum a Komisj Europejsk i rozpoczto realizacj projektu. W padzierniku 2009 r. podpisano Porozumienie o Wsppracy midzy Narodowym Bankiem Polskim i Narodowym Bankiem Republiki Biaorusi, kte okrela zasady i formy wsppracy pomidzy oboma bankami w zakresie pomocy technicznej. Jest to pite porozumienie zawarte przez NBP z bankami centralnymi w ostatnich latach. Dotychczas podpisano podobne umowy z bankami centralnymi Kazachstanu, Kirgizji, Mongolii i Wietnamu. Panie Marszaku! Panie Posanki! Panowie Posowie! Narodowy Bank Polski w 2009 r aktywnie przyczynia si do dalszego rozwoju polskiego systemu patniczego. Zakoczono prace zwizane z przygotowaniem Programu rozwoju obrotu bezgotkowego w Polsce na lata 2010-2013, kty zosta skierowany do Ministerstwa Finans, w celu przyjcia go jako programu rzdowego, aby obj jego realizacj wszystkie zaangaowane w t problematyk instytucje. Program zawiera szereg cel i dziaa, majcych suy upowszechnianiu obrotu bezgotkowego z korzyci dla spoeczestwa, gospodarki oraz instytucji publicznych i samorzdowych, w tym zmniejszenia koszt przyszego wejcia Polski do strefy euro. Rok 2009 by kolejnym rokiem wprowadzania jednolitego Obszaru Patnoci w Euro, tzw. SEPA. Celem projektu jest stworzenie jednolitych standard i zasad dokonywania patnoci bezgotkowych w caym obszarze SEPA, czyli w ramach Europejskiego Obszaru Gospodarczego. Narodowy Bank Polski odgrywa istotn rol w zakresie obsugi paneuropejskiego polecenia przelewu SEPA Credit Transfer, penic rol Banku rozliczeniowego dla tych krajowych bank komercyjnych, kte chc korzysta z porednictwa NBP (aktualnie z tej usugi korzysta 12 bank). Wysoka Izbo! Kolejnym wanym obszarem dziaalnoci banku centralnego jest dziaalno emisyjna. Na mocy ustawy Narodowemu Bankowi Polskiemu przysuguje wyczne prawo emitowania znak pieninych Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej. Zapewniajc bezpieczestwo pynnoci rozlicze przez dostarczenie do obrotu wszystkich wartoci nominalnych banknot i monet powszechnego obiegu oraz jako obrotu gotkowego, Narodowy Bank Polski przyczynia si do utrzymania stabilnoci monetarnej. Wedug stanu na koniec zeszego roku w obiegu znajdowao si 100,3 mld z. Oznacza to spadek wartoci pienidza gotkowego o 1,8 mld z w pornaniu do 2008 r. czny koszt zakupu przez Narodowy Bank Polski pienidza gotkowego w roku ubiegym wyni 429,4 mln z. W ubiegym roku Narodowy Bank Polski prowadzi prace nad zmian systemu sprzeday monet kolekcjonerskich. Przygotowano nowe zasady sprzeday i dystrybucji tych wartoci za porednictwem internetowego systemu sprzeday aukcyjnej, kte zaczy obowizywa od stycznia tego roku. Do realizacji tego zadania utworzono oraz wprowadzono aplikacj internetow Kolekcjoner. Podstawowym zaoeniem nowego systemu sprzeday byo wprowadzenie transparentnego, opartego na zasadach rynkowych mechanizmu alokacji wartoci kolekcjonerskich oraz wyeliminowanie uprzywilejowania cenowego firm numizmatycznych. Obsug nowego systemu sprzeday wartoci kolekcjonerskich zapewnia powoana Fundacja Narodowego Banku Polskiego. Panie Marszaku! Panie Posanki! Panowie Posowie! Rok 2009 r. by te okresem istotnych zmian w obszarze zarzdzania Narodowym Bankiem Polskim. W padzierniku 2008 r. Zarzd Banku przyj Strategi zarzdzania Narodowym Bankiem Polskim na lata 2009-2012. Strategia stanowi podstaw do wprowadzenia nowoczesnego systemu zarzdzania strategicznego, umoliwiajcego zwikszenie efektywnoci dziaania Banku. Suy temu m.in. wprowadzenie zintegrowanego podejcia procesowego oraz projektowego, a take kontrolingu strategicznego. W ubiegym roku zakoczono zapocztkowan we wrzeniu 2008 r., reorganizacj oddzia okrgowych NBP. Nastpia redukcja zatrudnienia wynikajca m.in. ze standaryzacji czynnoci w zakresie rachunkowoci, administracji, ochrony i informatyki oraz outsourcingu wybranych usug. W 2009 r. przecitne zatrudnienie w NBP wynioso w caym kraju 3 770 etat i byo nisze od zatrudnienia w roku poprzednim o 199 etat, czyli o 5,0 proc. Koszty wynagrodze w roku 2009 wraz z rezerwami i narzutami na wynagrodzenia byy wysze od wykonania w roku 2008 o 4,1 proc. Wysoka Izbo! Narodowy Bank Polski bardzo aktywnie uczestniczy w ksztatowaniu wiadomoci ekonomicznej polskiego spoeczestwa. Kluczowa rola przypada w tym kontekcie naszej dziaalnoci edukacyjnej. Jej celem jest zwikszanie wiadomoci spoecznej dotyczcej funkcjonowania gospodarki rynkowej, a narzdziami ksztacenie ekonomiczne na poziomie szkolnym, jak rnie realizacja licznych program edukacyjnych. Wr tych ostatnich wyrni mona audycje kierowane za porednictwem medi do szerokiego grona odbiorc, jak rnie programy profilowane, adresowane do konkretnych grup spoecznych zagroonych tzw. wykluczeniem finansowym. Projekty edukacyjne NBP kieruje do szerokiego krgu adresat, tj. rodowisk szkolnych, rodowisk akademickich oraz uczcych si os dorosych, rodowisk wyznaniowych, wiejskich oraz ogu spoeczestwa. W 2009 r. Zarzd NBP przyj Strategi edukacji ekonomicznej Narodowego Banku Polskiego na lata 2010-2012, ktej istot jest zwikszanie spoecznej wiadomoci roli i misji banku centralnego w yciu gospodarczym. Funkcjonuje Portal Edukacji Ekonomicznej NBP, publikujcy artykuy objaniajce mechanizmy ekonomiczne oraz zawierajcy kursy e-learningowe i prezentacje multimedialne. Uruchomiony zosta take portal Obserwator Finansowy powicony aktualnym wydarzeniom gospodarczym w Polsce i na wiecie. Jest to jedyny na naszym rynku i jeden z nielicznych na wiecie portali prezentujcych debat najbardziej cenionych ekonomist. Ma szczeglne znaczenie dla penienia przez NBP funkcji informacyjnej oraz edukacyjnej. Jest take rem informacji i wymiany pogld dla przedstawicieli medi, lider opinii oraz rodowisk nauczycielskich i akademickich. Dodatkowo, w celu wspierania dziaa promujcych rozw nauk ekonomicznych i edukacji, pod koniec 2009 r. zostaa utworzona Fundacja Narodowego Banku Polskiego. Wysoki Sejmie! Na zakoczenie pragn przypomnie, e w roku 2009 sukcesem zakoczy si proces przeniesienia wasnoci na rzecz NBP kolekcji obraz, ktre stanowiy pierwotnie wasno firmy Art B. Uzyskana przez Narodowy Bank Polski w wyniku rozlicze kolekcja dzie sztuki: 34 obrazy, grafiki i rysunki oraz 11 przedmiot rkodziea artystycznego, o wartoci 6 mln 325 tys. z zostaa zaplanowana do udostpnienia spoeczestwu. Podpisalimy umow z Muzeum Narodowym w Warszawie o przekazaniu w depozyt wszystkich dzie sztuki. Muzeum zorganizowao wystaw, na ktej zostay one zaprezentowane szerokiemu krgowi odbiorc. Panie Marszaku! Panie Posanki! Panowie Posowie! Dziaalnoci Narodowego Banku Polskiego w 2009 r. kierowa tragicznie zmary Prezes NBP  Sawomir Stanisaw Skrzypek. By to szczegnie trudny dla gospodarki rok, w ktym wiat zmaga si z najgbszym zaamaniem gospodarczym od lat trzydziestych ubiegego wieku. W tych trudnych warunkach Narodowy Bank Polski wypeni swoj rol w spos naleyty. Od samego pocztku aktywnie przeciwdziaa narastaniu zjawisk kryzysowych i prowadzi dziaania na rzecz utrzymania stabilnoci systemu finansowego w Polsce. Wyprzedzajco inicjowa dziaania majce na celu ograniczanie negatywnych skutk globalnego kryzysu gospodarczego, a odpowiedzialna polityka pienina przyczynia si do podtrzymania dodatniego wzrostu gospodarczego, czego nie udao si dokonaadnemu innemu krajowi Unii Europejskiej. Tragiczna mier Prezesa NBP Sawomira Skrzypka penicego jednoczenie funkcj Przewodniczcego Zarzdu NBP oraz Przewodniczcego Rady Polityki Pieninej moga wpyn na destabilizacj organ NBP powodujc zakenia w funkcjonowaniu rynku finansowego w Polsce. W tym miejscu chc podkreli, e kompetentne, godne i odpowiedzialne zachowanie si czonk Zarzdu NBP kierowanego przez Pierwszego Zastpc Prezesa p. Piotra Wiesioka oraz czonk Rady Polityki Pieninej po tragedii, oraz podjte w tej trudnej i skomplikowanej prawnie sytuacji decyzje zapewniy cigo dziaania banku centralnego i uchroniy nasz system finansowy przed destabilizacj. Jako Prezes Narodowego Banku Polskiego deklaruj, e bank centralny bdzie nadal dziaa na rzecz wartoci polskiego pienidza i stabilnego poziomu cen przy jednoczesnym wspieraniu polityki gospodarczej Rzdu. Narodowy Bank Polski pozostaje gotowy do podejmowania dodatkowych dziaa dla zachowania stabilnoci finansowej kraju i utrzymania wzrostu gospodarczego. Warunkiem sukcesu jest pena wsppraca i koordynacja polityki pieninej NBP i gospodarczej Rzdu oraz polityki nadzorczej Komisji Nadzoru Finansowego. Licz na to, e wsppraca midzy Narodowym Bankiem Polskim i wszystkimi orodkami wadzy gospodarczej bdzie si dalej rozwijaa, a jej efektem bdzie dokonujcy si w warunkach niskiej inflacji trway, zrnowaony i na tyle wysoki wzrost gospodarczy, kty pozwoli skutecznie dogania najbardziej rozwinite gospodarczo kraje na wiecie. Zapewniam, e Narodowy Bank Polski bdzie realizowa ten cel z pen determinacj.

Title: Speech in the Sejm
text: Transfiguration of the President of the National Bank of Poland Prof. Marek Belka in the Sejm of the Republic of Poland - 26 July 2011. Mr Speaker, Honourable Members, As the President of the National Bank of Poland and the Chairman of the Monetary Policy Council, I have the honour to submit two documents to the Sejm of the Republic of Poland: "Report on the implementation of the monetary policy assumptions in 2010" and "Report on the activities of the National Bank of Poland in 2010". This is not only the fulfillment of the statutory obligation to present to the Sejm the result of the NBP's action, but also an opportunity to familiarize the High Chamber with the conditions in which the bank and the Polish economy operated last year. Today's deliberations also provide an opportunity to change this year's events affecting the decisions and actions taken by the National Bank of Polish. Thank you, Mr Marshal. Honourable Members, I would like to thank the rapporteur. After a period of significant slowdown in global economic growth between 2008 and 2009, which was a consequence of the crisis in global financial markets, we have been observing a recovery in the global economy since 2010. After the global recession, however, countries are developing at a slow pace, and the economic situation in individual regions is still strongly affected. As far as the economic situation in the most developed countries is concerned, with a few exceptions, it is still impossible to talk about its stability. Economic activity is weak, well below potential, with high unemployment observed. The factors limiting the recovery in the economies of highly developed countries are the high level of household debt, uncertainty about the demand outlook limiting investment and the still unstable situation of the financial sector. The main risks to economic growth are excessive public finance deficits and dramatically high debt levels. This raises concerns not only about the effective implementation of the fiscal consolidation programme, but also, in some cases, about the solvency of these countries. This is particularly the case for Greece, Ireland and Portugal, but Italy and Spain are also increasingly affected by the problem of excessive public debt. Against this background, Germany, Sweden and the Baltic States are doing exceptionally well in Europe, where after a deep recession in 2009, a rapid recovery is currently being observed. In this context, given the close trade ties of Polish and Germany, one can assess the economic prospects of our country with some optimism. On the other hand, the economic situation in the United States is ambiguous, where after a dynamic improvement in the economic situation last year, there was a clear slowdown in GDP and employment growth. The lack of visible improvement in the real estate market, high unemployment and rapidly growing public debt are important risks to economic growth. A reflection of this risk, and at the same time a warning, was the downgrading by Standard & Poor's of the rating outlook for the US government debt from stable to negative. An additional problem is the difficulty of increasing the limit on public debt by the United States Congress. For the most part, the emerging markets, in particular the BRICS countries such as Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, the growth rate is relatively high. This is the result of the high dynamics of exports and the improvement of domestic demand. The dynamics of the global economy are clearly influenced by the effects of natural disasters and the overlapping political and armed conflicts. They have caused an increased demand for energy raw materials and agricultural products, which results in an explosion in the prices of these commodities. Over the past 12 months, food prices have risen by 34%, metals by 40% and agricultural non-food commodities by 46%. The change in the asset management strategy of investment and hedge funds also contributes to the increase in commodity prices. A growing share in their portfolio is held by raw materials, which are an alternative to investing in securities. The increase in commodity and food prices has contributed to a significant acceleration in inflation in emerging markets. For example, at the end of June, inflation in China was 6.4%, in Brazil d0 6.7%, in Turkey d0 7.2%, in India d0 8.8%, in Russia d0 9.4% and in Ukraine d0 11.9%. This initiated the process of tightening the monetary policy of most emerging markets. Poland has shown relatively high resilience to the global financial crisis. Properly conducted macroeconomic policy of the government, central bank and financial supervision caused that Poland was the only country in the European Union to resist the recession, and our financial system remained stable, although there was an obvious weakening of the growth rate in this situation. In 2010, along with the recovery in the global economy, the economic situation in Poland gradually improved. The growth rate supported by increasing consumption and industrial production of enterprises has been steadily increasing: in 2010 it reached 3.8%, and at the end of the first quarter of this year d0 4.4%. There has also been an increase in employment in the corporate sector, although the level of unemployment has not been significantly reduced. In 2010, capital expenditures fell, for the second year in a row. The decline in investment was driven by relatively low capacity utilisation and uncertainty about the demand outlook. Weak investment activity and, at the same time, a good liquidity situation of enterprises were the reasons for the limited demand for bank loans, despite the gradual relaxation of the criteria for granting them. At the end of 2010, there was a decrease in corporate credit debt by about 1%. Recently, this situation has been changing. At the end of June, we see an increase in the value of loans granted to enterprises, especially when it comes to investment loans. This indicates a long-awaited improvement in the investment activity of enterprises. Credit debt structure shows a clear predominance of credit to households over loan to non-financial corporations, even though in 2010 the growth rate of loan to households decreased from around 13% to less than 9% on an annual basis. A positive phenomenon should be considered the clear dominance of the PLN loan in the context of newly granted housing loans. Data from June this year, however, indicate a decrease in the growth rate of housing loans, i.e. krko mwi?c, i.e. the fastest growing segment of the credit market in Poland, but recently we have observed a certain decrease in the growth rate. At the same time, the volume of consumer credit has been falling for several quarters, which I consider a positive thing, because this segment of the credit market was characterized by the lowest quality and the highest percentage of so-called irregular loans. In the first months of 2010, there was a strong inflow of foreign capital to the Polish. It amounted to db12.4 billion in the first quarter and db37.9 billion for the full year 2010. In addition to the obvious positive effects, they were also less desirable, such as a significant appreciation of the zloty. I repeat that we are talking about 2010. On 9 April 2010, the National Bank of Polish intervened in the foreign exchange market. This contributed to stopping the excessive appreciation of the zloty and the tendency to speculate on the Polish currency. The NBP does not rule out intervention in the currency market, but not to defend any level of the zloty exchange rate, but to prevent its excessive fluctuations. High Sejm! I will now turn to the implementation of the most important task of the NBP, which according to the act is to maintain a stable price level while supporting the government's economic policy, as long as it does not limit the basic objective of the NBP. I would like to remind you that the National Bank of Polish conducted monetary policy in accordance with the strategy of direct inflation targeting. Since 2004, this target has been set at 2.5% with a symmetrical deviation range of 1 percentage point wide. At the same time, monetary policy is conducted in such a way as to support the maintenance of balanced economic growth. Four groups of instruments are used to implement monetary policy: interest rates, open market operations, deposit and credit operations and minimum reserves. In 2010, the average annual level of inflation as measured by the consumer price growth index was 2.6%, thus in line with the inflation target. The Monetary Policy Council conducted a mild monetary policy. The reference rate was kept at a historically low level of 3.5%. In our opinion, the correctness of such a policy was confirmed by limited demand pressure, significant uncertainty about the sustainability of the global recovery, and therefore the acceleration of economic growth in the country, as well as the risk of increasing the inflow of speculative capital to emerging economies, including Polish, and the associated risk of excessive fluctuations in the zloty exchange rate. This year, the consumer price growth index has exceeded its inflation target. In June, the inflation level was 4.2%. The acceleration of inflation in Poland, as in other countries, is mainly associated with the occurrence of strong price shocks on the global fuel and food markets. Temporarily, the increase in inflation in Poland was also related to the increase in VAT rates in January this year. All these factors are beyond the direct impact of national monetary policy. It should be emphasized that core inflation, i.e. excluding changes in fuel and food prices, was 2.4% at the end of June and remains under control. However, there is a danger that high fuel and food prices will begin to turn into wage inflation, i.e. they will be perpetuated by higher wage growth than would result from the rate of labour productivity growth. In addition, the high level of current inflation raises the risk of inflation expectations anchoring at an elevated level, which may make it more difficult and costly for the economy as a whole to manage inflation. For these reasons, the Monetary Policy Council has started a monetary policy tightening cycle this year. Interest rates were raised four times: in January, April, May and June, each time by 0.25 percentage points. As a consequence, the reference rate increased from 3.5% to 4.5%. It should be remembered that these decisions affect the economy with a significant delay, and their impact is strongest only after a few quarters. High Sejm! The purpose of changes in monetary policy is to induce specific behaviors of the economic operator. The transmission of these changes to the real sphere takes place through the financial system. Decision-making by the MPC must therefore be supported by research on the real sphere and on the development and stability of the financial system. The National Bank of Polish systematically conducts appropriate analyses and research in this area. The results of the research were used in the current activities of the NBP and to improve the tools used to develop forecasts that are of great importance in decision-making by the Monetary Policy Council. An important element of analytical and research activities is the presentation of their results. This is done through scientific publications of our employees as well as seminars and conferences organized by the NBP. In 2010, 113 publications by a NBP employee appeared in recognized national and international periodicals, of which 9 were on the so-called Philadelphia list. The National bank of Polish organized 3 international conferences and 26 open scientific seminars. We are the publisher of the scientific journal "Bank and Credit", which is a highly valued forum for the exchange of ideas in the field of macroeconomics and finance. Nbp also initiates and moderates discussions on current economic issues via the Financial Observer information portal. In 2010, more than 1200 articles, a blog and a video file on economics were published on it. Their authors are zarno experts from the NBP, as well as from outside the bank. For several years, the Polish banking sector has been dealing with the phenomenon of growing excess liquidity. Its main source is the exchange of funds flowing into Polish from the European Union in the central bank for zlotys In addition, in 2008-2009, excess liquidity increased as a result of the central bank's implementation of its strategy to counteract the adverse effects of the global financial crisis. Currently, the high excess liquidity of the banking sector makes it difficult to achieve the current monetary policy objectives, i.e. maintaining the krko-term market percentages at a level close to the NBP reference rate. The main instrument with which the NBP absorbs the excess liquidity of the banking sector were the basic operations of the open market. They were carried out regularly, once a week, in the form of issuing 7-day NBP cash vouchers. The average value of issues in 2010 amounted to PLN 74.9 billion. In comparison with the previous year, it was higher by PLN 43 billion. This year, the value of the issue has already increased to over PLN 100 billion, which proves that the banking sector remains very high, although recently we have observed its stabilization. By conducting open market operations, nbp strives to ensure that the contractual interest rates of the interbank market are close to the NBP reference rate. In this way, the bank prevents an excessive decrease in market percentages, which by too much increase in the money supply would cause an even greater increase in inflation. In 2010, the one-day interbank market rate, the so-called POLONIA, was on average 69 basis points lower than the reference rate. In order to improve the efficiency of open market operations, the NBP started using fine-tuning operations from December last year, including the issuance of cash vouchers with shorter maturities, mainly 3-day. As a result, the difference between the POLONIA rate and the reference rate has now decreased to approx. 15 basis points, which proves the effectiveness of the actions taken. I can add that the European Central Bank would be very proud if EONIA, the interest rate corresponding to POLONIA, was so close to the reference rate. There, this deviation is much greater. In 2010, the situation on the financial markets improved and the bank's demand for additional funding from the central bank disappeared. For this reason, the NBP gradually limited the use of the instruments introduced in October 2008 as part of the so-called Confidence Package in response to the global financial crisis, i.e. repo operations and currency swaps. Anyway: a5 in January 2010, the offering of foreign exchange swaps on the CHF/PLN pair was completed. a5 since April 2010, the offer of repo operations with a 6-month deadline has ceased maturity and currency swaps on the USD/PLN and EUR/PLN pairs, a5 since October 2010, repo operations have been completely abandoned. As a result of these changes, since October 2010, the NBP has been using the same set of monetary policy instruments as before the outbreak of the financial crisis. At the same time, we are closely and continuously monitoring the situation of the financial sector and remain fully ready to resume the application of the non-standard liquidity facility package if necessary. Honourable Members! The recent financial crisis has proved to be an extremely difficult challenge for the European institutions as well as for national authorities. Extensive interventions to restore confidence in the financial system and the effects of the current crisis in the form of an economic slowdown and an increase in public debt in some EU countries have sparked a debate on the lessons to be learned from this difficult lesson. The European Commission has set up an expert group chaired by Jacques de Larosi8fre to identify the main gaps in the current structure of financial supervision contributing to the emergence and spread of the crisis. The most important of them were: - firstly, the focus of the regulator's and supervisor's attention on individual financial institutions, thereby failing to recognise systemic risks; - secondly, insufficient cross-border cooperation between institutions responsible for financial stability in the countries of the European Union. Following the recommendations of the de Larosi8fre report, Europe has carried out a major reform of the financial safety net. Since January 2011, a new European System of Financial Supervisors has been in place in the European Union. Its activity is based on the following pillars: macroprudential and microprudential. The macroprudential system of the Union is governed by the newly established independent body, the European Systemic Risk Board. The experience of the recent crisis has shown that financial stability is a concept that goes far beyond the stability of individual financial institutions. Therefore, the main added value that the Council has brought is the perspective of a systemic analysis of financial stability. The Council focuses on identifying and responding to risks for the financial system as a whole. These risks may arise from links between financial institutions and markets, as well as from macroeconomic and structural considerations, including financial innovation. The Council has been equipped with instruments to respond to identified risks in order to eliminate or reduce them. These instruments are warnings and recommendations for remedial action. The President of the Council shall be the President of the European Central Bank. The Nbp Governor, like other governors of the national central bank in the European Union countries, is a member of the General Council of the same European Systemic Risk Board with voting rights. The NBP Governor was also elected to the Steering Committee as a representative of a country outside the eurozone and the only representative of the central bank of the Central and Eastern Europe region. The microprudential authority in terms of responsibility for the supervision of financial systems in the European Union countries and risk control in individual financial institutions remained in the hands of the national financial supervisory authority. However, coordination mechanisms have been strengthened. At central level, in place of The committee has created three new European Supervisory Authorities, responsible for the banking sector, the insurance sector and the financial market. In the aftermath of the crisis, the infrastructure for macro and micro-prudential supervision has been significantly strengthened and expanded. The tasks and instruments of influence of the various bodies responsible for financial stability, in particular the central bank, have been modified. In this respect, American solutions and some European Union countries, consisting in strengthening the role and competences of the central bank, deserve special attention. The lessons learned from the experience of the recent financial crisis and regulatory reforms in the European financial system also determine the need to strengthen the structure of financial supervision in Poland and to define the place and role of the NBP in it. It is indisputable that there is a need to build macroprudential supervision in Poland in the shape of the European Systemic Risk Board. Recommendations formulated by international organizations and current international practice indicate that the central bank should play a major role in macroprudential policy. This is primarily due to the following factors: - firstly, central banks are institutions with relevant experience, analytical skills and adequate human resources, - secondly, most central banks, including the National Bank of Polish, have a statutory task of promoting financial stability, - thirdly, central banks have the final say in the European Systemic Risk Board. Therefore, following the example of European solutions can also be beneficial in our country. A possible solution is to create a body responsible for macroprudential policy, in which the National Bank of Polish would play a leading role. This would allow the central bank, in close cooperation with the Ministry of Finance, the Polish Financial Supervision Authority and other institutions concerned with financial stability, to more effectively reduce systemic risk and protect the security of the national financial system. The need to ensure the financial security of the state through the creation of a spne, efficient and effective safety net should guide all the institutions that make up it and remain the focus of legislative activities. I put at the disposal of the High Chamber all the potential and expert knowledge of the National Bank of Poland in this area. High Chamber! The recent financial crisis has shown the weakness of the existing regulations on capital requirements in the banking sector and has highlighted the overly liberal supervisor in its approach to the risks managed by banks. In response to the crisis, the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision adopted a draft regulatory amendment called Basel III, amending the existing second Capital Agreement, Basel II. The new Basel regulations oblige banks to significantly increase the size of their capital base and the quality of capital accumulated, so that they can absorb potential losses to a greater extent. Higher requirements are intended to protect banks from bankruptcy, but also to limit possible budget costs if there is a need for state authorities to rescue the bank. Higher capital requirements and a more conservative approach to their quality are intended to guarantee greater stability of the banking sector in the future. The new requirements are to be introduced gradually, from 2013 to 2019. From the perspective of the central bank, the so-called countercyclical buffer deserves special attention. This buffer is to take the form of an additional capital requirement imposed on loans granted by banks to entities in the country, in which excessive growth of lending is observed. During a period of crisis, this buffer will be flexibly reduced. It is an innovative instrument whose use will be the basis for an effective macroprudential policy pursued by the competent national authorities. Due to the fact that Basel III will be incorporated into European law by the provisions of the EU directive, the so-called CRD IV, its regulations will also be obligatory for a bank in Poland. The adaptation of a bank in Poland to the Basel III regulations, the so-called CSB4, should not be a particularly difficult problem. Banks in Poland have a relatively high level of own funds of the highest quality, and their current conservative credit policy, resulting from Polish supervisory regulations, corresponds to the new Basel requirements. The National Bank of Polish analyses the situation of the banking sector on an ongoing basis d0 its ability to absorb possible losses due to the materialisation of credit risk and its resistance to hypothetical macroeconomic shocks. The results of the survey are published once every year in the Report on the Stability of the Financial System. In the last simulation published in the July report, the bank's financial condition was subjected to stress tests, assuming the occurrence of stress conditions d0 set at a much more stringent level than in the study conducted by the European Banking Authority. Its results indicate that the vast majority of commercial banks in Poland have sufficient capital to operate safely even in the unlikely scenario of a strong slowdown in economic growth. The new financial liquidity standards proposed by the Basel III regulations are also largely consistent with the liquidity standards in force in Poland. The main challenge for the bank in Poland will be to increase the share of stable and long-term foals of financing, the lack of which may inhibit the granting of long-term loans in the event of failure to take appropriate adjustment measures. It is therefore necessary to promote long-term forms of saving and to develop and disseminate long-term banking debt instruments. High Chamber! As part of its activities for the stability of the national financial system, the National Bank of Polish cooperated with the Ministry of Finance and the Polish Financial Supervision Authority in the Financial Stability Committee. The Committee shall provide a platform for the exchange of information and shall coordinate action in the event of events materially threatening the stability of the national financial system. In our opinion, the composition of the Financial Stability Committee should be supplemented by the Bank Guarantee Fund, which provides financial assistance to banks, which strengthens the security of the financial system in Poland. High Sejm! One of the factors of the financial security of the state is the size of foreign exchange reserves. Indeed, they support the financial credibility of the country, reducing the risk of a sharp outflow of foreign capital, as well as reducing the cost of financing on global markets. By managing foreign exchange reserves, the National Bank of Polish strives to ensure a high level of security of invested funds, the necessary degree of their liquidity and obtain the highest possible profitability. In 2010, the official reserve assets of the National Bank of Poland increased by nearly 15 billion euros, to 70 billion euros. This was the result of the inflow of funds from the European Union and income from investing reserves. At the end of June this year, official reserve assets reached a value of 75.3 billion euros. In terms of the size of reserve assets, Poland ranks 23rd in the world and 7th in Europe. The dominant part of foreign exchange reserves is invested in government securities and securities issued by international institutions. A small part of them are deposits held in banks with high creditworthiness. In 2010, the National Bank of Polish achieved a higher rate of return on reserves than in the previous year, which amounted to 4% in PLN terms, while in 2009 it was only 1.9%. This was the result of an increase in the price of securities, appreciation of reserve currencies against the zloty, as well as currency diversification of reserves. In 2010, Doch generated PLN 4.5 billion from investment activities related to the management of foreign exchange provisions, while net foreign exchange income income amounted to PLN 2.5 billion. After taking into account the remaining revenue and cost, the final financial result of the NBP for 2010 amounted to PLN 6.5 billion, i.e. it was higher than a year earlier by PLN 2.4 billion. At this point, I would like to remind you that the profit of the National Bank of Poland depends to a large extent on the development of the zloty exchange rate. In previous years, the subject of the NBP result aroused a lot of controversy. They concerned the interpretation of the accounting rules applied by the central bank in relation to the creation and resolution of provisions to cover the risk of changes in the zloty exchange rate. In December last year, the Monetary Policy Council unanimously adopted a resolution clearly specifying these principles. According to the Act on the National Bank of Poland, 95% of the NBP's profit, i.e. PLN 6.2 billion, was transferred to the state budget. High Chamber! The National Bank of Polish has been conducting analyses and research on the impact of the introduction of a common European currency in our country for many years. The results of these studies show that accession to the euro area should be beneficial for Polish in the long term, but that the right timing of the introduction of the euro, depending on the fulfilment of economic, institutional and, ultimately, political conditions, will be decisive for the development of the balance of benefits and costs in the short and medium term. Currently, the euro area is facing many problems. Requiring decisive political decisions. They concern not only the resolution of the current debt crisis of the peripheral countries, but also the discipline of budgetary policy. In the longer term, remaining outside the euro area risks economic marginalisation in the Union. Accession to monetary union should therefore be a strategic objective of the Polish. However, the ability of the Polish economy to benefit and resist the threats resulting from the exchange of the zloty for the euro will depend on several factors. First, you must complete all the formal conditions of Maastricht. As the crisis has shown, the ability to ensure that they are met once they have qualified for monetary union will be particularly important here. Secondly, it is necessary to ensure the broadly understood competitiveness of the economy by improving the quality of the factor of production, including the most important in the contemporary economy - human capital. Thirdly, an important criterion for joining the euro area should be to solve the debt problem of peripheral countries and to reform the economic governance system of the euro area. Despite the lack of an official planned date for the adoption of the euro, the National Bank of Poland is conducting activities aimed at the best possible preparation of the process of introducing a common currency. NBP representatives participate in the work of the National Coordination Committee for the Euro, the Coordination Council and the Interinstitutional Working Group on Preparations for the Introduction of the Euro by the Republic of Poland. Mr Speaker, Honourable Members, I would like to thank the rapporteur. The year 2010 was a period of great activity of the National Bank of Poland on the international arena. We took part in the preparations for the Presidency of the Council of the European Union, coordinated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, carrying out selected tasks in the area of financial services. We participated in the creation of the already mentioned European Systemic Risk Board. We work within the framework of the European System of Central Bank, in which, as the President of the NBP, I take part in the quarterly meetings of the General Council We participate in the work of many committees and about fifty different working groups and the ESCB task force. NBP representatives also take part in informal meetings of the ECOFIN Council and the work of the auxiliary body of the Council of the European Union. I also represent Poland in the World Bank Group, and specifically by having a bank, i.e. I participate in meetings of the Governor's Boards of the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund. In 2010, the Minister of Finance and the President of the Nbp applied to the International Monetary Fund for re-granting Poland access to the Flexible Credit Line. It plays an important role from the point of view of external stabilization of the economy, economic security of the state, protection of the value of the Polish currency and improves the credibility of Polish on international financial markets. In January this year, the IMF Executive Director's Board granted this request and granted Poland access to the Credit Line for two years, in the amount of about USD 30 billion. We provide technical and training assistance to the central banks of countries in transition. I will mention Azerbaijan, Armenia, Belarus, Georgia, Moldova and Ukraine. In addition, Afghanistan, Kosovo, Lebanon, Turkmenistan and Syria. A total of 33 central banks have so far benefited from our technical assistance. Together with the Bundesbank, we support the activities of the National Bank of Ukraine, we also participate in the ECB project for the National Bank of Serbia. High Sejm! The statutory task of the National Bank of Poland is to compile monetary and banking statistics, balance of payments and international investment position. Statistical data obtained by the NBP from financial institutions are one of the most important foals of information used in the central bank's monetary policy. They are also the basis for research and analytical work and the formulation of forecasts of the country's monetary situation. Statistics compiled by the NBP is, next to the statistics of the Central Statistical Office, one of the pillars of the country's statistical information system. The problem of balance of payments statistics, which has not been solved for many years, was Polish the size of the balance of errors and omissions. In 2010, it exceeded db13 billion, representing 8% of the total current account turnover. In the previous year, we undertook intensive work to significantly reduce this balance. The new estimates of balance of payments data published on 29 June this year more precisely illustrate the economic relations of the Polish with foreign countries. We have reduced the size of the balance of errors and omissions to an acceptable level, comparable to other European countries. High Chamber! The statutory task of the NBP is to organize cash settlements. The National Bank of Polish systematically conducts activities aimed at modernizing, expanding the functions and increasing the security of the payment system. In 2010, work began on a new version of the SORBNET system, supporting current accounts of the domestic bank kept in PLN. The new SORBNET2 system, which is expected to be launched in the first quarter of 2013, will use the latest IT solutions, which will improve the interbank settlement system in PLN. We are working on the development and popularization of cashless trade in Poland. Suffice it to say that costs with cash turnover are estimated in Poland at about 1% of GDP per year, while in the EU it is on average 0.4-0.6%. The largest part of these costs is borne by the National Bank of Polish, but also commercial banks, For these reasons, on the initiative and with the participation of the NBP, the "Program for the development of cashless trading in Poland for the years 2011-2013" was developed. The adoption of this document by the government will open the way for the implementation of the program, which will bring tangible benefits to the state, the economy and many entities. Mr Speaker, Honourable Members, The National Bank of Polish has the exclusive right to issue a cash sign of the Republic of Poland. By putting banknotes and coins into circulation, NBP ensures the liquidity of cash settlements and the appropriate quality of the monetary sign in circulation in Poland. The value of ready-made money in circulation as at 31 December 2010 amounted to PLN 103 billion. During the year, this increased by PLN 2.7 billion. This was due to the greater demand for monetary signs, primarily as a result of the economic recovery in Poland. We also issue collector coins and banknotes. This is to commemorate events and figures important for Polish society, as well as to disseminate knowledge about culture and history Polish. I will mention here the dwh, recently carried out by the NBP issues of collector coins, commemorating two important events for Polish: the beatification of John Paul II and the anniversary of the catastrophe at Smolensk. High Sejm! At the beginning of 2010, the National Bank of Polish introduced new rules for the acquisition of collector's items. Coins were sold only at electronic auctions, conducted in the Kolekcjoner IT system. This change was coldly received by the numismatic market, and at the same time made it difficult for people who do not have access to the Internet to buy coins and collector's notes. For these reasons, the demand for coins has clearly decreased. In this situation: -first of all, we have added the possibility of buying banknotes and collector coins at the cash desks of the NBP district branch, -we have made changes to the Kolekcjoner system, m.in we have introduced the possibility of purchasing in the online store, - we have established a Numismatic Affairs Council, composed of representatives of this environment, with an important opinion-giving and advisory function on all issues related to the issue of coins and collector's notes. The matter seems to be small, but because it had a wide social resonance, I allowed myself to occupy you for a minute. honourable Members, I would like to thank the rapporteur. December 31, 2010 was the last day of the exchange of cash withdrawn from circulation under the 1995 denomination. The National Bank of Polish already in September 2010 launched a large-scale information campaign "Let's exchange", which reminded about the final date of exchange of old zlotys. In total, last year we exchanged old zlotys with a value of PLN 2.7 million. In total, we exchanged 99.83% of the value of the pre-denomination cash mark. Together with Caritas Poland, we organized an action enabling the public to donate banknotes and coins of the old issue to charity as part of the "Wings" program. The action was propagated in the media, thanks to which it was possible to collect over 250,000 new zlotys for this project. The funds were donated to 300 scholarships for children from the poorest families. High Chamber! We conduct many educational activities. Last year, we completed 264 projects. Currently, we continue these activities, choosing topics and forms of educational activity, we use the experience and opinions of academic and scientific communities and consult with them the directions of our activities. We are working on creating an educational cake called the Money Center. It will be a place where we will use the latest multimedia techniques to disseminate economic knowledge. The cake will present the history of money, the history of banking and the mechanisms governing the economy and economy. The Money Centre will be located in the NBP Headquarters at ?wi?tokrzyska Street and will bear the name of my predecessor as the President of the NBP, the tragically deceased S?awomir Skrzypek. We plan to open the Centre at the turn of 2012 and 2013. High Chamber! Since 2008, the district branch and the Head Office of the National Bank of Poland have been restructured. As a result, last year employment decreased by 103 FTEs and at the end of the year amounted to 3666 FTEs in the head office and 16 district branches. This allowed to reduce wage costs by PLN 1.9 million. In May this year, there was a change in the internal organization of NBP's activities. Three internally spjne divisions were created, supervised by the President and Vice-President of the NBP. The division of tasks between divisions has been made in terms of content, which allows for closer cooperation between departments than before and opens up the possibility of further reorganization of the NBP in order to increase the efficiency of its activities and optimize the cost. Mr Speaker, Honourable Members, I would like to thank the rapporteur. The High Sejm appointed me president of the National Bank of Poland on 10 June 2010. My assumption of the office of President took place at a special moment, because the term of office of my predecessor was interrupted by a sudden, tragic death in the catastrophe near Smolensk. Moreover, after the financial crisis, the global macroeconomic situation was unstable and the outlook for economic growth was fraught with high uncertainty. The National Bank Polish react flexibly to changes in the external environment, adapting the available instruments to the current needs of the market. In this way, the central bank has contributed to maintaining the stability of the financial system and consolidating economic growth. Currently, the macroeconomic situation and prospects for economic growth in Poland are better. However, this does not mean that our economy does not face any problems. On the contrary, we face major challenges. From the point of view of macroeconomic policy, these are primarily: reducing inflation, reducing the deficit of the public finance sector and strengthening the security and stability of the financial system. These objectives can be effectively achieved only under conditions of close cooperation and coordination of the monetary policy of the National Bank of Poland, the budgetary policy of the Government and the supervisory policy of the Polish Financial Supervision Authority, in accordance with the constitutional principle of the functioning of the State body. Only in such conditions is it possible to achieve sustainable and balanced economic growth and to make the Polish economy resistant to unexpected shocks in the external environment. As the President of the NBP, I declare that the institution I lead will take all actions necessary to achieve our common goal: to increase the prosperity of poles. Thank you very much.

Jest to nie tylko wypenienie ustawowego obowizku przedstawienia Sejmowi rezultat dziaania NBP, ale take moliwo zapoznania Wysokiej Izby z uwarunkowaniami, w jakich funkcjonowa bank i polska gospodarka w ubiegym roku. Po okresie znacznego spowolnienia tempa wzrostu gospodarczego na wiecie w latach 2008 2009, kte byo nastpstwem kryzysu na wiatowych rynkach finansowych, od roku 2010 obserwujemy oywienie w gospodarce wiatowej. Niejednoznacznie natomiast przedstawia si sytuacja ekonomiczna w Stanach Zjednoczonych, gdzie po dynamicznej poprawie koniunktury w ubiegym roku nastpio wyrane spowolnienie tempa wzrostu PKB i zatrudnienia. Brak widocznej poprawy na rynku nieruchomoci, wysokie bezrobocie, a take szybko rosncy dug publiczny stanowi istotne czynniki ryzyka dla wzrostu gospodarczego.
