Jej wyniki wskazuj, e zdecydowana wikszo bank komercyjnych w Polsce ma wystarczajce kapitay, aby bezpiecznie funkcjonowa nawet w przypadku wystpienia mao prawdopodobnego scenariusza zakadajcego silne spowolnienie wzrostu gospodarczego. Rnie nowe normy pynnoci finansowej, proponowane przez regulacje Bazylei III, s w duym stopniu zbiene z normami pynnoci obowizujcymi w Polsce. Gnym wyzwaniem dla bank w Polsce bdzie zwikszenie udziau stabilnych i dugoterminowych re finansowania, ktych brak moe hamowa udzielanie dugoterminowych kredyt w przypadku niepodjcia odpowiednich dziaa dostosowawczych. Dlatego konieczne jest promowanie dugoterminowych form oszczdzania oraz rozw i upowszechnianie dugoterminowych bankowych instrument dunych. Wysoka Izbo! W ramach dziaalnoci na rzecz stabilnoci krajowego systemu finansowego Narodowy Bank Polski wsppracowa z Ministerstwem Finans i Komisj Nadzoru Finansowego w Komitecie Stabilnoci Finansowej. Komitet stanowi platform wymiany informacji oraz koordynuje dziaania w przypadku pojawienia si zdarze istotnie zagraajcych stabilnoci krajowego systemu finansowego. Naszym zdaniem skad Komitetu Stabilnoci Finansowej powinien zosta uzupeniony o Bankowy Fundusz Gwarancyjny, kty oprz gwarantowania depozyt, udziela pomocy finansowej bankom, przez co wzmacnia bezpieczestwo systemu finansowego w Polsce. Wysoki Sejmie! Jednym z czynnik bezpieczestwa finansowego pastwa jest wielko rezerw dewizowych. Istotnie wspieraj one wiarygodno finansow kraju, ograniczajc ryzyko gwatownego odpywu kapitau zagranicznego, a take obniaj koszt finansowania na rynkach globalnych. Zarzdzajc rezerwami dewizowymi, Narodowy Bank Polski dy do zapewnienia wysokiego poziomu bezpieczestwa inwestowanych rodk, niezbdnego stopnia ich pynnoci oraz uzyskania jak najwyszej dochodowoci. W 2010 r. oficjalne aktywa rezerwowe Narodowego Banku Polskiego wzrosy o blisko 15 mld euro, do 70 mld . Byo to skutkiem napywu rodk z Unii Europejskiej oraz dochod z inwestowania rezerw. Na koniec czerwca biecego roku oficjalne aktywa rezerwowe osigny warto 75,3 mld euro. Pod wzgldem wielkoci aktyw rezerwowych Polska zajmuje 23. miejsce w wiecie i 7. miejsce w Europie. Dominujca cz rezerw walutowych inwestowana jest w rzdowe papiery wartociowe oraz papiery emitowane przez instytucje midzynarodowe. Niewielk ich cz stanowi lokaty utrzymywane w bankach o wysokiej wiarygodnoci kredytowej. W 2010 r. Narodowy Bank Polski osign wysz ni w roku poprzednim stop zwrotu z rezerw, kta wyniosa 4% w ujciu zotowym, podczas gdy w roku 2009 byo to tylko 1,9%. Byo to efektem wzrostu cen papier wartociowych, aprecjacji walut rezerwowych wzgldem zotego, a take dywersyfikacji walutowej rezerw. Doch z dziaalnoci inwestycyjnej zwizanej z zarzdzaniem rezerwami dewizowymi wyni w roku 2010 4,5 mld z, natomiast wynik z tytuu rnic kursowych 2,5 mld z. Po uwzgldnieniu pozostaych przychod oraz koszt ostateczny wynik finansowy NBP za 2010 rok wyni 6,5 mld z, a zatem by wyszy ni rok wczeniej o 2,4 mld z. W tym miejscu przypomn, e zysk Narodowego Banku Polskiego zaley w zasadniczym stopniu od ksztatowania si kursu zotego. W poprzednich latach temat wyniku NBP budzi wiele kontrowersji. Dotyczyy one interpretacji zasad rachunkowoci stosowanych przez bank centralny w odniesieniu do tworzenia i rozwizywania rezerw na pokrycie ryzyka zmian kursu zotego. W grudniu ubiegego roku Rada Polityki Pieninej jednomylnie podja uchwa jasno precyzujc te zasady. Zgodnie z ustaw o Narodowym Banku Polskim 95% zysku NBP, czyli 6,2 mld z, zostao przekazane do budetu pastwa. Wysoka Izbo! Narodowy Bank Polski od wielu lat prowadzi analizy i badania na temat skutk wprowadzenia wspnej europejskiej waluty w naszym kraju. Wyniki tych bada dowodz, e w dugim okresie przystpienie do strefy euro powinno by dla Polski korzystne, jednak dla ksztatowania si bilansu korzyci i koszt w krkim i rednim okresie decydujcy bdzie wyb odpowiedniego momentu wprowadzenia euro uzalenionego od spenienia warunk ekonomicznych, instytucjonalnych, a w kocu i politycznych. Obecnie strefa euro zmaga si z wieloma problemami. Wymagajcymi podjcia zdecydowanych decyzji politycznych. Dotycz one nie tylko rozwizania biecego kryzysu zadueniowego kraj peryferyjnych, lecz take zdyscyplinowania polityki budetowej. W duszym okresie pozostawanie poza stref euro grozi marginalizacj ekonomiczn w Unii. Dlatego przystpienie do unii monetarnej powinno by strategicznym celem Polski. Zdolno polskiej gospodarki do czerpania korzyci i przeciwstawiania si zagroeniom wynikajcym z zamiany zotego na euro bdzie jednak zalee od kilku czynnik. Po pierwsze, naley wypeni wszystkie formalne warunki z Maastricht. Jak pokaza kryzys, szczeglnie wana bdzie tu zdolno do zapewnienia trwaoci ich spenienia ju po zakwalifikowaniu si do unii walutowej. Po drugie, naley zadba o szeroko rozumian konkurencyjno gospodarki poprzez popraw jakoci czynnik produkcji, w tym najistotniejszego we wspczesnej gospodarce - kapitau ludzkiego. Po trzecie, istotnym kryterium wejcia do strefy euro powinno by rozwizanie problemu zaduenia kraj peryferyjnych oraz zreformowanie systemu zarzdzania gospodarczego strefy euro. Pomimo braku oficjalnej planowanej daty przyjcia euro w Narodowym Banku Polskim prowadzone s dziaania majce na celu jak najlepsze przygotowanie procesu wprowadzania wspnej waluty. Przedstawiciele NBP uczestnicz w pracach Narodowego Komitetu Koordynacyjnego do spraw Euro, Rady Koordynacyjnej oraz Midzyinstytucjonalnych Zespo Roboczych do spraw Przygotowa do Wprowadzenia Euro przez Rzeczpospolit Polsk. Panie Marszaku, Panie Posanki, Panowie Posowie! Rok 2010 by okresem duej aktywnoci Narodowego Banku Polskiego na arenie midzynarodowej. Bralimy udzia w koordynowanych przez Ministerstwo Spraw Zagranicznych przygotowaniach do sprawowania przewodnictwa w Radzie Unii Europejskiej, realizujc wybrane zadania w obszarze usug finansowych. Uczestniczylimy w tworzeniu wspomnianej ju Europejskiej Rady ds. Ryzyka Systemowego. Pracujemy w ramach Europejskiego Systemu Bank Centralnych, w ktym jako Prezes NBP bior udzia w kwartalnych posiedzeniach Rady Ognej Bierzemy udzia w pracach wielu komitet oraz okoo pidziesiciu rnych grup roboczych i zespo zadaniowych ESBC. Przedstawiciele NBP bior take udzia w nieformalnych posiedzeniach Rady ECOFIN oraz pracach organ pomocniczych Rady Unii Europejskiej. Reprezentuj take Polsk w Grupie Banku wiatowego, a konkretnie mic w banku, tzn. uczestnicz w posiedzeniach Rad Gubernator Banku wiatowego oraz Midzynarodowego Funduszu Walutowego. W 2010 r. Minister Finans i Prezes NBP wspnie wystpili do Midzynarodowego Funduszu Walutowego z wnioskiem o ponowne przyznanie Polsce dostpu do Elastycznej Linii Kredytowej. Odgrywa ona wan rol z punktu widzenia zewntrznej stabilizacji gospodarki, bezpieczestwa gospodarczego pastwa, ochrony wartoci polskiej waluty oraz poprawia wiarygodno Polski na midzynarodowych rynkach finansowych. W styczniu biecego roku Rada Dyrektor Wykonawczych MFW pozytywnie rozpatrzya ten wniosek i przyznaa Polsce dostp do Linii Kredytowej na dwa lata, w wysokoci okoo 30 mld USD. Udzielamy pomocy technicznej i szkoleniowej bankom centralnym pastw w okresie transformacji. Wymieni tu Azerbejdan, Armeni, Biaoru, Gruzj, Modawi i Ukrain. Ponadto Afganistan, Kosowo, Liban, Turkmenistan i Syria. cznie 33 banki centralne dotychczas skorzystay z naszej pomocy technicznej. Wspnie z Bundesbankiem wspieramy dziaania Narodowego Banku Ukrainy, bierzemy take udzia w projekcie EBC na rzecz Narodowego Banku Serbii. Wysoki Sejmie! Ustawowym zadaniem Narodowego Banku Polskiego jest opracowywanie statystyki pieninej i bankowej, bilansu patniczego oraz midzynarodowej pozycji inwestycyjnej. Dane statystyczne pozyskiwane przez NBP od instytucji finansowych s jednym z najwaniejszych re informacji wykorzystywanych w prowadzonej przez bank centralny polityce pieninej. Stanowi one take podstaw prac badawczo-analitycznych i formuowania prognoz sytuacji pieninej kraju. Statystyka sporzdzana przez NBP jest, obok statystyki GUS, jednym z filar systemu informacji statystycznej kraju. Nierozwizanym od wielu lat problemem statystyki bilansu patniczego Polski bya wielko salda bd i opuszcze. W 2010 r. przekroczyo ono 13 mld euro, co stanowio 8% cakowitej wartoci obrot na rachunku biecym. Jeszcze w poprzednim roku podjlimy intensywne prace w celu istotnego zmniejszenia tego salda. Nowe szacunki danych bilansu patniczego opublikowane 29 czerwca br. bardziej precyzyjnie obrazuj relacje gospodarcze Polski z zagranic. Wielko salda bd i opuszcze sprowadzilimy do akceptowalnego poziomu, pornywalnego z innymi krajami europejskimi. Wysoka Izbo! Ustawowym zadaniem NBP jest organizowanie rozlicze pieninych. Narodowy Bank Polski systematycznie prowadzi dziaania na rzecz modernizacji, rozszerzenia funkcji oraz zwikszania bezpieczestwa systemu patniczego. W 2010 r. rozpoczto prace nad now wersj systemu SORBNET, obsugujcego rachunki biece bank krajowych prowadzone w zotych. Nowy system SORBNET2, ktego uruchomienie przewiduje si na pierwszy kwarta 2013 r., bdzie wykorzystywa najnowsze rozwizania informatyczne, co usprawni system rozrachunk midzybankowych w zotych. Prowadzimy prace nad rozwojem i upowszechnieniem w Polsce obrotu bezgotkowego. Wystarczy powiedzie, e koszty z obrotem gotkowym szacowane s w Polsce na okoo 1% PKB rocznie, podczas gdy w UE jest to rednio 0,4-0,6% . Najwiksz cz tych koszt ponosi Narodowy Bank Polski, ale tak banki komercyjne, Z tych powod z inicjatywy i przy udziale NBP opracowano Program rozwoju obrotu bezgotkowego w Polsce na lata 20112013. Przyjcie tego dokumentu przez rzd otworzy drog do wdroenia programu, co przyniesie wymierne korzyci dla pastwa, gospodarki i wielu podmiot. Panie Marszaku, Wysoka Izbo! Narodowy Bank Polski ma wyczne prawo emitowania znak pieninych Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej. Poprzez wprowadzanie do obiegu banknot i monet NBP zapewnia pynno rozlicze gotkowych oraz odpowiedni jako znak pieninych w Polsce w obiegu. Warto pienidza gotkowego w obiegu wedug stanu na 31 grudnia 2010 r. wyniosa 103 mld z. W cigu roku wzroso to o 2,7 mld z. Wynikao to z wikszego zapotrzebowania na znaki pienine, przede wszystkim na skutek oywienia gospodarczego w Polsce. Emitujemy rnie monety i banknoty kolekcjonerskie. Ma to na celu upamitnianie wydarze i postaci wanych dla polskiego spoeczestwa, jak rnie ma suy upowszechnianiu wiedzy o kulturze i historii Polski. Wspomn tu o dwh, ostatnio przeprowadzonych przez NBP emisjach monet kolekcjonerskich, upamitniajcych dwa wane dla Polski wydarzenia: beatyfikacj Jana Pawa II i rocznic katastrofy pod Smoleskiem. Wysoki Sejmie! Na pocztku 2010 r. Narodowy Bank Polski wprowadzi nowe zasady nabywania wartoci kolekcjonerskich. Monety sprzedawano jedynie na aukcjach elektronicznych, prowadzonych w systemie informatycznym Kolekcjoner. Zmiana ta zostaa chodno przyjta przez rynek numizmatyczny, a jednoczenie utrudnia zakup monet i banknot kolekcjonerskich osobom niemajcym dostpu do Internetu. Z tych powod popyt na monety wyranie si obniy. W takiej sytuacji: -po pierwsze przywrilimy moliwo zakupu banknot i monet kolekcjonerskich w kasach oddzia okrgowych NBP, -dokonalimy zmian w systemie Kolekcjoner, m.in. wprowadzilimy moliwo zakupu w sklepie internetowym, -powoalimy Rad do spraw numizmatycznych, zoon z przedstawicieli tego rodowiska, penic istotn funkcj opiniodawczo-doradcz we wszystkich kwestiach dotyczcych emisji monet i banknot kolekcjonerskich. Sprawa niby drobna, ale poniewa miaa szeroki rezonans spoeczny pozwoliem sobie p minuty czasu Pastwu zaj. Panie Posanki, Panowie Posowie! 31 grudnia 2010 r. by ostatnim dniem wymiany znak pieninych wycofanych z obiegu w ramach denominacji z 1995 r. Narodowy Bank Polski ju we wrzeniu 2010 r. rozpocz zakrojon na szerok skal kampani informacyjn Wymiemy si, kta przypomniaa o kocowym terminie wymiany starych zotych. W sumie w zeszym roku wymienilimy stare zote o rnowartoci 2,7 mln z. cznie wymienilimy 99,83% wartoci znak pieninych sprzed denominacji. Zorganizowalimy wraz z Caritas Polska akcj umoliwiajc spoeczestwu przekazanie banknot i monet starej emisji na cel dobroczynny w ramach programu Skrzyda. Akcja zostaa rozpropagowana w mediach, dziki czemu udao si zebra ponad 250 tys. nowych zotych dla tego progamu. rodki zostay przekazane na 300 stypendi dla dzieci z najbiedniejszych rodzin. Wysoka Izbo! Prowadzimy wiele dziaa edukacyjnych. Zrealizowalimy w zeszym roku 264 projekty. Obecnie kontynuujemy te dziaania, wybierajc tematy i formy aktywnoci edukacyjnej, korzystamy z dowiadcze oraz opinii rodowisk akademickich i naukowych i konsultujemy z nimi kierunki naszych dziaa. Pracujemy nad utworzeniem placki edukacyjnej pod nazw Centrum Pienidza. Bdzie to miejsce, gdzie za pomoc najnowszych technik multimedialnych bdziemy upowszechnia wiedz ekonomiczn. Placka prezentowa bdzie dzieje pienidza, histori bankowoci oraz mechanizmy rzdzce ekonomi i gospodark. Centrum Pienidza zostanie umiejscowione w Centrali NBP przy ulicy witokrzyskiej i bdzie nosi imi mojego poprzednika na stanowisku prezesa NBP, tragicznie zmarego Sawomira Skrzypka. Otwarcie Centrum planujemy na przeomie 2012 i 2013 r. Wysoka Izbo! Od 2008 r. prowadzona jest restrukturyzacja oddzia okrgowych i Centrali Narodowego Banku Polskiego. W jej wyniku w ubiegym roku zatrudnienie obniyo si o 103 etaty i na koniec roku wynioso 3666 etat w centrali i 16 oddziaach okrgowych. Pozwolio to obniy koszty wynagrodze o 1,9 mln z. W maju biecego roku nastpia zmiana wewntrznej organizacji dziaalnoci NBP. Utworzono trzy, wewntrznie spjne, piony nadzorowane przez Prezesa i Wiceprezes NBP. Podzia zada midzy piony zosta dokonany pod wzgldem merytorycznym, co pozwala na cilejsz ni dotychczas wspprac midzy departamentami i otwiera moliwoci dalszej reorganizacji NBP w celu zwikszenia efektywnoci jego dziaa i optymalizacji koszt. Panie Marszaku, Panie Posanki, Panowie Posowie! Wysoki Sejm powoa mnie na stanowisko Prezesa Narodowego Banku Polskiego 10 czerwca 2010 r. Objcie przeze mnie urzdu Prezesa nastpio w szczegnym momencie, poniewa kadencja mojego poprzednika zostaa przerwana nag, tragicznmierci w katastrofie pod Smoleskiem. Ponadto, po okresie kryzysu finansowego globalna sytuacja makroekonomiczna bya nieustabilizowana, a perspektywy wzrostu gospodarczego obarczone wysok niepewnoci. Narodowy Bank Polski elastycznie reagowa na zmiany zachodzce w otoczeniu zewntrznym, dostosowujc dostpne instrumenty do biecych potrzeb rynku. W ten spos bank centralny przyczyni si do utrzymania stabilnoci systemu finansowego i utrwalenia wzrostu gospodarczego. Obecnie sytuacja makroekonomiczna i perspektywy wzrostu gospodarczego w Polsce s lepsze. Nie oznacza to jednak, e nasza gospodarka nie boryka si z adnymi problemami. Przeciwnie, stoj przed nami powane wyzwania. Z punktu widzenia polityki makroekonomicznej s to przede wszystkim: ograniczenie inflacji, zmniejszenie deficytu sektora finans publicznych oraz wzmocnienie bezpieczestwa i stabilnoci systemu finansowego. Cele te mog by skutecznie osignite jedynie w warunkach cisej wsppracy i koordynacji polityki pieninej Narodowego Banku Polskiego, polityki budetowej Rzdu i polityki nadzorczej Komisji Nadzoru Finansowego, zgodnie z konstytucyjn zasad wspdziaania organ Pastwa. Tylko w takich warunkach moliwe jest osignicie trwaego i zrnowaonego wzrostu gospodarczego oraz uodpornienie polskiej gospodarki na niespodziewane wstrzsy w otoczeniu zewntrznym. Jako Prezes NBP deklaruj, e kierowana przeze mnie instytucja bdzie podejmowa wszystkie dziaania niezbdne do realizacji naszego wspnego celu: wzrostu dobrobytu Polak. Dzikuj bardzo.

Title: Monetary policy challenges in a non-euro EU country
text: Monetary policy challenges in a non-euro EU country Speech by Marek Belka, Governor of the National Bank of Poland Euro50 Group Meeting The Eurozone in the aftermath of the Euro Crisis Willard Hotel, Washington DC 12 October 2014 Ladies and gentlemen, Let me first thank the organizers for giving me the opportunity to speak at this fo-rum. Since this is a breakfast meeting and you have a terrific lineup of speakers to-day, I will try to be brief and get right to the point. I would like to share with you some thoughts on what the euro crisis and its legacy implies for non-euro EU coun-tries, such as Poland. 1. The lessons from the euro crisis I think it is fair to say that the euro crisis was a game-changer in our thinking about the viability of currency unions in general and euro accession in particular. As you all know, the theoretical case for the euro was the theory of Optimum Currency Are-as developed by Robert Mundell in early 1960s and later refined by many others. The theory stipulated that to make a currency area work you needed essentially two things: labor force mobility and some sort of budgetary transfers on the federal level. The two features were to make up for the loss of natural asymmetric shock absorbers such as independent monetary policy and freely floating exchange rates. Although, frankly, the early euro area had neither of those features, the belief at the time was  first  that countries would engage in structural reforms increasing the flexibility of their labor markets and  second  that economic integration would reduce the like-lihood of asymmetric shocks in the first place. Unfortunately, the recent crisis revealed that the currency union not only hasnt eliminated asymmetric shocks, but in fact might have induced a major shock itself. This goes back to the argument that inflation rates would not converge quickly across the monetary union, due to Balassa-Samuelson effects and overly loose fiscal policies. With a single nominal interest rate determining the cost of borrowing, this meant that low real rates in the periphery fueled spending booms financed by huge capital flows from the core countries. All the subprime crisis did was to cast doubt on the sustainability of this process, triggering the familiar sudden stop scenario, called by Paul Krugman the mother of all asymmetric shocks. But I think the impact of the crisis was so severe not only because  with limited la-bor force mobility and no serious federal fiscal transfers  the adjustment to the asymmetric shock had to be painful. There were also two other factors at play which exacerbated the initial problem. First, there was the negative feedback loop between sovereign and bank solvency. Euro area banks have over the years built up considerable exposures to their domes-tic sovereigns  higher than their counterparts in the UK or the US. In the face of a marked fiscal deterioration  resulting from government response to the crisis  this debt load has encouraged speculation on banks solvency, which required European governments to intervene and rescue banks, which in turn increased the riskiness of sovereign bonds, threatening banks even further. Second, as argued perhaps most forcefully by Paul de Grauwe, due to various in-stitutional limitations it was not clear in the initial stages of the crisis whether the euro area had a lender of last resort for governments in quite the same sense as other countries. In any case, market participants seemed to think that it didnt and consequently priced the risk of default of Spain much higher than, say, the UK de-spite the latters higher debt-to-GDP ratio at the time. This is not to say that there were no legitimate reasons for the Eurosystem to act differently than a non-EA cen-tral bank, but this different position of the ECB vis-a-vis euro area sovereigns has made it more difficult to stop the self-fulfilling default trajectories. 2. Non-euro EU countries are here to stay One obvious implication of all this is that euro area needs institutional reforms that will make it more robust and more flexible in tackling shocks. And, indeed, serious work is already underway on this front with the ESM and the SSM to name just two key pieces of legislation. Yet, although we can expect Banking Union to weaken the link between banks and sovereigns, I dont think it can eliminate it altogether  at least as long as government debt retains its preferential regulatory treatment. The second implication is that the European Community cannot afford to once again underestimate the risks of premature expansion of the euro area. There are the Maas-tricht criteria which should be met over the long run, of course. But, half-jokingly, I propose a tougher test: if a country doesnt have as competitive an economy as Switzerland, as flexible a labor market as Denmark and as disciplined public fi-nances as Estonia, it should think twice about adopting the euro. Clearly, these criteria can only be taken half seriously, but at least they give a sense of the scale along which countries should measure their capacity to join. Moreover, countries that do not score well on my test, should not hope that any of their potential econom-ic deficiencies can be miraculously fixed by the euro. The bottom line here is that non-euro EU member states are probably here to stay  at least for the foreseeable future  and for good reasons so. But if that is the case, then it makes sense to ponder challenges faced by monetary policymakers in such countries. This is indeed what I intend to do now focusing on the case of Poland which I am obviously most familiar with. 3. Autonomous monetary policy in a world of no autonomy To set the stage let me just say that Polish economy has weathered the crisis remark-ably well. Since 2008 GDP in Poland grew by over 20% which is really something, if you consider that during that time euro area GDP has not even managed to break even. At the same time, inflation has been kept under control, averaging 2.7% over the past decade which is practically at the NBPs target of 2.5%. Part of this success is attributable to the floating exchange rate. Note, that from the point of view of an external investor, wages in Poland have fallen by roughly 30% in early 2009 with no painful renegotiation of contracts or labor force changes simply by letting the zloty depreciate  something that wouldnt be possible in a currency union. But of course it would be naive to say that we are immune to developments in the euro area. To the contrary. With over 50% of our exports going to the euro area, and 25% to Germany alone, it is no wonder that price and output dynamics in Poland are strongly correlated with those in the euro area  even if the scale of the movements is somewhat different. Moreover, over 55% of our banking sector assets are owned by financial institutions from the euro area  most notably in Germany and Italy. We are thus not only closely linked to the real side of the euro area economy, but also to its financial sector. And cross-border lending from European banks is one of the chan-nels through which ECB monetary policy impulses can feed through to the Polish economy. This brings me to the key challenge for conducting monetary policy in Poland and perhaps also in other non-euro EU member states. This challenge consists in having to conduct autonomous monetary policy under conditions of strongly limited au-tonomy. This limited autonomy is not due to any institutional or legal restrictions, but a consequence of the free movement of international capital and cross-border financial linkages. And capital-flow and exchange-rate volatility that come with it can have a powerful adverse impact on macroeconomic and financial stability. Very loose global liquidity conditions and near-zero interest rates in core markets have encouraged capital inflows to emerging markets  especially those with relatively high real interest rates and developed capital markets. Through a well-known mech-anism, such capital inflows may lead to excessive strengthening of the domestic cur-rency, undercutting the competitiveness of firms in the tradable sector. They can also fuel credit booms and provide incentives for greater use of foreign currency denomi-nated liabilities, which in turn may lead to unsustainable balance sheet structures  something many countries in Central and Eastern Europe, including Poland, have struggled with. And now we come to the dilemma: if it is the interest rate differential thats driving capital inflow, then it might seem natural to respond by aligning interest rates in emerging economies with those in core markets. But, after all, interest rates in emerg-ing economies were higher for a reason. Depending on the economy in question, cut-ting rates too low could fuel an internal- rather than external-financed boom, with similarly adverse consequences. These considerations remain highly relevant for non-euro EU countries even as the Fed is exiting from its unconventional monetary policy measures, since the ECB is going in the opposite direction. This means that capital flow volatility is still to be expected in the euro area neighborhood. This is certainly not to say that a new round of monetary policy easing by the ECB is unwelcome. To the contrary, as I have stressed above, given close trade ties and the correlation of inflation and output between Poland and the euro area, any measures supporting demand in the euro area are desperately needed. But the challenge of re-sponding to capital-flow and exchange-rate volatility remains. I cannot pretend to have a universally applicable solution, but I can offer some sug-gestions based on our experiences in Poland. First, I think a case can be made for central banks to lean against the wind in the FX market. Let me explain what I mean by this. Before the crisis, the consensus was that inflation targeting central banks should only care about the exchange rate to the extent that it affected inflation. Im afraid this is no longer enough. Of course, as Ive stressed above, it is generally good to have a freely floating exchange rate. It serves as a buffer against asymmetric shocks and introduces some volatility in the FX mar-ket which should discourage complacent attitudes towards risk. But at the same time short-term FX developments can pose financial stability concerns, even if they have limited direct impact on inflation. The central bank should lean against such devel-opments, because if it doesnt, its inflation target could become compromised in the longer run anyway. Hence, central banks need to strike the right balance between, on the one hand, reacting against temporary swings in FX during risk-on-risk-off phases and, on the other hand, suppressing FX risk and with it market disci-pline. Second, although monetary policy itself cannot be autonomous, it can and should be supplemented by autonomous macroprudential policy. Macroprudential policy should remain autonomous because the developments that it is designed to handle are inherently local, rather than global. For example, housing and labor market char-acteristics are markedly different across EU countries and so different LtV or DTI can be appropriate in different jurisdictions. And having a locally-oriented macropru-dential policy makes the lack of autonomy in interest rate policy less problematic, as it allows the central bank to keep rates more aligned with core markets without jeop-ardizing financial stability. Finally, with a leaning against the wind approach to FX developments and au-tonomous macroprudential policy limiting the risk of credit booms, the central bank should be flexible in its pursuit of the inflation target. Although I am not a particular fan of baseball, I like Warren Buffets saying that great players watch the field, not the scoreboard. Similarly, the central bank should look at underlying pro-cesses, rather than be obsessed by keeping inflation on target every year. And on this note, I feel I should end  wishing you further inspiring discussions and a nice, productive day. Thank you.

Title: Building Market Economies in Europe. Lessons and challenges after 25 years of transition
text: Speech by Marek Belka, President, Narodowy Bank Polski Building Market Economies in Europe. Lessons and Challenges after 25 years of Transition 24 October 2014 Ladies and Gentlemen, Dear Colleagues, Last August, Tony Barber published in the Financial Times1 an article about the events marking the beginning of the political and economic transition in Central and Eastern Europe. And I agree wholeheartedly with what Mr. Barber wrote there: If someone had predicted to me at the start of 1989 that all these events would come to pass, I would have been tempted to ask what they were smoking. It was indeed a turning point in our history  25 years ago it became possible for Poland and its neighbours to start building democracy and a market economy. 1 Tony Barber, Polands past points to the future of its neighbours, Financial Times, 19 sierpnia 2014 r. At todays conference we will speak about why and how it was possible for this to happen. We will also try to find out what lessons from the transition can be drawn for the future. It is clear to me that what the economies in transition share, is the aim: to catch up with the living standards of the advanced market economies. Notwithstanding this common objective, the experience of the transition countries in the region has varied. As Robert Merton Solow, said in 1991: There is not some glorious theoretical synthesis of capitalism that you can write down in a book and follow. You have to grope your way." After the fall of the Soviet bloc, countries from Central and Easter Europe have been designing and constructing from the ground up their own market economies, remaining under influence of an unique set of factors of an economic, political and social nature. I would like to refer today to the factors that, in my opinion, were important for the Polish transformation, namely: the economic strategy, the political determination, and finally, the people. Lets start with the strategy. 1. Strategy First of all I would like to underline the importance of having a clear strategy. In Poland, in 1989, the first democratically-elected government faced the challenge of designing a strategy leading to the creation of a market economy. The obstacles to achieving this aim, inherited from the communist past, were huge: a severe crisis of public finance overburdened with subsides, inflation bordering on hyperinflation, shortages of goods, an enormous foreign debt, a collapsing balance of payments and low productivity. The Polish government decided to implement a strategy of rapid and comprehensive reforms, later recognized as the so-called "shock therapy". Its advocates argued that, in order to establish normal market conditions and restart economic growth, reforms composed of three essential elements  price liberalization, stabilization and privatization had to be undertaken as quickly as possible. The programme incorporating strategy based on these 3 elements was launched in January 1990. It was a tough austerity programme. There were adverse results at first: inflation of over 100 per cent during the first two months of implementation, a drop in production and consumption and  slightly later  a rise in unemployment, which remained very high for years. But first positive results appeared relatively soon. They included the elimination of demand-driven inflation, equilibration of the market, promotion of exports and stimulation of private entrepreneurship. The initial rapid internal changes helped to activate the determinants of long-term development, including those of an external character. In this regard, the activation of trade played a major role in reinvigorating the economy. One of the core elements of the success of the Polish transition during the last 25 years has also been a relatively stable and consistent economic policy. With changing economic reality, monetary policy had to evolve rapidly and build up its credibility at the same time. And it did. Gradual liberalization of the exchange rate policy took the Polish zloty all the way from a fixed peg, through a crawling corridor, towards the free-float. The responsible way of conducting this process stabilized the macroeconomic environment and developed the shock-absorbing capacity of the zloty, which was successfully tested with the crisis in late 2008. One of the signs of stability provided by the economic policy has been lower inflation volatility than in most peer countries. Also fiscal policy was generally more prudent than in other transition economies. No major imbalances have been allowed to accumulate. Secured by the constitutional provision, public debt to GDP ratio has never exceeded 60%, while private indebtedness has also been kept sustainable which can also be attributed to the traditional and conservative banking sector. And the current account deficit has never become excessive. Institution building and structural reforms carried out in the 90s were perhaps less spectacular than the macrostabilisation big-bang, but were implemented in a consistent way. Step-by-step we adopted anti-monopoly policy, established the stock exchange and introduced a variety of privatization schemes. We made some mistakes, but they were corrected in a pragmatic way. One example  in the early 90s a number of state-own and private commercial banks faced a solvency crisis, cost by a large share of non-performing loans that were not paid back by inviolable companies. For the state own banks the government helped with rehabilitation and recapitalization  they were recapitalized with long-term treasury bonds so that they could ride of bad loans. They were able to clean up their credit portfolio, which was necessary to prepare them for privatization. In mid 90s incentives to attract foreign direct investments began to bring positive results. All in all, by the end of the 90s we managed to set up the solid institutional foundations for future gains from our increasingly open and competitive economy. 2. Political dimension of an economic transition In democratic systems politicians are in the hands of the voters. In order not to lose public support they usually prefer to speak about bright future than about painful transition strategies. But sometimes, with regard to fundamental policy goals, an agreement between parties can be reached. Let me mention the two most important forces that united Poland to support the pains of transition. Firstly, I have to mention the creation of the Solidarity movement and the events of 1989: the Round Table negotiations that led to the first partially democratic elections. The people were delighted with the new democracy and besides, there was nothing to look back and long for in the past. The Poles were reunited and looking to the future. Bad experience of command economy helped in a sense, politically, to gain the support. Second thing is the power of the European integration process. For Poland, the aim of becoming a member of the European Union was of great importance. It meant re-unification of Europe and return to European democratic values. Ultimately it is to lead to better living standards. Over those 25 years all political forces shared and supported the idea of the EU membership. And this provided for continuity in macroeconomic policy  we change prime ministers, we changed finances ministers even more frequently, but the policy was broadly continued. 3. The people I dont have in mind here people like Lech Wasa, Vaclav Havel, Jegor Gajdar, Leszek Balcerowicz, Aleksander Kwaniewski or Tadeusz Mazowiecki. No doubt, they were indispensable. But I have in mind the people as a society Polish society had two important features that constituted the core of transition: innate support for democracy and capitalist traditions. Poland has democratic traditions that date back to the Middle Ages, at least this is what we like to say. But, true, there was no problem in convincing Poles to become democrats and to live in democracy. With regard to capitalist traditions  they dated from before the World War II, so there were many points of reference in the process of building structures of free market in the early 1990s. Commercial laws could have been adopted on the basis of Polish pre-World War II laws. Moreover, in Poland there was a vibrant shadow economy, even in command economy, under communist rules, we had relatively skilled and entrepreneurial workforce. And 10 per cent of the non-agricultural GDP was created in that private initiative as we used to called it  shadow or semi-shadow economy. So these were strong pillars of economic and political development throughout, or at least at the beginning of those 25 years. Ladies and Gentlemen, I hope you agree with me now that a well-designed economic strategy, supported by the politicians and by the society is the key element of transition. However, you will also agree with Winston Churchills words. He said: "However beautiful the strategy, you should occasionally look at the results". Let me therefore look at the results in a nutshell. Between 1991 and 2013 GDP per capita increased from 32 to 62 per cent of the EU-15 average. It now stands at almost 70% of the EU-28 average. Moreover, the last 25 years have seen a major structural shift in the Polish economy. Back in 1990, 28% of the working population was employed in agriculture. This share has decreased by half so far. Services gained importance in absorbing the labour force, increasing its share from 36 to almost 60% of total employment. Massive adjustments have also taken place in Polands formerly overgrown industrial sector. Private sector in Poland employs more than 75% of the working population, up from 50% in 1990. This share is higher than in France, the Netherlands or the Nordic countries. Private enterprises are particularly successful in exploring new export markets and competing in an international environment. What stands behind the success? Stable macroeconomic environment; persistent restructuring and finally, Polands attractiveness to foreign investors. This stems, in particular, from the well-educated labour force, low labour costs and rather high labour market flexibility, both in terms of employment and wages. Of course I need to mention the expansion of exports. While most Western European countries have been losing their market shares in world exports, Poland has doubled it over the last two decades. What is especially worth emphasizing is the increasing technology content of exports: high- and medium-technology intensive exports account for almost half of its total value. As a matter of fact, this doubling of export share of Poland in the world market is entirely due to increase in competitiveness  we are trading with less dynamic regions then on average, so its not the case that we export especially to the rising stars of the world economy. Secondly, we trade in rather traditional or low growing goods and services so this does not carry us forward neither  it the competitiveness. So we have carved out a bigger share in the global markets due entirely to our increased competitiveness. Having reached the status of an upper-middle income country, a new overriding objective is to progress to the top class. We aspire to the status of an advanced economy. In essence, it means that our challenge is to switch from the growth model based on capital accumulation and lower labour costs, towards an innovation-driven one. According to the World Bank and IMF studies, the main obstacles on this way are an inefficient institutional setup combined with unfavourable demographics and low human capital, which leads to a low level of innovation in the economy. So, this can lead some people in Poland to say  well, 25 years have been a huge success, but we are in a corner  what comes next? We dont know. How to bring about this next step of advancement from a relatively high-income country to an advanced economy stage? This is a problem. Usually we say how much we have to do to improve the environment for innovation. And we  properly  lament about the low level of public services, legal framework that is not propitious for innovation and risk taking, I fully agree. But on the other hand we know that innovation is a painful process  its much easier not to innovate, to replicate rather than innovate. And to be stimulated to innovate, your life shouldnt be too easy. Is the life of Polish entrepreneurs so difficult as they say, as we sometimes agree with this? I beg to differ. Poland has a fantastic, splendid economic location for doing business. Poland has low taxation and undervalued zoty. Poland has a big, popular tolerance for interpreting laws in favour of entrepreneurs, even if we see difficulties and even if we see cases to the contrary. But isnt it so that in such a propitious environment the need to innovate is reduced? Just think about it. The other great challenge for further growth is related to demographic changes. Dear Colleagues, Im not going to continue to this introductory remarks, leaving the floor to David Lipton, who was a participant of this early heroic stage of reforms in the early 90s or late 80s, even. He can share with you his personal experience and personal remarks about how Poland has changed to his knowledge, how the whole region has changed. We know that we have achieved a lot, we know that its a lot to be done and the second part is maybe even more difficult. But we have a good meeting with very competent experienced people to try to draw lessons for the future from our past successes. Thank you very much.

Title: Report on the activities in 2020
text: Warsaw, July 22, 2021 Prof. dr hab. Adam Glapiski President of the National Bank of Poland Activity report National Bank of Poland in 2020 Mr Speaker, High House, Honourable Members, Honourable Members. As the President of the National Bank of Poland and the Chairman of the Monetary Policy Council, I have the honour to present the Report on the implementation of the monetary policy assumptions for 2020 and the Report on the activities of the National Bank of Poland in 2020. Of course, due to the time constraints that have been introduced, I will only discuss the main elements of this report. Mr Speaker, Honourable Members, The outbreak of the pandemic last year led to the biggest collapse in economic activity around the world in decades. In order to mitigate the effects of the pandemic in many countries, governments and central banks have taken completely unprecedented anti-crisis measures. Also in Poland, the pandemic and the restrictions related to it led to a strong decline in economic activity last year. We were threatened not only by a very deep recession, but also by a permanent reduction in the potential of the Polish economy, we were threatened by the bankruptcy of many companies, a strong increase in unemployment and a decrease in the income of Poles for a long time. In addition, inflation would fall below the National Bank of Poland's target in the medium term. That is why the National Bank of Polish as one of the first central banks in Europe, also in the world, introduced measures aimed at supporting the Polish economy in the face of the pandemic. First, in 2020, we cut interest rates three times, including the reference rate by a total of 1.4 percentage points, to 0.1 percent. Secondly, we have launched structural open market operations consisting of buying on the market secondary Treasury bonds and bonds guaranteed by the State Treasury. As part of these operations, by the end of June 2021, we purchased a total of bonds worth almost PLN 136 billion. PLN 136 billion for the first time in the history of the Polish central bank. Thirdly, we have lowered the reserve requirement ratio. Fourthly, we have made a promissory note loan available to banks. And finally, in the face of a strong appreciation of the zloty  fast and strong, the National Bank of Polish intervened in the currency market, reinforcing the impact of the earlier easing of monetary policy. Mr Speaker, Honourable Members, What are the effects of our policy last year today? There is no doubt that the NBP's actions have limited the costs of the pandemic for the Polish economy, for Polish companies, and above all for all Poles. Thanks to our decisions, the interest rate on loans has decreased significantly. As a result, the expenditure of households and companies on servicing loans taken out decreased by PLN 7 billion per year. In addition, the yield on Government bonds and bonds guaranteed by the State Treasury decreased significantly and the liquidity of the secondary market for these bonds was maintained. This allowed for the immediate launch of payments of funds to Polish enterprises and households as part of the government's anti-crisis shields. In total, since the beginning of the pandemic, about PLN 140 billion has been paid out as part of them. As a result, the decline in real GDP last year in Poland amounted to only 2.7 percent and was more than twice as small as the average in the European Union. In addition, unemployment has not increased significantly, making it one of the lowest in the entire European Union today. At the same time, the financial results of most companies are very good, and the real income of Poles is constantly growing. Most importantly, all forecasts indicate that not only in the current year, but also in future years, in several future years, we have a chance for very strong economic growth. It is worth emphasizing that the NBP's activities not only effectively supported the Polish economy, including its current recovery, but also significantly reduced the costs of anti-crisis programs for the budget, and therefore for the Polish taxpayer. Savings of the state budget in this respect are estimated at over PLN 7 billion, and only last year, which I'm talking about. In addition, in 2020, the NBP contributed PLN 7.4 billion to the state budget, coming from the generated profit. Mr Speaker, Honourable Members, In recent months, concerns about the condition of the Polish economy have subsided in many comments about the increase in inflation. In the last months of this year. Inflation has indeed increased, which of course is the subject of thorough nbp analyses. However, the increased level of inflation is temporary, and its significant increase in the last six months  which concerns many economies around the world  is mainly due to factors completely independent of the NBP's monetary policy. The annual price dynamics are primarily increased by the global increase in the prices of raw materials, which is strongly reinforced by the so-called statistical base effect , since we measure everything to the period of the year before. Regulatory factors also contributed significantly to the increase in prices in Poland, including a significant increase in fees for garbage collection and an increase in electricity prices as a result of the EU policy of rationing carbon dioxide emission allowances. I want to strongly emphasize that these factors are completely independent of any actions of the NBP, as well as of the domestic economic situation. At the same time, they are fully responsible, I emphasize, in full for exceeding the NBP inflation target. If we do not take them into account, we are below the target, the means of the inflation target. Inflation is projected to remain above the upper limit of deviations from the inflation target until the end of this year, but will decline as early as next year. I would like to remind you that in accordance with the implemented monetary policy strategy, the NBP's goal is to maintain inflation at the level of 2.5 percent with a symmetrical range of deviations 1 percentage point in the medium term. And that's what we're fully delivering on. In the longer term, inflation remains at a level consistent with the NBP's target and will continue to do so in the coming years. In the period in which I have the honour to serve as the President of the NBP, inflation in Poland averaged 2.1 percent, so it was fully consistent with the inflation target. In the following years  unless there are further external shocks  inflation will return to the NBP target. We will continue to pursue a monetary policy that supports sustainable economic growth and long-term economic development Polish. Mr Speaker, Honourable Members, The COVID-19 pandemic has created significant risks not only to economic growth and macroeconomic balance, but also to the stability of the entire financial system. The National Bank of Polish, in cooperation with the Government and other institutions of the financial safety net, has taken decisive action to reduce risks in this area. First of all, the NBP quickly provided the banking sector with liquidity. This was mainly due to the structural open market operations I have already mentioned and the reduction of the mandatory reserve rate. The good liquidity situation of the banking sector is confirmed not only by liquidity ratios at the moment, but also by the fact that during this difficult period it was not necessary to provide any bank with liquidity support in the form of a refinancing loan. In turn, the reduction of NBP interest rates was beneficial for maintaining the dynamics of the economy and contributed to reducing the burden on existing borrowers. Together with the support from the financial shields and moratoriums, which you remember, which were introduced, together with these loan repayment moratoria, it reduced the risk of a strong deterioration in the quality of the banks' loan portfolio. Banks have significantly increased their credit risk write-offs prudentially, but the scale of their actual credit losses has so far been smaller, generally smaller than we feared at the beginning of the pandemic. It is enough to reach for the media of that time. Reducing the risk of excessive credit restriction by banks was served by enabling them to use funds from the so-called systemic risk buffer. In March 2020, the liquidation of the buffer was recommended to the Minister of Finance by the Financial Stability Committee  a macroprudential body chaired by the President of the NBP. As a result, banks received over PLN 30 billion of capital at their disposal, which until now had been frozen in their balance sheets. At the same time, we have stipulated that the funds released from the buffer may not increase the planned dividends, but should be used to cover losses and lending to the economy. The banking sector ended 2020 with a solvency ratio of more than 20 percent  more than 1.3 percentage points more than in 2019. The solvency ratio has increased, not decreased. This was precisely the result of the banks retaining profits. To sum up, despite the scale of the shock and the high uncertainty regarding the consequences of the COVID-19 pandemic, the whole crisis turns out to be less of a threat to the stability of the financial system in the face of the countermeasures taken than it seemed last year. Currently, the greater threat is posed  more and more likely  by high write-downs on the legal risk of foreign currency loans granted by banks. The NBP received an inquiry from the Supreme Court on this issue and the answer from the National Bank of Poland has already been provided. Mr Speaker], High House, thank you very much. As the central bank of the state, the National bank of Polish, is responsible for conducting issuing activities and organizing monetary settlements. This task gained particular importance last year, because the ongoing epidemic situation in the country has resulted in a significant increase in the demand of Poles for cash - significant, violent, fast. In these difficult conditions, the NBP met the logistical challenges, ensuring efficient and uninterrupted supply of banks with Polish currency. Thanks to this, Polish women and Poles had uninterrupted access to cash through ATMs and bank branches, which maintained public trust in the state and its institutions. These experiences show that cash continues to play a very important role in stabilising the financial system in crisis situations. Despite this, during the pandemic we have recorded cases of refusal to accept cash. In the opinion of the National Bank of Poland, such a situation is legally and socially unacceptable. Therefore, in order to secure the universal availability and acceptance of cash on the payment market, in November 2020 I announced the commencement of work on the development of the National Strategy for the Security of Cash Transactions. The preparation of solutions ensuring broadly understood security of cash transactions, which are one of the priority tasks of the NBP in 2021, was entrusted to the Cash Trading Council at the NBP Management Board. It required an additional cooperation with all public institutions competent for the areas covered by the Strategy and with representatives of the cash market. Mr Speaker], High House, thank you very much. Last year was also full of challenges for the process of managing foreign exchange reserves. We had to face not only an increase in volatility on the financial markets, a deterioration in the creditworthiness of issuers of securities in the conditions of a strong economic downturn, but also an increase in operational and settlement risk due to the transition of many financial institutions to the remote work mode. I can proudly say that in this area the NBP has also fulfilled its statutory tasks without reservations. At the end of 2020, the official reserve assets of the National Bank of Poland were the equivalent of almost 126 billion euros, of which an important part is the monetary gold reserve, amounting to almost 230 tons. The monetary gold reserve increased to 230 tons. This amount of reserves has allowed the commonly used reserve adequacy indicators to be maintained at an appropriate level, strengthening the financial credibility of Polish on foreign markets and safeguarding potential balance of payments needs. Of course, first of all, high security of invested funds and their proper high liquidity are required, only after meeting these conditions, you can take care of increasing the profitability of reserves in the long term. . Various actions taken allowed to reduce the risk of the portfolio of provisions, but also to increase its profitability. In 2020, the rate of return on provisions calculated in PLN amounted to 5.2 percent, and calculated in the currency of the instruments 2.3 percent and was much higher than the average over the last 5 years. As a result, income from investment activities related to the management of foreign exchange reserves amounted to PLN 6.9 billion and was the main component of the financial result, which in 2020 amounted to PLN 9.3 billion. According to the NBP Act, 95 percent of this amount has already been transferred to the state budget. Taking all this into account, I can proudly say today that in 2020, as in previous years, the NBP not only achieved its statutory goals, but also actively supported the Polish economy in the face of the pandemic. Thank you for your attention.
text_original: Warszawa, 22 lipca 2021 r. Prof. dr hab. Adam Glapiski Prezes Narodowego Banku Polskiego Sprawozdanie z dziaalnoci Narodowego Banku Polskiego w 2020 roku Panie Marszaku, Wysoka Izbo, Szanowne Panie Posanki, Szanowni Panowie Posowie. Jako Prezes Narodowego Banku Polskiego i Przewodniczcy Rady Polityki Pieninej mam zaszczyt przedstawi Sprawozdanie z wykonania zaoe polityki pieninej na rok 2020 oraz Sprawozdanie z dziaalnoci Narodowego Banku Polskiego w 2020 roku. Oczywicie ze wzgldu na wprowadzone ograniczenia czasowe omwi tylko gwne elementy tego sprawozdania. Panie Marszaku, Wysoka Izbo! Wybuch pandemii w zeszym roku doprowadzi do najwikszego od dekad zaamania aktywnoci gospodarczej na caym wiecie. W celu agodzenia skutkw pandemii w wielu krajach rzdy oraz banki centralne podjy cakowicie bezprecedensowe dziaania antykryzysowe. Rwnie w Polsce pandemia oraz restrykcje z ni zwizane doprowadziy do silnego spadku aktywnoci gospodarczej w ubiegym roku. Grozia nam nie tylko bardzo gboka recesja, ale te trwae obnienie potencjau polskiej gospodarki, grozia nam upado wielu firm, silny wzrost bezrobocia i spadek dochodw Polakw na duszy czas. Ponadto w rednim okresie inflacja spadaby poniej celu Narodowego Banku Polskiego. Dlatego Narodowy Bank Polski jako jeden z pierwszych bankw centralnych w Europie, take na wiecie wprowadzi dziaania, ktrych celem byo wsparcie polskiej gospodarki w obliczu pandemii. Po pierwsze, w 2020 roku trzykrotnie obniylimy stopy procentowe, w tym stop referencyjn cznie o 1,4 punktu procentowego, do poziomu 0,1 procent. Po drugie, uruchomilimy strukturalne operacje otwartego rynku, polegajce na skupywaniu na rynku wtrnym obligacji skarbowych i gwarantowanych przez Skarb Pastwa. W ramach tych operacji do koca czerwca 2021 roku skupilimy cznie obligacje o wartoci prawie 136 miliardw zotych. 136 miliardw zotych po raz pierwszy w historii polskiego banku centralnego. Po trzecie, obniylimy stop rezerwy obowizkowej. Po czwarte, udostpnilimy bankom kredyt wekslowy. I wreszcie, w obliczu silnej aprecjacji zotego  szybkiej i silnej, Narodowy Bank Polski dokona interwencji na rynku walutowym, wzmacniajc oddziaywanie wczeniejszego poluzowania polityki pieninej. Panie Marszaku, Wysoka Izbo! Jakie s dzi efekty naszej polityki w zeszym roku? Nie ulega wtpliwoci, e dziaania NBP ograniczyy koszty pandemii dla polskiej gospodarki, dla polskich firm, a przede wszystkim dla wszystkich Polek i Polakw. Dziki naszym decyzjom istotnie spado oprocentowanie kredytw. W rezultacie wydatki gospodarstw domowych i firm na obsug zacignitych kredytw zmniejszyy si o 7 miliardw zotych w skali roku. Ponadto istotnie obniya si rentowno obligacji skarbowych oraz gwarantowanych przez Skarb Pastwa i utrzymana zostaa pynno rynku wtrnego tych obligacji. Pozwolio to na natychmiastowe uruchomienie wypat rodkw dla polskich przedsibiorstw i gospodarstw domowych w ramach rzdowych tarcz antykryzysowych. cznie od pocztku pandemii wypacono w ich ramach okoo 140 miliardw zotych. W rezultacie spadek realnego PKB w ubiegym roku wynis w Polsce zaledwie 2,7 procent i by ponad dwukrotnie mniejszy ni rednio w Unii Europejskiej. Ponadto nie wzroso istotnie bezrobocie, dziki czemu naley dzisiaj do najniszych w caej Unii Europejskiej. Jednoczenie wyniki finansowe wikszoci firm s bardzo dobre, a realne dochody Polakw cay czas rosn. Co najwaniejsze, wszystkie prognozy wskazuj, e nie tylko w biecym roku, ale te w przyszych latach, w kilku przyszych latach, mamy szans na bardzo silny wzrost gospodarczy. Warto podkreli, e dziaania NBP nie tylko skutecznie wspary polsk gospodark, w tym jej obecne oywienie, lecz take istotnie zmniejszyy koszty programw antykryzysowych dla budetu, a zatem i dla polskiego podatnika. Oszczdnoci budetu pastwa z tego tytuu s szacowane na ponad 7 miliardw zotych, i to tylko w ubiegym roku, o ktrym mwi. Ponadto w 2020 roku NBP zasili budet pastwa kwot 7,4 miliarda zotych, pochodzcych z wypracowanego zysku. Panie Marszaku, Wysoka Izbo! W ostatnich miesicach, obawy o kondycj polskiej gospodarki ustpiy w wielu komentarzach trosce o wzrost inflacji. W ostatnich miesicach tego ju roku. Inflacja rzeczywicie wzrosa, co oczywicie jest przedmiotem wnikliwych analiz NBP. Jednak podwyszony poziom inflacji jest przejciowy, a za jej znaczny wzrost w ostatnim proczu  ktry dotyczy zreszt wielu gospodarek na caym wiecie  odpowiadaj gwnie czynniki niezalene cakowicie od polityki pieninej NBP. Roczn dynamik cen podwysza przede wszystkim globalny wzrost cen surowcw, ktry jest silnie wzmacniany przez tak zwany efekt bazy statystycznej , poniewa wszystko mierzymy do okresu rok wczeniej Do tego wci odczuwamy skutki pandemicznych zaburze dotyczcych transportu midzynarodowego i globalnych acuchw dostaw. Do wzrostu cen w Polsce istotnie przyczyniy si take czynniki regulacyjne, w tym znaczne zwikszenie opat za wywz mieci oraz podwyka cen prdu na skutek unijnej polityki racjonowania uprawnie do emisji dwutlenku wgla. Chc zdecydowanie podkreli, e wspomniane czynniki s cakowicie niezalene od jakichkolwiek dziaa NBP, a take od krajowej koniunktury. Odpowiadaj one przy tym w caoci, to podkrelam, w caoci za przekroczenie celu inflacyjnego NBP. Gdyby ich nie wzi pod uwag znajdujemy si poniej celu, rodka celu inflacyjnego. Prognozy wskazuj, e wskutek odziaywania tych czynnikw inflacja do koca biecego roku prawdopodobnie utrzyma si powyej grnej granicy odchyle od celu inflacyjnego, jednak ju w przyszym roku si obniy. I z tego si w peni wywizujemy. W duszym okresie inflacja utrzymuje si bowiem na poziomie zgodnym z celem NBP i taka te bdzie w kolejnych latach. W okresie, w ktrym mam zaszczyt peni funkcj Prezesa NBP, inflacja w Polsce wyniosa rednio 2,1 procent, a wic bya w peni zgodna z celem inflacyjnym. W nastpnych latach  o ile nie pojawi si kolejne zewntrzne szoki  inflacja wrci do celu NBP. Bdziemy nadal prowadzili polityk pienin, ktra wspiera zrwnowaony wzrost gospodarczy i dugofalowy rozwj gospodarczy Polski. Panie Marszaku, Wysoka Izbo! Pandemia COVID-19 stworzya istotne zagroenia nie tylko dla wzrostu gospodarczego i rwnowagi makroekonomicznej, lecz take dla stabilnoci caego sytemu finansowego. Narodowy Bank Polski, we wsppracy z Rzdem i innymi instytucjami sieci bezpieczestwa finansowego, podj zdecydowane dziaania suce ograniczeniu ryzyka w tym obszarze. Przede wszystkim NBP szybko zasili sektor bankowy w pynno. Suyy temu gwnie wspomniane ju przeze mnie strukturalne operacje otwartego rynku i obnienie obowizkowej stopy rezerwy . Dobr sytuacj pynnociow sektora bankowego potwierdzaj nie tylko wskaniki pynnoci w tej chwili, ale take fakt, e w tym trudnym okresie nie byo koniecznoci udzielenia adnemu bankowi wsparcia pynnociowego w postaci kredytu refinansowego. Z kolei obnienie stp procentowych NBP byo korzystne dla podtrzymania dynamiki gospodarki i przyczynio si do zmniejszenia obcie dotychczasowych kredytobiorcw. Wraz ze wsparciem z tarcz finansowych i moratoriami, o krych Pastwo pamitaj, ktre zostay wprowadzone, wraz z tymi moratoriami spat kredytw ograniczyo ryzyko silnego pogorszenia si jakoci portfela kredytowego bankw. Banki istotnie zwikszyy ostronociowo odpisy na ryzyko kredytowe, ale skala ich faktycznych strat kredytowych bya dotychczas mniejsza, zasadniczo mniejsza ni obawialimy si na pocztku pandemii. Wystarczy sign do wczesnych mediw. Zmniejszeniu ryzyka nadmiernego ograniczenia kredytu przez banki suyo umoliwienie wykorzystania przez nie rodkw z tzw. bufora ryzyka systemowego. W marcu 2020 roku likwidacj bufora rekomendowa Ministrowi Finansw Komitet Stabilnoci Finansowej  organ makroostronociowy, ktremu przewodnicz jako Prezes NBP. W efekcie banki otrzymay do dyspozycji ponad 30 mld z kapitau, ktry do tej pory by niejako zamroony w ich bilansach. Jednoczenie zastrzeglimy, e rodki uwolnione z bufora nie mog zwiksza zaplanowanych dywidend, lecz naley je przeznaczy na pokrycie strat i kredytowanie gospodarki. Rok 2020 sektor bankowy zakoczy ze wspczynnikiem wypacalnoci ponad 20 procent  o ponad 1,3 punktu procentowego wicej ni w 2019 roku. Wspczynnik wypacalnoci wzrs a nie zmala. Byo to wanie wynikiem zatrzymania zyskw przez banki. Podsumowujc, mimo skali szoku i wysokiej niepewnoci dotyczcej konsekwencji pandemii COVID-19 i cay ten kryzys okazuje si mniejszym zagroeniem dla stabilnoci systemu finansowego w obliczu podjtych krokw przeciwdziaajcych, ni wydawao si to w zeszym roku. Obecnie wiksze zagroenie stanowi  coraz bardziej prawdopodobne  wysokie odpisy na ryzyko prawne kredytw walutowych udzielanych przez banki. NBP otrzyma od Sdu Najwyszego zapytanie w tej kwestii i odpowied z Narodowego Banku Polskiego zostaa ju przekazana. Panie Marszaku], Wysoka Izbo! Jako bank centralny pastwa, Narodowy Bank Polski, jest odpowiedzialny za prowadzenie dziaalnoci emisyjnej i organizowanie rozlicze pieninych. To zadanie zyskao szczeglne znaczenie w ubiegym roku, gdy trwajca sytuacja epidemiczna w kraju wpyna na znaczny wzrost zapotrzebowania Polakw na gotwk - znaczny, gwatowny, szybki. W tych trudnych warunkach NBP sprosta logistycznym wyzwaniom, zapewniajc sprawne i nieprzerwane zaopatrywanie bankw w walut polsk. Dziki temu Polki i Polacy mieli niezakcony dostp do gotwki poprzez bankomaty i placwki bankowe, co podtrzymywao spoeczne zaufanie do pastwa i jego instytucji. Dowiadczenia te pokazuj, e w sytuacjach kryzysowych gotwka peni nadal bardzo wan rol stabilizujc system finansowy. Mimo to, w czasie pandemii odnotowalimy przypadki odmowy akceptacji gotwki. W ocenie Narodowego Banku Polskiego taka sytuacja jest niedopuszczalna prawnie i spoecznie. Dlatego, w celu zabezpieczenia powszechnej dostpnoci i akceptacji gotwki na rynku patniczym, w listopadzie 2020 r. zapowiedziaem rozpoczcie prac w zakresie opracowania Narodowej Strategii Bezpieczestwa Obrotu Gotwkowego. Przygotowanie rozwiza zapewniajcych szeroko pojte bezpieczestwo obrotu gotwkowego, nalece do priorytetowych zada NBP w 2021 r., zostao powierzone Radzie ds. obrotu gotwkowego przy Zarzdzie NBP. Wymagao ono podjcia dodatkowej wsppracy ze wszystkimi instytucjami publicznymi, waciwymi kompetencyjnie dla obszarw objtych Strategi oraz z przedstawicielami rynku gotwkowego. Panie Marszaku], Wysoka Izbo! Ubiegy rok obfitowa take w wyzwania dla procesu zarzdzania rezerwami dewizowymi. Musielimy si zmierzy nie tylko ze wzrostem zmiennoci na rynkach finansowych, pogorszeniem wiarygodnoci kredytowej emitentw papierw wartociowych w warunkach silnego osabienia koniunktury gospodarczej, ale take wzrostem ryzyka operacyjnego i rozliczeniowego w zwizku z przejciem wielu instytucji finansowych do trybu pracy zdalnej. Mog z dum powiedzie, e i w tym obszarze NBP wypeni take bez zastrzee swoje ustawowe zadania. Na koniec 2020 roku oficjalne aktywa rezerwowe Narodowego Banku Polskiego stanowiy rwnowarto niemal 126 mld euro, z czego istotn czci jest zasb zota monetarnego, wynoszcy prawie 230 ton. Zasb zota monetarnego wzrs do poziomu 230 ton. Taka wielko rezerw pozwolia utrzyma na waciwym poziomie powszechnie stosowane wskaniki adekwatnoci rezerw, wzmacniajc wiarygodno finansow Polski na rynkach zagranicznych i zabezpieczajc potencjalne potrzeby bilansu patniczego. Oczywicie przede wszystkim wymagane jest wysokie bezpieczestwo inwestowanych rodkw i ich waciwa wysoka pynno, dopiero po spenieniu tych warunkw, mona dba o podwyszenie dochodowoci rezerw w dugim okresie. . Podjte dziaania rnego rodzaju, pozwolio ograniczy ryzyko portfela rezerw, ale take podwyszy jego dochodowo. W 2020 roku stopa zwrotu z rezerw obliczona w zotych wyniosa 5,2 procent, a obliczona w walucie instrumentw 2,3 procent i bya znacznie wysza ni rednio w cigu ostatnich 5 lat. W efekcie, dochd z dziaalnoci inwestycyjnej zwizanej z zarzdzaniem rezerwami dewizowymi wynis 6,9 mld z i stanowi gwn skadow wyniku finansowego, ktry w 2020 r. wynis 9,3 mld z. Zgodnie z ustaw o NBP, 95 procent tej kwoty ju wpyno do budetu pastwa. Biorc to wszystko pod uwag, mog dzisiaj z dum powiedzie, e w 2020 roku, podobnie jak w poprzednich latach, NBP nie tylko realizowa swoje ustawowe cele, ale te aktywnie wspiera polsk gospodark w obliczu pandemii. Dzikuj Pastwu za uwag.

Title: Report on the activities in 2021
text: Warsaw, 21 July 2022 Prof. Adam Glapiski Governor of Narodowy Bank Polski Report on the activities of Narodowy Bank Polski in 2021 Speaker of the Sejm, Members of the House! As every year, I am honoured to present to you the Report on Monetary Policy and Report on NBP Operations. Both documents present the statutory activities conducted by the central bank last year. I will briefly discuss the most important of these, beginning with monetary policy. At the outset, let me remind you that Narodowy Bank Polski implements monetary policy in accordance with the Constitution, the Act on NBP and with the Monetary Policy Guidelines, which are adopted each year. The main objective of monetary policy is to maintain price stability. At the same time, monetary policy is conducted in such a way as to be conducive to sustained economic growth and financial system stability. For many years, monetary policy strategy has been based on the concept of the medium-term inflation target. The Monetary Policy Guidelines explicitly state that: () due to macroeconomic and financial shocks, inflation may temporarily deviate from the target and that The response of monetary policy to shocks is flexible and depends on their causes and the assessment of persistence of their consequences. This is important because for almost three years the Polish economy has been faced with unprecedented disturbances, initially triggered by the pandemic, and currently by the war in Ukraine. These shocks are an enormous challenge in many fields, including for monetary policy, because they intensify the amplitude of the macroeconomic changes. Please allow me to recall that in the first quarters of 2021 the Polish economy was only just making up for the pandemic losses, and the uncertainty about the future course of the pandemic was a significant risk factor for the sustainability of the economic recovery. At that time, inflation was running at a level consistent with the NBP target, although in the next quarters  like in other countries  it began to gradually rise. At that time, the main factors contributing to the rise in inflation were beyond the influence of domestic monetary policy; they were, above all, the increase in global commodity prices and global supply disruptions, as well as regulatory factors. Taking into account the nature of the majority of the factors boosting price growth, in the first three quarters of the year it was rationally judged that following a temporary rise, inflation would decline in 2022. I will repeat this sentence  taking into account the nature of the majority of the factors boosting price growth, in the first three quarters of the year it was entirely rational to judge that following a temporary rise, inflation would decline in 2022. This was indicated by all the available forecasts  not only the forecasts of Narodowy Bank Polski, but also of the most important international institutions, including the International Monetary Fund and its special mission to Poland. In these conditions, from the point of view of the knowledge it possessed at that time, the Monetary Policy Council correctly kept interest rates unchanged. This was correct from the point of view of the knowledge possessed at that time, and not from the point of view of the knowledge we have today, after two years, when we know what happened. This is why the accusations that NBP began the cycle of monetary policy tightening too late are unfounded. In light of the knowledge at the time, this would have been neither correct nor rational. It was only in the run-up to the meeting of the Monetary Policy Council in October 2021 that the inflation outlook changed significantly. In particular, global energy commodity prices rose sharply once again, as did prices of agricultural commodities. This pushed up the inflation forecast and extended the expected period of higher price growth. At the same time, incoming information indicated that the next wave of the pandemic would have a limited impact on the economic conditions, that it would not lead to mass lockdowns. Consequently, there was a higher risk that in the medium term  in other words, more or less two years  price growth would persist at a level above the inflation target. In this situation, in order to reduce the risk, from October 2021 monetary policy has immediately been tightened. In particular, we have raised NBP interest rates significantly. The reference rate has risen by a total of 6.4 percentage points to the current level of 6.5 per cent. Moreover, we have returned the required reserve ratios to the pre- pandemic level and ended bond purchases on the secondary market. Therefore, in recent quarters we have taken very decisive action to reduce inflation. Speaker of the Sejm, Members of the House! Although monetary tightening limits and will limit inflation, like in other countries it is high today because it has been boosted by sharp rises in global commodity prices and disruptions in global production and international trade. I underline here the word global, because these are factors going beyond our national circumstances  initially connected with the pandemic, and currently exacerbated by the Russian aggression against Ukraine  and causing price rises all around the world. It is worth remembering that in the euro area inflation is currently the highest ever recorded and in the United States and the United Kingdom inflation is the highest in forty years. In most countries in our region inflation is in double digits and is higher than in Poland. In those countries that began to tighten monetary policy earlier and raised interest rates earlier it also turned out not to make a difference. However, it is worth remembering that although inflation is high everywhere, this does not necessarily apply to economic growth. The Polish economy is one of few economies in the region which can boast that it has more than made up for the pandemic losses. To this day, this is not the case in the major European countries, I recall that GDP growth in the first quarter of this year stood at 8.5 per cent, and Polish GDP exceeded by over 8 per cent the pre-pandemic level, with very low unemployment, practically without unemployment and with a favourable situation in the labour market. This is a great success of all Poles. It is a great success that is not appreciated enough on a daily basis, but which is appreciated abroad. Admittedly, in the coming quarters a significant slowdown in GDP growth is forecast, just like everywhere, in the whole of Europe and around the world, but in the second half of next year economic growth is expected to pick up again. In view of the conditions presented in the current year, NBP has continued to tighten monetary policy, because our priority is the reduce inflation. However, it is worth remembering that a reduction in the inflation triggered by the strong supply shocks must occur gradually  especially since a fundamental economic slowdown is expected  in order not to generate excessive social costs, and above all significant unemployment. This is why monetary policy continues to be conducted in a responsible manner, namely, in a way that reduces inflation and at the same time is conducive to sustainable economic growth. Speaker of the Sejm, Members of the House! I will now move on to the remaining areas of NBP activities, beginning with supporting financial system stability. The stability of the financial system, in particular the stability of the banking sector, is a necessary condition for meeting the inflation target, as well as maintaining sustainable long-term economic development. In 2021, the economic repercussions of the COVID-19 pandemic continued to be a source of threats to financial stability. Ultimately, these threats proved to be less severe for the economy and the banking sector than initially expected. Credit losses last year fell significantly and failed to confirm fears of excessive tightening of lending by banks. The activities of NBP and the government taken in 2020 and continued last year effectively supported the banking sector. In the past year, the costs of the legal risk related to FX mortgage loans have continued to present a challenge for the banks. NBP positively assesses the approach of the banks  the creation of a reserve for the legal risk of FX housing loans and offering borrowers a settlement. These measures have helped the banking sector to become more resilient to the financial effects of this risk. This year has seen additional challenges facing the banks in the form of the consequences of the rise in inflation and higher interest rates, strengthened by the possible negative effects of the war in Ukraine. Rising interest rates impact financial stability in a variety of ways. A positive result was observed as early as last year in the form of lower mortgage loan growth, which had earlier been judged by the Financial Stability Committee as a possible source of imbalance in the residential real estate market. Higher interest rates were also conducive to a rebound in the profitability of the banking sector following the pandemic. Thanks to this, the banks increased their ability to absorb future shocks, e.g. the economic repercussions of the war in Ukraine, which are difficult to foresee. However, the increase in the cost of loan servicing may cause credit risk for banks to materialise. In particular, this concerns people who have long-term housing loans and interest based on a variable interest rate. There is no doubt that the burden on indebted households budgets has increased. However, I believe the assessments of the related risk that appear in the media, as well as in politics, in the political sphere, are exaggerated: approximately 4/5 of mortgage loans were granted before the period of historically low interest rates, only 1/5 were granted during the period of particularly low interest rates, and all the banks required income buffers from the borrowers safeguarding their debt-servicing capabilities, even in the event of higher interest rates than those in place at the moment. Lets also not forget that since the moment that these loans were taken out there was relatively high wage growth, which to a large extent offsets the effect of higher instalments. This is why the increase in the cost of credit does not have to automatically trigger problems with its repayment, which can be seen in the statistics. Taking into account these circumstances, Narodowy Bank Polski presented an opinion that financial support, government financial support, should be limited to only those borrowers who actually need it  introduced through legislation and financed by the banks. Only for those borrowers who actually need it, and not for everyone, as is the case. We believe the Borrower Support Fund is a suitable mechanism which will ensure this. In the opinion of NBP, better targeting of support would reduce moral hazard, would reduce the costs of banks and would be more favourable for the state budget. Speaker of the Sejm, Members of the House! Despite the persistence of the epidemic in Poland, last year we did not observe a sharp increase in demand for cash, as was the case in 2020. The value of cash in circulation as at the end of 2021 was 355.6 billion zloty, which represents a rise of 10.5% compared to the previous year. The increase in cash in circulation in 2021 was related to the increase in total money supply in the economy. On the other hand, in 2022 the value of cash in circulation increased more strongly, which was a result of the greater market demand for cash in physical form following Russias aggression against Ukraine and the emergence of far-reaching concern, or even panic, among the population. The culmination of withdrawals from NBP, and therefore withdrawals by clients of commercial banks, took place at the end of February and beginning of March, and their scale significantly exceeded the demand for cash that was observed at the beginning of the pandemic. It exceeded it significantly. However, despite the above-average social demand for cash, Narodowy Bank Polski was able to fully satisfy this demand. And this was what I meant when I said publicly that we have an endless supply of cash. This endless supply, of course, is countable  it is endless, but in the sense that there will not be a shortage, so that clients will be able to withdraw money from the banks and will not need to panic. And I stand by this statement. Speaker of the Sejm, Members of the House!
